Students will study a variety of ethical theories and consider the views of thinkers from the past and contemporary society. Topics will include animal rights, conservation and use of natural resources, and environmental justice with respect to pollution and climate change.

fields.title: Geospatial Intelligence Certificate Program Capstone Project
fields.description: This is a senior-level course in which students demonstrate how the geospatial knowledge and skills learned from earlier courses can be applied to a national security problem. Key elements of the capstone project include: preparation of a problem statement (intelligence question); identifying sources of information; applying technical, communications and analytic principles; understanding situational conditions; preparing actionable recommendations for decision makers; and communicating findings in a professional manner. Repeatable for a maximum of six credit hours.

fields.title: Special Topics in Integrated Science and Engineering
fields.description: This is a special topics course designator that can be used for any of a variety of topics that cut across disciplines within the broad realm of integrated science and engineering. Requisites may vary by section.

fields.title: Robotics Project Summary
fields.description: Students will reflect upon their experience gained in a prerequisite supervised robotics project course, a robotics internship, a robotics research project or an equivalent experience. Results will be disseminated to the academic community via a presentation, a report and/or other means.

fields.title: Science Outreach in Schools
fields.description: A service learning course in which students engage in outreach activities in area high schools. Emphasis is placed on planning and implementing effective tutoring or enrichment activities as well as reflection and assessment of outcomes.

fields.title: Exploration of Topics in STEM
fields.description: This course provides introduction to and exploration of a variety of STEM-related topics. Course content will vary and could include introduction to STEM curriculum, academic planning, time management and study skills, stress and anxiety management, campus student resources, undergraduate research topics, graduate school considerations, and discussion of STEM career options. May be repeated for credit as course content changes. Students should consult the instructor prior to enrolling for this course. Course provides university elective credit.

fields.title: General Instructional Methods for Science in Grades 6-12
fields.description: This general teaching methods course provides a solid foundation for planning curriculum and instruction for middle and high school students. Topics include engaging adolescent learners, lesson design, instructional strategies and assessment models. Students in this course must have a science major and expressed a strong interest in becoming a secondary science teacher.
fields.prerequisites: PHYS 397 , Topic: Science Pedagogy.

fields.title: Introduction to Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: This course is an introduction to human communication. It surveys mechanisms of communication and clinical populations served by audiologists, speech-language pathologists and relevant professionals such as educators and neuropsychologists. Roles and responsibilities of audiologists and speech-language pathologists are discussed.

fields.title: Phonetics
fields.description: This course is an introduction to the articulation of speech sounds, techniques for speech transcription, including basic transcription skills in International Phonetic Alphabet (IPA), and considerations of phonetic and phonemic systems.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only.

fields.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Speech and Hearing Mechanism
fields.description: This course offers a detailed study of the anatomy and physiology related to communication sciences and disorders.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only.

fields.title: Speech and Hearing Science
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to the acoustics of speech and hearing. It is also an introduction to physical acoustics, sound generation and transmission, resonance, speech acoustics, and speech perception.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only.

fields.title: Language Development
fields.description: This course is the study of language acquisition, development, structure and function in typically developing children.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only and junior standing; CSD 207 , CSD 208 and CSD 209 ; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Audiology
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to the symptoms, causes and treatment of hearing disorders. Hearing test instrumentation and interpretation in clinical situations are emphasized.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only and junior standing; CSD 207 , CSD 208 and CSD 209 ; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Pediatric Speech and Language Disorders
fields.description: This course is an introduction to speech and language disorders in children. An overview of assessment and treatment is presented.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 300 and junior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Aural Rehabilitation
fields.description: This course offers a focused study on the impact of hearing loss on human communication across the lifespan.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 301 and junior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Topics in Speech Production and Perception: Implications for Clinical Populations
fields.description: This course is a focused study of topics in speech production and perception as related to communication sciences and disorders. The underlying mechanisms associated with these functions for human communication are surveyed and examined with an emphasis on the effects of communicative disorders. The interdisciplinary nature of communication sciences and disorders is highlighted. This course is relevant to a range of fields of study including (but not limited to) speech-language pathology, audiology, speech, language, hearing sciences, psychology, linguistics, health sciences, nursing and occupational therapy.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 101 , CSD 207 , CSD 209 and MATH 220 , or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Professional Issues and Person-Centered Care in Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: This course addresses professional issues including professional conduct, evidence-based practice, ethics, social determinants of health, and considerations for person-, family-, and/or care-partner centered care.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 200 , CSD 207 , CSD 300 , CSD 314 and senior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Neuroanatomy and Neurogenic Communication Disorders
fields.description: This course is an introduction to neuroanatomy with emphasis on neurogenic communication disorders.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 208 and senior standing, or departmental permission.

fields.title: Adult Neurogenic Communication Disorders
fields.description: This course addresses fundamental considerations for communication and swallowing disorders of acquired neurogenic etiology. Evaluation methods and treatment strategies are explored.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 208 , CSD 415 and senior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Introduction to Sign Language
fields.description: Provides an introduction to American Sign Language, the deaf community and English-based signed systems.

fields.title: Sign Language II
fields.description: Focuses on developing conversational skills of students whose core vocabulary and knowledge of the grammar and pragmatics of sign language are basic; distinguishes ASL from English sign systems.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 420 or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Methods and Observation in Speech Language Pathology
fields.description: This course is an introduction to the clinical process in speech-language pathology via guided observation and participation in laboratory and professional clinical interactions. Practical clinical methodologies are emphasized.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only; CSD 314 and senior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Methods and Observation in Audiology
fields.description: This course is an introduction to the clinical process in audiology via guided observation and participation in laboratory and professional clinical interactions. Practical clinical methodologies are emphasized.
fields.prerequisites: CSD majors only; CSD 301 and senior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Special Studies in Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: Provides students opportunity for independent study and/or small class instruction in elective topics.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: See catalog section "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Research in Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: Focuses on both basic and applied research interpretation.

fields.title: Workshops in Speech-Language Pathology and Audiology
fields.description: Designed to provide a detailed study of a particular topic of interest in speech pathology and/or audiology.

fields.title: Seminar in Audiology (Clinical Methods)
fields.description: This course addresses selected topics, issues and other content designed to prepare students for clinical practice in audiology. Content is treated on an introductory level with emphasis upon problem solving, integration of information across didactic and practical knowledge toward clinical skill development.

fields.title: Instrumentation in Audiology
fields.description: A study of topics and procedures of instrumentation that are fundamental to clinical practice including electricity and electronics, filters, calibration, acoustical impedance, analog and digital signals, and acoustics.

fields.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Auditory System
fields.description: This course provides advanced study of the anatomy and physiology of the peripheral and central auditory systems to include cochlear and neural mechanisms of sound coding.

fields.title: Anatomy and Physiology of the Vestibular Pathway
fields.description: This course is an introduction to anatomy and physiology of the vestibular and oculomotor systems. Course content includes videonystagmography testing including oculomotor assessments, positional testing and caloric testing with both didactic and hands-on components. Normal mechanisms will be discussed in light of diagnosis and treatment of pathological processes.

fields.title: Audiologic Assessment
fields.description: This course provides a study of auditory disorders and the measurement of hearing including an overview of behavioral and physiologic measures. Emphasis is placed on the behavioral evaluation of the peripheral system, tests of cochlear and retrocochlear differentiation, and immittance measures.

fields.title: Aural Rehabilitation and Education Audiology
fields.description: This course focuses on the impact of hearing loss on human communication across the lifespan. Aural habilitation and rehabilitation procedures common to the 20th century are compared with today's trends and with projected advances expected for the 21st century. Additional emphasis is placed on the role of aural habilitation and rehabilitation in an educational setting.

fields.title: Advanced Vestibular Physiology and Testing
fields.description: This course is an advanced study of the anatomy and physiology of the oculomotor and vestibular systems. It includes detailed study of basic and advanced concepts in clinical testing, treatment and mechanisms of rehabilitation of disorders of the vestibular and balance system.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Practicum A
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic and a variety of other settings. Lab fee required.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 510 .

fields.title: Advanced Sign Language
fields.description: Advanced sign language will enhance the communication skills of the student whose core vocabulary and knowledge of application of sign language are basic. The course arranges opportunities for building fluency and reception, as well as expanding knowledge of sign systems and the appropriateness in a given situation.

fields.title: Communication Disorders of the Traumatically Brain Injured
fields.description: An overview of the role of speech-language pathology in the interdisciplinary management of cognitive-communicative deficits associated with traumatic brain injury.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 604 and permission of the instructor for non-departmental majors.

fields.title: Psychoacoustics
fields.description: A study of the relationship between a sound stimulus and the behavioral response it produces in a listener.

fields.title: Seminar in Audiology (Clinical Methods II)
fields.description: This course addresses selected topics, issues and other content designed to prepare students for clinical practice in audiology. Content is treated on an introductory level with emphasis upon problem solving, integration of information across didactic and practical knowledge toward clinical skill development.

fields.title: Autism
fields.description: Focus on demographics of autism spectrum disorders, historical and contemporary diagnostic and treatment procedures, and the role of the speech-language pathologist in interdisciplinary programs.

fields.title: Augmentative Communication
fields.description: Assessment and intervention strategies for the speechless population will be presented. Students will participate in demonstrations of alternative communication systems. An interdisciplinary team approach to (re)habilitation will be studied.

fields.title: Industrial Audiology
fields.description: A study of the effects of noise upon humans and topics relevant to hearing conservation, such as noise assessment and risk factors, hearing protectors, audiometric testing, employee training and record keeping.

fields.title: Business Applications in Audiology
fields.description: This course focuses on the various professional and business practices and regulations that impact audiology. Topics include licensure, certification, ethical and professional standards of practice, as well as practice management and business methods common to the practice of audiology.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Practicum B
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic and a variety of other settings. Lab fee required.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 519 and CSD 525 .

fields.title: Language Development and Disorders in Children for School Personnel
fields.description: A comprehensive study of the language development of children, the various characterizations of language impairment in children, and intervention issues and strategies, with a particular focus on academic and educational implications and interdisciplinary management in daycare, preschool and school environments.

fields.title: Birth to Five: Language Development and Disorders
fields.description: Language and emergent literacy development and disorders in the birth to five population are reviewed. Screening, prevention, assessment and intervention strategies for serving infants, toddlers and preschoolers are highlighted.

fields.title: Evaluation and Treatment of Swallowing Disorders
fields.description: Current research and clinical management will be presented of individuals showing difficulties in feeding orally and aspirating. Normal physiology of deglutition and the multidisciplinary approach toward the management of dysphagia will be emphasized.

fields.title: Tinnitus and Pharmacology
fields.description: This course addresses epidemiology, neurophysiological mechanisms, a variety of assessment approaches and current management options for tinnitus (bothersome and non-bothersome). Basic concepts in general pharmacology and common medications related to audiology practice will be discussed.

fields.title: Introduction to Hearing Aids
fields.description: A study of hearing handicap and its management in adults, including amplification technologies, electroacoustic analyses, and prescription and verification procedures. Emphasis is on the foundations of clinical management.

fields.title: Neuromotor Speech Disorders
fields.description: The objective of this course is to familiarize students with theoretical and clinical aspects in the areas of dysarthria and apraxia. Similarities and differences of the speech impairments in these disorders will be demonstrated and applied to diagnosis and treatment.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 604 .

fields.title: Speech Practicum A
fields.description: This is the first in a series of practicum courses. It includes both practice-base and didactic components.

fields.title: Speech Practicum B
fields.description: This is the second in a series of required practicum courses. It includes both practice base and didactic components.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 581 .

fields.title: Speech Practicum C
fields.description: This required practicum course is an intermediate level practice-based experience.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 581 , CSD 623 and CSD 640 .

fields.title: Research in Audiology
fields.description: Evaluations of research designs and methods in audiology, critique of published articles and student involvement in designing experiments on assigned topics.

fields.title: Neuroanatomy and Neurophysiology of Speech and Language
fields.description: Neuroanatomy and neurophysiology with an emphasis on speech and language behavior. Comprehensive examination of the neuroanatomic and neurophysiologic substrate for cognition and communication.

fields.title: Neurophysiologic Measures I
fields.description: Study of the neurophysiological and electrophysiological properties of the human peripheral and central auditory pathways.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Practicum C
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic and a variety of other settings.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 539 or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Research and Statistics
fields.description: This course introduces students to data analyses and statistics commonly used in hearing and balance research. Students are encouraged to bring their own data collections to class.

fields.title: Neurophysiologic Measures II
fields.description: This course is an advanced study of the neurophysiological and electrophysiological properties of the human auditory and related sensory and motor systems.

fields.title: Advanced Hearing Aids
fields.description: This course is an advanced study of hearing handicap and its prosthetic management. Various technologies, prescription methods and verification procedures are critically reviewed.

fields.title: Pediatric Speech Sound Disorders
fields.description: Speech sound production and associated skills in children are considered including articulation, motor planning and execution, phonological patterns, and phonological awareness. Emphasis is given to the identification of differences versus disorders and specific assessment and intervention approaches for various speech sound disorders.

fields.title: Pediatric Feeding Disorders
fields.description: Students study typical and disordered feeding and swallowing disorders in children, including anatomy and physiology, clinical and instrumental evaluation, and therapeutic management. This course includes interprofessional education related to the roles and responsibilities of allied medical and educational partners involved in care.

fields.title: Aging and Communication
fields.description: The normal biological, psychological and sociological changes associated with aging, as well as cultural and healthcare issues that impact aging adults in the United States, are discussed. Strategies and models for service delivery associated with speech-language, cognitive and swallowing disorders in this population will be addressed.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Practicum D
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic and a variety of other settings.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 619 or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Processes and Disorders of Speech Fluency
fields.description: Advanced diagnostic and therapeutic aspects of stuttering for children and adults are studied. Particular emphasis is placed on differentiating incipient stuttering from normal disfluencies.

fields.title: Auditory Pathophysiology
fields.description: A study of the various disorders of the external, middle and inner ears; the retrocochlear and central auditory systems; and the vestibular and balance system.

fields.title: Audiology Rotation A
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at clinical settings external to the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 629 .

fields.title: School-Age Language and Literacy Disorders
fields.description: Evidence-based practices for the screening, assessment and intervention of school-age children and adolescents with language and literacy disorders are reviewed.

fields.title: Language Disorders in Adults
fields.description: Theoretical comparative aspects and clinical management of aphasia in adults are emphasized. Communication disorders associated with right hemisphere brain damage are also considered.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 604 .

fields.title: Counseling for Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: This course will provide an introduction to basic interviewing and counseling skills necessary to help clinicians achieve the greatest success possible when working with patients with communication and balance disorders. This course will also discuss health literacy and the importance of ensuring that patients can effectively navigate complex information related to their hearing and balance health.

fields.title: Voice Disorders
fields.description: Students study the anatomy and physiology of normal voice production. This course reviews clinical and instrumental evaluation methods with emphasis on acoustic, aerodynamic and stroboscopic evaluation. Differential diagnosis of functional, organic, and neurogenic voice and resonance disorders and the treatment of these disorders across the lifespan are reviewed. Consideration for special voice populations including gender-affirming voice, laryngectomy and artificial airway.

fields.title: Reading and Research
fields.description: Designed to allow graduate students to pursue independent study and/or research in the area of speech, language and hearing disorders under appropriate faculty supervision. May be repeated for credit.

fields.title: Speech Practicum D
fields.description: This required practicum course is an advanced level practice-based experience.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 581 , CSD 582 and CSD 583 .

fields.title: Speech Practicum E
fields.description: This required practicum course is an advanced level practice-based experience. Both CSD 683 and CE 650 may be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 682 and permission of head of department.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in Speech Pathology and Audiology
fields.description: This course will cover advanced considerations relative to the diagnosis and management of individuals with speech, language and hearing disorders.

fields.title: Comprehensive Continuance
fields.description: Continued preparation in anticipation of the comprehensive examination. Course may be repeated.

fields.title: Thesis Research
fields.description: The thesis option generally requires three to four semesters to complete. Students choosing the thesis option will not be required to complete the written comprehensive examination. Students should talk with their advisor prior to this option. This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.

fields.title: Geriatric Audiology
fields.description: This course studies the aging process as it relates to communication and hearing. Evaluation and treatment strategies for the geriatric client are emphasized, along with special topics related to aging including auditory anatomy and physiology, diagnostic and rehabilitative services, and changes in auditory perception with advancing age.

fields.title: Pediatric Audiology
fields.description: Normal and pathological development of the auditory system; pediatric audiometric assessment; auditory and communication aspects in the habilitation of hearing-impaired children.

fields.title: Directed Research
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunity for research in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor. Emphasis on developing a question and hypothesis; selecting subjects and variables to investigate; collecting and analyzing data; and reporting results should provide the student with a meaningful research experience.

fields.title: Independent Study
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunities in-depth study in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Rotation B
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at clinical settings external to the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 639 .

fields.title: Implantable Auditory Devices
fields.description: This course addresses topics in the areas of cochlear implants and other implantable auditory devices. This course covers the basic knowledge in selection criteria for candidacy, signal processing of cochlear implants, pre and post implant audiological procedures, and habilitation/rehabilitation of patients with implantable auditory devices.

fields.title: Audiology Clinical Rotation C
fields.description: Supervised clinical practicum at clinical settings external to the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 719 .

fields.title: Medical Audiology
fields.description: Advanced study of the diagnosis and evaluation of hearing and balance disorders.

fields.title: Directed Research
fields.description: This course provides the opportunity for research in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor. Students are required to participate in gathering data and observing the process of developing new knowledge through research. Emphasis is placed on the student becoming an expert consumer of research, as well as gaining an appreciation for research methodology.

fields.title: Methods of Measurement in CSD
fields.description: Principles for applying instruments, technologies and measurement tools to research in a wide variety of investigations and clinical applications in communication sciences and disorders. A survey and in-depth review of the principal equipment and instrumentation that is available and predicted to be available to researchers and clinicians in the communication sciences and disorders.

fields.title: Ph.D. Professional Development Seminar I
fields.description: Discusses issues related to success in Ph.D. programs and development of skills as a researcher, leader, expert clinician and academician, such as characteristics of successful Ph.D. students; approaches to integrating course work; research learning; preparing review papers and research proposals; ethics in Ph.D. education and research; issues related to IRBs; intellectual property; collaborations; scholarly networks; authorships; and the funding of research. Topics are selected and designed to meet the individual needs of specific cohorts of CSD Ph.D. students early in their programs.

fields.title: Ph. D. Professional Development Seminar II
fields.description: Discusses issues related to preparing for the dissertation experience and life beyond a Ph.D. program. Topics may include strategies for writing up scientific results; differences between dissertations and research articles; getting into print; strategies for presenting research and strategic selection of venues; and planning and developing an academic/research career, such as the first job and post docs; choosing the employer; the application and selection process; establishing oneself as a researcher, scholar and academic; surviving the first university position; facts and fiction of tenure and promotion; and thinking beyond the first job (career planning). Specific topics are selected and designed to meet the individual needs of specific cohorts of CSD Ph.D. students that apply later in their programs.

fields.title: Grant Writing in Communication Sciences and Disorders
fields.description: This course offers a practical guide to writing persuasive grant proposals. The course will take the student from an original idea to its distillation into a compelling research question, presenting clear methods to answer the research question, assessing outcomes and navigating the appropriate funding agency. Discussions will include examples, hands-on activities, peer review of proposals and presentations by experienced faculty members.

fields.title: Professional Seminar in Audiology
fields.description: This course addresses selected topics, issues and other content designed to prepare students for clinical practice in audiology. Content is treated on an expert level with emphasis upon problem solving, integration of information across didactic and practical knowledge toward clinical skill development.

fields.title: Directed Research
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunity for research in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor. Emphasis on developing a question and hypothesis, selecting subjects and variables to investigate, collecting and analyzing data, and reporting results should provide the student with a meaningful research experience.

fields.title: Independent Study
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunities in-depth study in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor.

fields.title: Audiology Externship A
fields.description: Full-time clinical practicum with limited supervision at clinical settings external to the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 729 .

fields.title: Professional Seminar in Audiology
fields.description: This course addresses selected topics, issues and other content designed to prepare students for clinical practice in audiology. Content is treated on an expert level with emphasis upon problem solving and integration of information across didactic and practical knowledge toward clinical skill development.

fields.title: Audiology Externship C
fields.description: Full-time clinical practicum with limited supervision at clinical settings external to the Communication Sciences and Disorders Speech-Language-Hearing Clinic. This course may be repeated with permission of instructor for up to 6 credits.

fields.title: Foundations of Teaching and Learning
fields.description: This course is designed to equip future educators with the foundational knowledge and skills necessary for effective teaching at the college level. Through a blend of theoretical frameworks and practical applications, students will explore the core principles of pedagogy, curriculum design and assessment strategies.

fields.title: Mentored Teaching Experience in CSD
fields.description: Students enrolled in this course are mentored in a teaching assignment by an experienced faculty mentor. Teaching will be examined through observation, conferences, review of records and communication skills. Competencies for the Ph.D. student will be examined and related to best practices in pedagogy.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in CSD: Child Language Disorders
fields.description: This seminar focuses on the current views of etiology, assessment and treatment procedures of child language disorders.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in CSD: Aerodigestive Concerns
fields.description: This seminar focuses on the current views of etiology, assessment and treatment procedures of aerodigestive disorders.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in CSD: Neurolinguistics
fields.description: This seminar would be devoted to study and discussion of one or more topics current in neurolinguistic investigation. Possible topics include: PED and fMRI studies of language processing; event-related potentials; connectionist models of speech errors and paraphasias; morphosyntactic disorders in language disorders; role of prosody in language processing and neurological disorders; pragmatic studies of populations with brain damage.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in CSD: Voice Disorders
fields.description: This seminar focuses on the current views of etiology, assessment and treatment procedures of voice disorders.

fields.title: Advanced Seminar in CSD: Selected Topics I
fields.description: This seminar focuses on advanced study of selected topics of interest in communication sciences and disorders. May be repeated for credit.

fields.title: Experimental Phonetics
fields.description: Advanced and in-depth study of speech perception and production, including acoustics, intelligibility, current technologies and instrumentations, and theoretical models guiding research approaches.

fields.title: Directed Research
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunity for research in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor. Emphasis on developing a question and hypothesis, selecting subjects and variables to investigate, collecting and analyzing data, and reporting results should provide the student with a meaningful research experience.

fields.title: Independent Study
fields.description: This course sequence provides opportunities in-depth study in an area of special interest as directed by a faculty mentor.

fields.title: Doctoral Dissertation in CSD
fields.description: Culminating research project. Enrollment beyond second semester is contingent upon dissertation committee approval. This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.

fields.title: Dissertation Continuance
fields.description: Required continuance for dissertation after 12 credits earned for CSD 920 .

fields.title: Fundamental Human Communication: Presentations [C1HC]
fields.description: Study of human communication as a process. Overview of the principles and practices of interpersonal, small group and public communication. Emphasis on examining the role of self-concept, perception, culture, verbal and nonverbal dimensions in the communication process, using power and managing conflict, applying critical listening, practicing audience analysis within informative speech making. Public speaking required. May be used for general education credit. May not be used for major credit.
fields.prerequisites: If you have already earned credit for SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 , or SCOM 123 , you are not eligible to enroll for another SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 .

fields.title: Fundamental Human Communication: Individual Presentations [C1HC]
fields.description: Study of human communication as a process. Overview of the principles and practices of interpersonal, small group and public communication. Emphasis on examining the role of self-concept, perception, culture, verbal and nonverbal dimensions in the communication process, using power and managing conflict, applying critical listening, practicing audience analysis within informative speech making. Public speaking required. May be used for general education credit. May not be used for major credit.
fields.prerequisites: If you have already earned credit for SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 , or SCOM 123 , you are not eligible to enroll for another SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 .

fields.title: Fundamental Human Communication: Group Presentations [C1HC]
fields.description: Study of human communication as a process. Overview of the principles and practices of communication in small group and public communication contexts. Emphasis on examining the role of self-concept, perception, culture, verbal and nonverbal dimensions in the communication process, using power and managing conflict, applying critical listening, practicing audience analysis, and constructing informative and persuasive group presentations. Public speaking required. May be used for general education credit. May not be used for major credit.
fields.prerequisites: If you have already earned credit for SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 , or SCOM 123 , you are not eligible to enroll for another SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 .

fields.title: Introduction to Sport Communication
fields.description: This class provides a foundation for students who are pursuing a minor in sport communication. The course provides an overview about information management and how it applies to the professional sporting industry. Students will learn about careers in sport information, how an organization communicates with the media and its constituents, and how communication in sport has evolved and continues to evolve.
fields.prerequisites: Sport communication minor.

fields.title: Introduction to Communication Theory
fields.description: This course studies the theories and models that inform students' understanding of human communication processes. Emphasis is placed on the processes of theory building, comparison of theories, and the implications and application of theory to particular contexts. Consideration is given to the role of communication in all human endeavors. This course must be taken concurrently with SCOM 240L .
fields.prerequisites: Declared SCOM majors or declared SCOM minors only, and SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 , and sophomore standing or above.

fields.title: Communication Theory Lab
fields.description: This lab is designed to complement and supplement the SCOM 240 lecture course. Students will discuss, write and/or give presentations related to content covered in SCOM 240 . This course must be taken concurrently with SCOM 240 .
fields.prerequisites: Declared SCOM majors or SCOM minors only, and SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 , and sophomore standing or above.

fields.title: Presentational Speaking
fields.description: This course offers a study of methods for preparing and presenting public speeches. Students consider impromptu and extemporaneous speaking, sales speeches, business presentations and other special occasion speeches. Emphasis is placed on performance and evaluation.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major.

fields.title: Sport Communication Techniques: Writing and Reporting
fields.description: Basic skills of sport writing and reporting are studied and applied. Students gain experience in a variety of sports and learn and apply skills in researching, interviewing, reporting, writing columns and features involving the world of sports.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 230 .

fields.title: Signs, Symbols and Social Interaction
fields.description: This course studies verbal and nonverbal communication as used in human interaction. Consideration is given to the function of symbolic systems in self-concept development, the structuring of reality, and social discourse. Attention is directed toward the use of signs and symbols by different ethnic groups, genders, age groups and geographic groups.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 .

fields.title: Intercultural Communication
fields.description: This course explores intercultural theories and concepts within historical and political contexts and examines systems of power implicated in our communication. Exploring communication processes from critical and cultural perspectives encourages students to reflect on cultural knowledge, practices, attitudes, belief systems, and assumptions of self and others in our globalized and technological world. Working through course materials and activities together, we develop intercultural communication skills to cultivate more equitable relations.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 121 , SCOM 122 or SCOM 123 .

fields.title: Introduction to Public Relations
fields.description: Study of basic principles and practices of public relations. Consideration given to public relations problems and pragmatic solutions utilizing oral, written and electronic communication media and skills.

fields.title: Public Relations Techniques I: Written
fields.description: This course offers a study of writing fundamentals for public relations. Emphasis is placed on practice of effective writing for a variety of media (press releases, public service announcements, brochures, newsletters). Students must be able to use word processing software.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Introduction to Communication Research
fields.description: This course is an introduction to the principles, methods and analysis techniques used in the field of communication. Emphasis is placed on a broad-based understanding of the breadth of research in the field. This course includes both qualitative and quantitative research methods, methods of literature review and research article critiques. This course fulfills the College of Arts and Letters writing-intensive requirement for the major.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major.

fields.title: Study Abroad Pre-Departure Seminar
fields.description: This course prepares students participating in short-term study abroad programs in communication studies by exploring important social, historical and cultural content relevant to the study abroad locations and topics.

fields.title: Interdisciplinary Special Topics in Communication Studies
fields.description: This course is a study of interdisciplinary topics and issues in human communication. Emphasis will be on contemporary theories, research and principles. May be repeated up to six credits.

fields.title: Feminist Blogging: Writing for Shout Out! JMU
fields.description: The goal of this course is to work in a feminist collective to write daily blog posts for the Shout Out! JMU blog. Students will organize the blog, research and write blog posts, publicize the blog, and create dialogue by commenting on one another's blog posts as a means of consciousness raising.

fields.title: Third Wave Ecofeminism
fields.description: This course explores the historically strong association between women and nature, in which the image of Mother Earth is central, and critiques the power-as-domination assumption of our culture shown in the exploitation of women and of the earth itself. Religious, psychological, social, historical and scientific manifestations of this assumption will be examined, along with alternative models of power and responsibility. Students will explore the considerable research on ecofeminism.

fields.title: Special Topics in Health Communication
fields.description: Study of current topics and issues in health communication. Course content will vary by faculty. See MyMadison for the topic. May be repeated up to six credits.

fields.title: Language and Culture
fields.description: An introduction to linguistic anthropology. Explores the complex relationships between language and culture through topics such as language acquisition and socialization; language, thought and worldview; language and identity; multilingualism; how and why languages change; literacy; and the politics of language use and language ideologies.

fields.title: Special Topics in Organizational Communication
fields.description: Study of topics and issues in organizational communication. Emphasis on contemporary theories, research and principles. May be repeated up to six credits.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 240 , SCOM 350 , and Organizational Communication concentration; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Sport Communication Minor Practicum
fields.description: This course provides approved co-curricular learning experience in sport communication. May be repeated for a maximum of 6.00 credit hours.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 230 ; Sport communication minor.

fields.title: Topics in Communication Studies
fields.description: This course studies current topics and issues in human communication. Emphasis is placed on contemporary theories, research and principles.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor, or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Communication in Romantic Relationships
fields.description: This class acquaints students with relevant theory and research associated with communication in various stages of romantic relationships including initiation, maintenance and dissolution. Emphasis is on honing one's ability to understand communication theory, research and application while enhancing one's communication skills in romantic relationships. Additionally, students will improve their ability to communicate about relationship research through writing, presenting and discussing.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Competitive Speech Team
fields.description: This course offers students experience in intercollegiate speech competition. Students have an opportunity to research, prepare, practice and compete in interpretation, public address and limited preparation events. Students will cultivate communication skills while researching, practicing and competing; while listening to and critically evaluating others' speeches; and while meeting and engaging with other competitors, coaches and judges. No more than six hours of practicum credit can be applied to the SCOM major. Students must be on the university's speech team to enroll.

fields.title: Debate Team
fields.description: This course is a practicum course for students competing in intercollegiate debate competition with the JMU Debate Team. Students are required to practice, prepare and research arguments on the national collegiate debate topic and participate in practice and competition debates. No more than six hours of practicum credit can be applied to the SCOM major. Students must be on the university's Debate Team to enroll.

fields.title: Practicum in Communication Studies
fields.description: Approved co-curricular activities and/or projects of a practical nature. No more than six hours of practicum credit can be applied to major. Proposals must be submitted to and approved by the course instructor for section and credit hour registration. To receive repeat credit, see school director.

fields.title: Bluestone Communications Practicum
fields.description: This is the practicum course for JMU's student-run public relations firm, Bluestone Communications. Students further their theoretical understanding and practical skills in the processes of research, planning, communication/action and evaluation by implementing public relations strategies and tactics for specific organizations. Students need to apply to take this course.

fields.title: Introduction to Interpersonal Communication
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to the fundamental theoretical perspectives in interpersonal communication. Emphasis is placed on the effects of verbal and nonverbal messages on continuity and change in personal relationships. Students consider the influence of cultural and social contexts on messages in relationships and develop their communication competence in diverse interpersonal contexts.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Small Group Communication
fields.description: This course studies the communication processes involved in solving problems when working with others in a small group context. Emphasis is placed on the concepts of roles, norms, leadership and decision-making. Students consider small group factors which influence problem-solving effectiveness.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Special Topics in Interpersonal Communication
fields.description: This course studies current topics and issues in interpersonal communication. Topics and issues may include, but are not limited to aging and lifespan, communication education, computer mediated relations, deception and secrecy, friendship and rivalry, relationship rejuvenation, and social support. This course may be repeated up to six credits.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Communication and Conflict
fields.description: This course considers theories of conflict emerging from the communication discipline and their application to different forms of conflict at all levels of human interaction. This course offers an examination of communication and varied responses to conflict in diverse situations. Emphasis is placed on competencies required for successful management, intervention and transformation of conflict.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Negotiations
fields.description: This course provides an overview of negotiation as a strategy for dealing with conflict.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: The Art of Public Debate
fields.description: This course focuses on the practical application and critical examination of debate in the public sphere. The course provides students with experience in researching, constructing and presenting topics for public debate. Additionally, students will be asked to examine pieces of public debate in order to provide them with the tools to critically examine public discourse in a manner consistent with being a productive and active citizen. This course will culminate with a public debate tournament.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Principles and Processes of Interviewing
fields.description: This course studies communication principles and processes in interviewing. Emphasis is placed on interpersonal processes involved in interview structures, goals and question types. Students develop their communication skills in information, persuasive, counseling, health care, employment and performance appraisal interviews.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Persuasion
fields.description: The study of oral communication as a determinant of attitudinal and behavioral change. Emphasis on the various kinds of artistic and nonartistic proofs as they apply to human motivation. Consideration of the application of behavioral research findings to persuasion.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 240 .

fields.title: Argument and Advocacy
fields.description: This course studies the techniques and principles of argument and advocacy. Emphasis is placed on developing, presenting and defending a position on controversial questions. Consideration is given to contemporary theories of public argument.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Contemporary Rhetorical Theory and Practice
fields.description: Examines contemporary rhetorical theory and practice in relation to specific social, economic and technological changes in the 20th century, with particular emphasis on theoretical frameworks. Students learn about the changing needs of postmodern communicators and how new rhetorical theories have developed to anticipate, respond to, and shape those changes. Also explored is the value of contemporary rhetorical theories for communicative and performative events.
fields.prerequisites: WRTC 200 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Oral Interpretation
fields.description: Study and application of theories concerning the oral presentation of various forms of literature including prose, poetry, drama and nonfiction materials. Emphasis on performance.
fields.prerequisites: Any 100-level SCOM course.

fields.title: Nonverbal Communication
fields.description: Study of nonverbal means through which people relate to one another. Consideration of the communicative effects of environment, facial expression, voice, posture, gestures, touch, distance and physical appearance.
fields.prerequisites: Any 200-level SCOM course.

fields.title: Free Speech in America
fields.description: The study of the evolution of freedom of speech in America from Colonial times to the present day. Emphasis on the major periods of development and on the role of courts in defining freedom of speech. Special consideration of contemporary freedom of speech controversies.

fields.title: Communication, Diversity and Popular Culture
fields.description: This course explores the representational, institutional and communication practices that contribute to the construction of identities and diversity in popular culture. Students will explore how ideologies are reproduced and how understandings of race, class, gender, ethnicity, sexuality, ability and a range of other intersecting axes of identity are shaped within popular culture artifacts. Emphasis will be placed on critical analysis of current popular culture texts.
fields.prerequisites: Any 100-level SCOM course.

fields.title: Communication and Gender
fields.description: This course explores the role of communication in the social construction of gender across a variety of contexts. Students will critically examine the interconnectedness of sex, gender, sexuality, race and class toward understanding systems of privilege and oppression in communication practices and social institutions. Focus is on communication as a tool for personal and social change.
fields.prerequisites: Any 100-level SCOM course.

fields.title: Ethnographic Approaches to Communication Studies
fields.description: This course examines the value of ethnographic methodologies and other narrative forms of scholarship for enriching understandings of complex social issues and exploring the potential of communication toward shaping social change. Students will develop literacies in reading and evaluating ethnographic works and interrogating their contributions toward cultivating more just social worlds.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Organizational Communication
fields.description: This course draws on communication theory to analyze various organizational communication practices such as the management of workers, development of organizational culture and interaction with larger systems. Students gain a complex understanding of organizing practices by investigating how historical events have influenced organizational communication and managerial practices at work. Learning is complemented by an experiential learning project.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Visual Rhetoric
fields.description: A study of the rhetorical foundations of visual and verbal arguments in academic disciplines and popular culture. Students will analyze and produce visual and verbal arguments in a variety of rhetorical contexts.
fields.prerequisites: WRTC 103 and any 100-level communication studies course or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Communication and Social Movements
fields.description: This course studies the use of communication in social movements. Emphasis is placed on the types of communication used in social movements and on ways to produce and respond to such messages. This course examines a variety of different social movements within the political process including nonprofit organizations.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: American Political Culture and Communication
fields.description: This course studies the functions performed by communication in politics. Emphasis is placed on a variety of communication forms and techniques used by advocates both in campaigning and governing. Consideration is given to contemporary campaigns and the role of communication in their successes and failures.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Environmental Communication and Advocacy
fields.description: This course is an exploration of the multifaceted aspects of environmental controversies including the rhetoric, advocacy campaigns and decision-making processes that produce and attempt to manage environmental conflict. Emphasis on persuasive efforts by, interest groups, corporations, resource managers, government agencies, scientific experts, politicians and citizens to influence public understanding of environmental issues, adoption of sustainable behavior and lifestyles, and public policy outcomes.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor; or environmental sciences, environmental studies, environmental management and environmental humanities minor; or political communication minor.

fields.title: Food as Communication
fields.description: This course examines food as symbolic in everyday life, with attention to negotiated understandings of identities, communities, cultures and environments. The course focuses on issues such as how we communicate identity through food consumed and not consumed; how food choices create, shape and reflect communities and cultures; how messages from mass media and government frame, influence and shape food practices; and how food practices intersect, communicate and impact surrounding environments.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or African, African American and Diaspora Studies minor.

fields.title: Immigrant Advocacy
fields.description: This course invites students to adopt narrative approaches to communication and identity, and to reflectively learn from the storied and lived experiences of immigrants locally and in the United States. Students will have opportunities to hear from members of local non-profit organizations that serve migrant populations and will work toward developing engaging, creative advocacy of social justice and universal human rights.
fields.prerequisites: Any 100-level SCOM course.

fields.title: Youth, Communication and Culture
fields.description: This course critically examines the complex and evolving interconnections between young people, communication and culture. Grounded in the understanding that there is no one singular lived experience of "youth," the course focuses on: how young people are represented in popular culture artifacts; how cultural beliefs about various young people are constructed by public discourse; how diverse young people navigate popular culture messages; how they are constructed as target markets; and how they use technology to claim space in the broader culture. This course encourages students to examine their own experiences with and relationships to a range of communication artifacts.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Business and Professional Communication Studies
fields.description: Students investigate the nuance and complexity of communication in modern organizational life. A portion of the class is dedicated to the skills involved in a competitive, successful career search. In addition, students develop the skills to become an ethical and effective organizational citizen.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Communication, Diversity and British Popular Culture
fields.description: This course explores the rhetorical dimension of communication practices and texts found in British popular culture. Emphasizing critical analysis, students will examine how issues of diversity are communicated, represented and contested across British media such as television, film, music and digital platforms. The course examines how strategic communication choices construct cultural narratives in a diverse, multicultural world. Emphasis is placed on critical thinking and self-reflexivity.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the JMU semester in London.

fields.title: British Media and Society
fields.description: Study the history, nature and impact of mass media in the United Kingdom. Emphasis on the impact modern media has on society, and society has on media. Consideration of similarities and differences in mass media in the United States and Great Britain. Consideration of the relationship between mass media and the arts. Focus on 20th century mass media in London, one of the world's preeminent and most influential centers. London term only.

fields.title: Public Relations Techniques II: Visual
fields.description: Study of visual communication techniques for public relations. Survey of design principles and elements used for developing visually effective messages with an emphasis on publication design and production, photography, and computer-mediated presentations. Students should provide a camera and be familiar with desktop publishing and presentational software.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 261 and fully-admitted SCOM major in the public relations concentration.

fields.title: Public Relations Theory and Concepts
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to introduce students to the theoretical body of knowledge in public relations. In this course, students will learn core tenants of important theories and concepts and apply these to the ethical practice of public relations. The breadth of theories covered will be useful for any public relations specialization and builds an essential foundation to better understand the research-based character of the public relations process.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major in the public relations concentration.

fields.title: International Public Relations
fields.description: This course explores the special professional challenges and opportunities arising from the dynamic global public relations developments characterizing the beginning of this century, taking into account social, economic, political, legal and cultural factors as well as new media developments.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major.

fields.title: Sports Public Relations
fields.description: This class is designed to provide students with opportunities to explore the profession of sports public relations. In this class, students will discuss various sports communication issues including media relations, community relations, player relations, fan relations, crisis communication, sports social responsibility and more.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Advanced Public Relations Writing
fields.description: This course offers advanced public relations students experience in the wide range of writing style and applications that are essential to successfully begin their professional careers. The course focuses on understanding and mastering action-oriented communication methods and best professional practices. This course provides both a conceptual framework and in-depth training in advanced techniques.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 261 and fully-admitted SCOM major in the public relations concentration.

fields.title: Topics in Engaged Public Relations
fields.description: Students will explore a specific context of public relations and how public relations theories, processes, and skills can be used in the context. During the semester, students will discuss specific publics within the context and apply ethical communication strategies and tactics to engage with those publics. Courses provided could include crisis communication, corporate social responsibility, social media management, fashion public relations, etc. based on the expertise of the instructor.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major.

fields.title: Introduction to Health Communication
fields.description: This course offers an introduction to the study of communication in health and illness contexts. It covers the impact of interpersonal relationships, sociocultural and organizational influences, and media and health campaigns on health beliefs and behaviors. Emphasis is placed on strategies and approaches that promote effective communication in a variety of health contexts.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor or Sport Communication minor.

fields.title: Disability and Advocacy
fields.description: This class will go over the history of disability rights rhetoric in the advancement of disability civil rights in the United States. Topics will include (but not be limited to) the three models of disability discourse (moral, medical and social); strategies employed during the passage of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA); the ways in which disability civil rights has been coopted by non-disabled folks; how some advocacy strategies created limitations in the enforcement of the ADA; and current discourse surrounding the improvement of disability civil rights in the United States.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM majors or minors, disability studies minors, medical humanities minors or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Rhetorical Research Methods
fields.description: The study of rhetorical and critical research methods in various communication contexts. Emphasis is on developing and applying appropriate standards to consider communicative factors such as audience, tone, and rhetorical strategies. Consideration of criticism of public address, mass media, and other forms of persuasive communication. Students will be expected to conduct an original research project and present findings in a paper and/or oral presentation.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 with a minimum grade of "C-".

fields.title: Quantitative Experimental Research Methods
fields.description: The study of quantitative research methods in various communication contexts. Emphasis is on ability to research literature, develop and evaluate experimental design, and apply and interpret statistical tests. Students will be expected to conduct an original research project and present findings in a paper and/or oral presentation.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 with a minimum grade of "C-".

fields.title: Qualitative Research Methods
fields.description: Study of interpretive approaches to communication research using a variety of qualitative research methods, including field observation, qualitative interviewing, focus groups, narrative analysis and discourse analysis. Students will plan and conduct an exploratory qualitative study, prepare a written research report including a literature review and make a research presentation.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 with a minimum grade of "C-".

fields.title: Survey Research Methods
fields.description: The study of survey research methods in various communication contexts. Emphasis on using survey research methodology in communication audits, public relations problems and public opinion polling and the ability to research literature, develop and evaluate survey questions, and apply and interpret statistical tests. Students will be expected to conduct an original research project and present findings in a paper and/or oral presentation.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 with a minimum grade of "C-".

fields.title: Campaign Research Methods
fields.description: The study of research methods in various communication contexts. Emphasis is on ability to use research methods at various stages of communication planning including background research, primary research, strategic planning, monitoring and evaluation. Students will be expected to conduct an original research project and present findings in a paper and/or oral presentation.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 with a minimum grade of "C-".

fields.title: Directed Projects
fields.description: Supervised projects related to any aspect of human communication. Emphasis on original individual or group programs beyond the school's usual curricular or co-curricular offerings. Formal report(s) required for awarding of credit.

fields.title: Study Abroad Seminar
fields.description: Intensive examination of specialized international communication topics arranged in cooperation with a faculty member. Prior arrangements must be made with the program director.

fields.title: Sport Communication Internship
fields.description: This advanced internship course offers students the opportunity to apply and refine their sports communication skills in a professional setting beyond the practicum level. Designed for students who have successfully completed the sports communication practicum, this course emphasizes deeper engagement, strategic communication and increased responsibility in the field. Students will take on more specialized roles, contribute to higher-level projects and demonstrate advanced competencies in areas such as media relations, content creation, digital strategy or event communication. This course may be repeated for a maximum of six credit hours with departmental approval.
fields.prerequisites: Sport Communication minors only; SCOM 230 and SCOM 312 ; and permission of the school director.

fields.title: Advanced Topics in Communication Studies
fields.description: This course offers an in-depth exploration and analysis of a communication-related theory, context, topic or problem, culminating in a research project documented in written, oral, visual and/or multimedia presentations. Course content varies based on faculty expertise.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Attachment Communication
fields.description: This class acquaints students with relevant theory and research associated with the science of attachment, its impact on brain development and its subsequent impact on how we communicate throughout the lifespan. In addition to gaining an in-depth understanding of how attachment impacts communication and relationships throughout life, students will also improve their ability to communicate about attachment research through writing, presenting and discussing.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Feminist Rhetorics
fields.description: Surveys key women figures in classical and contemporary rhetorical traditions and challenges the strategies used to historicize this tradition from feminist perspectives. Explores diverse feminist rhetorical discourses informed by race, sexual orientation, ethnicity and social class.
fields.prerequisites: WRTC 103 or equivalent and junior or senior standing; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Leadership Communication
fields.description: This course promotes understanding and development of organizational leadership through investigation of theory and analysis. Students explore varied and sometimes contradictory models of leadership and learn how to articulate and express ideas that encourage others to advocate for and bring about positive change.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Legal Communication
fields.description: Study of the role of communication in the legal process. Emphasis on communication questions/problems which litigants, lawyers, judges and jurors face. Consideration of legal argument, negotiation, trial advocacy, decision making and communication technologies.

fields.title: Family Communication
fields.description: Study of the processes and functions of family communication, including managing dating, marital, parent-child and inter-generational relations. Theoretical and applied examination of communication and cultural processes that define and construct family structures, systems and boundaries. Course also examines histories of family communication as constructed in popular culture.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 280 and Fully Admitted SCOM Majors only.

fields.title: Oral History
fields.description: This course will explore the theory and practice of oral history. Through a series of readings, students will consider the many promises and challenges of the discipline, including issues related to memory, objectivity, ethics, the law, and technology. Students will also engage in an experiential learning exercise in which they collaborate to produce an oral history project.

fields.title: Advanced Topics in Advocacy Studies
fields.description: Advanced topics in advocacy studies is the concentration's capstone. Through case studies, readings, discussions and experiential activities students investigate complex issues in the field of advocacy. Students apply theoretical knowledge and skills as they explore the interaction between advocacy and communication.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and senior standing.

fields.title: Communication Tools for Organizational Challenges
fields.description: Organizations frequently face challenges related to communication, collaboration, training, facilitating meetings and conversations about complex issues, and navigating change. This course equips students with the knowledge and tools to address these challenges and implement communication-based interventions. Through hands on learning, students will identify an organizational challenge and design responses that facilitate positive change and collaboration.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Communication, Culture and Identity
fields.description: This class examines theory and research of cultural communication, and reflexively considers how communication practices construct identities and arrange social relations within diverse contexts and applied settings.
fields.prerequisites: Any one of the following courses: SCOM 305 , SCOM 347 , SCOM 348 , SCOM 349 , SCOM 352 , or SCOM 357 .

fields.title: Advanced Studies in Organizational Communication
fields.description: This capstone course uses case studies, readings, discussions and experiential activities to investigate complex issues that emerge for organizations and their members. Students apply theoretical knowledge and skills to the analysis of communication problems through an applied field study in an organization.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 350 and senior standing, or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Political Campaign Communication
fields.description: An advanced study of communication techniques, procedures and processes as they relate to political campaign communication. Emphasis upon the design, execution and production of various communication messages. Consideration of the impact and utilization of various technologies in political campaigns.

fields.title: Fundraising Campaigns and Donor Motivation
fields.description: This course examines the theories and practices of fundraising campaigns, including campaign planning, fundraising communication, donor research and motivation, branding and message development, stewardship and recognition, special events, planned giving, capital campaigns, program evaluation, and fundraising ethics.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor, and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Public Relations Management
fields.description: This course offers intensive study and research of advanced communication management skills, theory and principles using case and field studies. Special attention is given to systematic and ethical management of communication and action affecting an organization's internal and external publics.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 260 and fully-admitted SCOM major in the public relations concentration.

fields.title: Public Relations Campaigns
fields.description: This is the capstone course for the public relations program of study. Students further their theoretical understanding and practical skills in the processes of research, planning, communication/action and evaluation by conducting campaigns for specific organizations.
fields.prerequisites: SCOM 362 , one advanced research method course ( SCOM 381 , SCOM 383 , SCOM 385 , SCOM 386 or SCOM 388 ), and one public relations context course ( SCOM 363 , SCOM 365 , SCOM 369 or SCOM 460 ).

fields.title: Student-Run Public Relations Firm
fields.description: This is the capstone course for the public relations program of study. Students further their theoretical understanding and practical skills in the processes of research, planning, communication/action and evaluation by implementing public relations strategies and tactics for specific organizations. Students need to apply to take this course.

fields.title: Special Topics in Sport Communication
fields.description: This course studies current topics and issues in sports communication. Course content varies based on faculty expertise. This course may be repeated up to six credits.
fields.prerequisites: Sport Communication minor and SCOM 230 .

fields.title: Rhetoric of Environmental Science and Technology
fields.description: This course offers an advanced study of the way the public receives, makes sense of, and influences scientific and technical information about environmental issues. Implications of these processes on environmental policy will be analyzed. Readings and assignments will concentrate on the interactions between technical and public spheres of communication, with an in-depth examination of the way the media facilitates the transfer of information between scientific communities and public audiences.
fields.prerequisites: WRTC 103 or equivalent and junior or senior standing; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Interpersonal Communication in Health Contexts
fields.description: This course explores how effective interpersonal communication supports the management of mental and physical health within social networks. Students will examine health-related experiences; the roles of stress, coping and social support; the connection between relationship contexts on health outcomes; and strategies for collaboration in clinical and non-clinical settings.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Health Communication Campaigns
fields.description: This course focuses on the theoretical principles and practical considerations relevant to designing, implementing and evaluating health communication campaigns. Emphasis is placed on the collection and analysis of formative research. The final project for the course involves designing a health campaign targeting a specific audience.
fields.prerequisites: Fully-admitted SCOM major or minor, and SCOM 370 ; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Culture and Health Communication
fields.description: This course explores the relationship between culture and health in different contexts. In particular, the course focuses on the role of communication in understanding diverse health beliefs and engaging in dialogue about our own health beliefs.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Media and Politics
fields.description: This course is a study of the media's role in the political system, concentrating on the dynamic and interdependent relationships among journalists, politicians, the public and public policy. The course explores media and politics theories; how media practices and technologies shape political decision making; how political forces influence media institutions; and how public opinion and media narratives are shaped.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted SCOM major or minor (SCOM, CLTC, HTHC).

fields.title: Media and Politics
