fields.description: Intermediate skills in jazz dance technique, vocabulary and movement combinations. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: None for School of Theatre and Dance majors and dance minors. Non-majors: DANC 146 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Tap
fields.description: Intermediate skills in tap dance technique, vocabulary and models of sequencing. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: None for School of Theatre and Dance majors and dance minors. Non-majors: DANC 147 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: History of Dance: Renaissance Through the 20th Century
fields.description: A survey of dance history in Western civilization from the Renaissance to the present. Emphasis is on the dance idioms of ballet and modern.

fields.title: Topics in Dance
fields.description: Study of selected timely topics in dance. May be repeated when course content changes. See MyMadison for current topic.

fields.title: Contemporary Dance Ensemble Repertory II (0, 4)
fields.description: Intermediate-level experiences in performance, choreography and technical theatre with a modern dance ensemble. May be repeated for credit. Prerequisite: DANC 211 or the equivalent and concurrent enrollment in a dance technique course.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 211 or the equivalent and concurrent enrollment in a dance technique course.

fields.title: Virginia Repertory Dance Company II (0, 4)
fields.description: Advanced rehearsal, performance and technical theatre experience in a modern dance company. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 212 or the equivalent and concurrent enrollment in a dance technique course.

fields.title: Injury Prevention and Conditioning
fields.description: This course is designed to educate the dancer and dance education student on specific injury prevention and conditioning principles to improve overall dancer health and wellness. A combination of lecture and movement-based labs will cover all aspects that may contribute to injury risk in dancers and allows recognition of these risks in the educational or performance setting.
fields.prerequisites: Dance majors, dance minors and STAD majors; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Anatomy and Somatic Studies for the Dancer
fields.description: An introduction to the structure and function of the human body, along with an overview of contemporary bodywork theories and techniques essential to the education of dancers. Emphasis will be on the application of knowledge within the context of dance technique.
fields.prerequisites: Sophomore, junior and senior dance majors only.

fields.title: Dance in Community
fields.description: This course introduces students to the use of creative movement and dance in community settings. Emphasis is on concepts and skills utilized in designing and implementing movement experiences for diverse populations.

fields.title: Intermediate Modern Dance II (0, 4)
fields.description: Modern dance technique for an accelerated intermediate level. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 240 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Ballet II (0, 4)
fields.description: Ballet technique on an accelerated intermediate level. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 242 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Dance Composition I (2, 2)
fields.description: Introductory studies of dance composition with focus on the learning and development of choreographic techniques and styles. Compositional movement studies and solo/duet dances will be utilized for exploring and developing the student's individual creativity.
fields.prerequisites: Dance majors only.

fields.title: Intermediate Jazz II/Musical Theatre Styles
fields.description: Intermediate Jazz II / Musical Theatre Styles is a continuation of the jazz dance techniques in the dance program at the upper-intermediate level. The primary focus of this class will be on the study and training of historic and contemporary musical theatre jazz movement and its cultural influences. The course may be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 246 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Dance Teaching Practicum
fields.description: This course provides pre-service teachers with hands-on teaching experience prior to full-time student teaching. The course provides the opportunity for dance education students to observe certified teachers, plan lessons, reflect on effective teaching strategies, analyze the complexities of teaching and demonstrate professional behaviors that promote student learning. Course work includes topics on classroom management, assessment and effective teaching strategies.

fields.title: Directed Projects
fields.description: Supervised projects related to the study of dance. Credit given for original, individual or group programs beyond the usual course offerings in dance. A suitable completed project or report is required before credit will be given. Teaching assistantships are also registered as directed projects. May be repeated multiple times.
fields.prerequisites: Dance majors only.

fields.title: Contemporary Dance Ensemble Repertory III (0, 4)
fields.description: Advanced-level experiences in performance, choreography and technical theatre with a modern dance ensemble. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 311 or the equivalent and concurrent enrollment in a dance technique course.

fields.title: Virginia Repertory Dance Company III (0, 4)
fields.description: Advanced rehearsal, performance and technical theatre experience in a modern dance company for the professional level dancer. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 312 or the equivalent and concurrent enrollment in a dance technique course.

fields.title: Advanced Modern Dance (0, 4)
fields.description: Modern dance technique on an advanced level. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 340 or the equivalent.

fields.title: Advanced Ballet (0, 4)
fields.description: Ballet technique on an advanced level. May be repeated for credit.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 342 or the equivalent.

fields.title: Dance Composition II (2, 2)
fields.description: Dance composition study involving the development and use of complex choreographic structures with emphasis on creating small and large group dance compositions, as well as the exploration of contemporary choreographic styles and techniques.
fields.prerequisites: DANC 345 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Advanced Jazz
fields.description: A continuation of the dance technique in the dance program. Advanced skills in jazz technique with special emphasis on the development of performance skills. May be repeated for credit.

fields.title: The Dance Professional
fields.description: Introduction to the professional dance world through lectures, discussions and research. Emphasis will be placed on the preparation of skills and materials necessary to pursue dance as a career. Contemporary dance trends and issues will also be explored.
fields.prerequisites: Senior dance majors only.

fields.title: Methods of Teaching Dance
fields.description: An exploration of teaching creative movement in elementary school and dance in secondary school. Topics include creative movement, dance education and arts integration. This course considers lesson planning, classroom management and assessment in middle and high school.
fields.prerequisites: Junior and senior dance majors only.

fields.title: Student Teaching
fields.description: Enables students to apply, in the public school classrooms and the comprehensive child development programs, those skills and attitudes acquired in all components of teacher education. Under the guidance of university supervisors, students are provided activities designed to familiarize them with the classroom teacher's role.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 160 and EDUC 200 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Dance
fields.description: Special studies are independent studies for students to pursue individual research under the guidance of a faculty advisor. Special studies differ from directed projects in that they are more research-based than project-based, although some student mainstage designs might also be undertaken as special studies. Based on the agreed upon workload, this course may be assigned credit hours of 1-3 credits.

fields.title: Internship
fields.description: Internships may be registered for credit at the discretion of the individual faculty advisor. Overrides for internships must be completed no later than four weeks prior to the internship start date. Based on the agreed upon workload, this course may be assigned credit hours of 3-6 credits.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Repeatable for a maximum of 6 credits.

fields.title: Introduction to Data
fields.description: An interdisciplinary introduction to how data is organized, managed, visualized and analyzed across STEM disciplines. Ethical collection and use of data, with real-world test cases. Fundamentals of the tools and applications used in the analysis of data sets.

fields.title: Introduction to Machine Learning
fields.description: This is an introductory course on machine learning with focus on regression and classification methods. The objective is to familiarize students with some basic models and algorithms for machine learning and prepare them for research or industry application of machine learning techniques. Several software libraries and publicly available datasets will be used to illustrate the application of these techniques. The emphasis will be on machine learning algorithms and application, with some broad explanation of the underlying principles.
fields.prerequisites: MATH 229 , or MATH 220 with permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Principles of Data Science
fields.description: This course introduces students to the principles and tools of data science. It provides a foundation for properly collecting and analyzing data to draw insights and to answer data-driven questions. By using real-world examples, this course prompts students to think critically about applying these understandings to their workplace. Students get a broad overview of data warehousing and querying as well as data exploration, visualization and analysis. This course also introduces students to the principles of ethics, privacy, fairness and accountability in collection and management of databases and in making decisions based on data.
fields.prerequisites: MATH 522 or permission of the department.

fields.title: Data Visualization
fields.description: This course will introduce students to industry-standard graphic and data design techniques to create effective visualization and data storytelling. Students will also learn about the ethical implications of data visualization and evaluate the reliability and validity of data sets.
fields.prerequisites: DATA 525 .

fields.title: Applied Machine Learning
fields.description: This course will emphasize the core underlying principles, models and applications specific to machine learning and systems in production. In addition to gaining conceptual understanding of the mathematics underlying various machine learning models, students will gain hands-on experience in applying various machine learning models to real datasets using production-ready software platforms and programming languages.
fields.prerequisites: DATA 525 .

fields.title: Data Science for Environment and Society
fields.description: This course is designed to cover two pivotal areas: social and geospatial network analysis. It is tailored for students and professionals who are interested in applying data science techniques to environmental and societal challenges. Through this course, participants will learn to harness the power of network analysis in the context of social structures and geospatial data, enabling them to uncover patterns, relationships and insights critical for addressing complex issues in our society and environment.
fields.prerequisites: DATA 527 .

fields.title: Foundations in Digital Studies
fields.description: This course uses hands-on work with digital tools and techniques to answer questions in the humanities and social sciences. It examines the histories of major digital projects and methods; introduces students to a range of resources, spaces, and practitioners within the College of Arts and Letters and across JMU; and considers the impact of digital technologies as complex, socially situated and political tools through which humans make meaning. This course is required for the Digital Studies minor, but is open to all.

fields.title: Introduction to Disability Studies
fields.description: This course is required for the disability studies minor. It provides students with an overview of the ways disability is positioned within a number of intellectual frameworks, including the political, rhetorical, social, educational, historical and legal.
fields.prerequisites: Declaration of the disability studies minor.

fields.title: Diversity, Equity and Justice in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: Considers current problems and issues in early childhood education.
fields.prerequisites: Fully accepted into Teacher Education; minimum grades of "C" or better in ECED 372 , ECED 444 , ECED 445 and LED 355 .

fields.title: Diversity in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This course guides students in critically examining their own perspectives regarding diversity, seeks to expand students' awareness and understanding of individuals and groups representing differences, and explores pedagogical issues and practices essential for embracing the whole community of learners and families.

fields.title: Introduction to Early Childhood Education
fields.description: Introductory study of the role of the teacher, the role of the learner and the developing child as the basis for designing programs and developing curriculum for children 0-8 with different abilities and from various cultures.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag).

fields.title: Natural and Social Sciences for Young Children
fields.description: Study of content, processes, teaching methods and materials for teaching science and social studies in the early childhood classroom. Knowledge of cognitive development as applied to the selection of content in method will be examined.
fields.prerequisites: Fully accepted into Teacher Education (02 Flag); Minimum grades of "C" in ECED 372 , ECED 444 , ECED 445 and LED 355 .

fields.title: Practicum in Child Development
fields.description: This course is a supervised field experience in which students work in an early childhood laboratory classroom with pre-kindergarten age children. It emphasizes applications of age-appropriate guidance strategies for facilitating children's total development, including children with diverse needs. Observational strategies for assessing growth and progress are developed.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C" in each of ELED 271 , ECED 372 and LED 366 ;

fields.title: The Young Child
fields.description: This course integrates child development knowledge and theories, academic content knowledge, and age/stage appropriate guidance strategies for teaching children pre-kindergarten through grade three. Emphasis on observational/assessment strategies and inquiry processes related to young children's growth and development as a basis for teaching decisions.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag); a minimum grade of "C" in ECED 372 .

fields.title: Practicum in Primary Grades
fields.description: This field experience supports the study of child development and emerging literacy through direct observation and interactions with children in a classroom setting. Candidates will examine and reflect on their personal attitudes, assumptions and behaviors toward students and their families who represent diverse class, cultural and linguistic backgrounds. Students will complete 80 hours over the course of the full semester (16 weeks).
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag), A minimum grade of "C" in ECED 372 .

fields.title: Mathematics Content and Pedagogy for Early Childhood Education I
fields.description: This is the first of two courses that helps prospective early childhood teachers (PreK-3) develop mathematical content and pedagogical knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-3. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning in the following mathematical strands: number and number sense, computation and estimation, and patterns, functions and algebra.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag).

fields.title: Mathematics Content and Pedagogy for Early Childhood Education II
fields.description: This is the second of two courses that helps prospective early childhood teachers (PreK-3) develop mathematical content and pedagogical knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-3. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning of geometry, measurement, data analysis and probability.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag); a minimum grade of "C" in ECED 372 .

fields.title: Integrated Day Practicum
fields.description: This all-day, primary-grade practicum allows students to demonstrate their educational decision-making skills through planning, implementing and evaluating appropriate activities for children of diverse interests, needs and abilities. Strategies to assess learning, guide behavior, work with professionals and involve families are applied in this practicum and accompanying seminar.
fields.prerequisites: Fully accepted into Teacher Education (02 Flag); minimum grades of "C" in ECED 372 , ECED 444 , ECED 445 and LED 355 .

fields.title: Student Teaching ECED
fields.description: Enables students to apply in public school classrooms those understandings, skills and attitudes acquired in all components of teacher education. Under the guidance of university supervisors and cooperating teachers, students engage in full-time teaching responsibilities.
fields.prerequisites: Meet all requirements for student teaching (03 Flag); minimum grades of "C" in ECED 304 , ECED 372 , ECED 442 , ECED 443 , ECED 444 , ECED 445 , LED 355 and LED 456 .

fields.title: Fieldwork in Family and Community
fields.description: This fieldwork is designed to provide support for students and reinforces skills and concepts learned during the education program which are being applied during student teaching. Particular attention is given to school and family/community unity.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grades of "C" in ECED 372 , ECED 441 , ECED 442 , ECED 443 , ECED 454, ECED 461 , LED 366 , LED 436 ,and ECED 444 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: Designed to give capable students opportunities to complete independent research on educational problems under faculty guidance. The plan for the study must be presented to the department head in prescribed form for approval prior to registration.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag).

fields.title: Capstone in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: The teaching seminar is a space for students to reflect on their experiences, grapple with how to best meet the needs of diverse learners and contemplate their evolving identity as a teacher. Through this course, students will recognize the vital role that families and communities play in shaping and supporting children. Students will become a resource for themselves, their peers, their grade level team, their students and the families. As students transition from being a student to a professional, they will continue to develop not only their content knowledge and pedagogy, but also their skills and dispositions.

fields.title: Honors Project
fields.prerequisites: Teacher Ed Program 02 Flag.

fields.title: Observation and Study of the Young Child
fields.description: Skills for observing, recording and interpreting the behavior of the young child as a basis for adult intervention and guidance are developed. Laboratory experience is required.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 160 .

fields.title: The Creative Arts in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This course introduces theory and writing about creativity, and requires critical analysis of theory in terms of application in the early childhood classroom. Students plan, implement and evaluate activities in music, literature and the visual arts that are consistent with creativity theory.

fields.title: Early Childhood Practicum with Attention to Diversity
fields.description: This practicum provides a setting for observations and experiences in ECED classrooms and in the guiding and teaching of young children including those whose cultures or languages represent diverse family contexts. The accompanying seminar provides opportunities for activities and discussion related to PreK-3 classrooms and accompanying texts.

fields.title: Facilitating Children's Natural and Social Science Constructions
fields.description: Study of the history, content, processes, teaching methods and materials for teaching natural and social sciences in Pre-K to 3rd grade. Focus is on constructivist learning theory, levels of inquiry, and national and state standards as applied to the selection of content, method and learning equivalent.

fields.title: Children and Mathematics in Grades PreK-3
fields.description: This course provides students with the knowledge, skills and understandings to design and implement effective mathematics programs in PreK-3 grades. Focus is on appropriate mathematics content, teaching strategies and curriculum materials from a developmental perspective.

fields.title: Constructivist Curriculum Design and Evaluation
fields.description: Theories and practices in the design, implementation, and evaluation of curriculum for pre-kindergarten and kindergarten through third-grade children are examined with an emphasis on development through play.

fields.title: Early Childhood Practicum with Attention to Special Education
fields.description: This practicum provides a setting for observations and experiences in ECED classrooms and in the guiding and teaching of young children including those with special needs. The accompanying seminar provides opportunities for activities and discussion related to PreK-3 classrooms including those whose abilities require accommodations and adaptations.
fields.prerequisites: ECED 511 .

fields.title: Working with Parents of Young Children
fields.description: Study of the role of the teacher in early childhood education relating to and working with families, school personnel and communities. Methods of involving stakeholders and providing effective communication among groups are emphasized. Resources for supporting parents and engaging the community are examined.
fields.prerequisites: ELED 632 .

fields.title: Reading and Research
fields.description: Directed reading and research in areas of student interest. Reading and research may be done only in the major field of study. A plan of study must be submitted in prescribed form and approved prior to registration for the course.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 630 and written permission of the advisor and coordinator.

fields.title: Student Teaching Internship in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: Student teaching provides a context in which to demonstrate and integrate the skills, knowledge and dispositions that are essential for success as a classroom teacher. Under the guidance of a university supervisor students are expected to reflect on the teaching role as they assume the full responsibilities typical of teachers in grades PreK-3.
fields.prerequisites: ECED 508 , ECED 510 , ECED 511 , ECED 512 , ECED 544 , ECED 609 and ECED 611 ; LED 566 and LED 636 ; ELED 632 .

fields.title: Introduction to an Economic Topic
fields.description: A one-week course offered during winter term or summer that introduces an economic topic/issue that is currently capturing significant interest in today's world.

fields.title: Introduction to Macroeconomics [C4GE]
fields.description: Behavior of systems at the national and international levels. Topics include the methodology of economics as a social science, supply and demand, definition and measurement of important macroeconomic variables, and theoretical models of growth, inflation, interest rates, unemployment, business cycles, stabilization policy, exchange rates and the balance of payments. May be used for general education credit.
fields.prerequisites: Not open to students who are enrolled in or who have received credit for ECON 332 . Maximum of 2 attempts for ECON 200 .

fields.title: Introduction to Microeconomics
fields.description: Topics covered include supply and demand, consumer choice, economics of the firm and industry, production costs, distribution theory, international trade, public policy, comparative economic systems and the philosophy of economics. This course is not open to students who are enrolled in or who have received credit for ECON 331 .
fields.prerequisites: Not open to students who are enrolled in or who have received credit for ECON 331 . Maximum of 2 attempts for ECON 201 .

fields.title: Contemporary Economic Issues and Policy Alternatives
fields.description: Application of elementary economic theory to current economic issues. Special emphasis is placed on public policy alternatives.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: International Economics
fields.description: A survey of the relationships among national economies, including trade theory, trade policy, international monetary relations and the balance of payments.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 . Not open to students who are enrolled in or have already received credit in ECON 370 or ECON 372 .

fields.title: Introduction to Quantitative Analysis in Economics
fields.description: Students will learn key mathematical and statistical concepts used in economics. Topics will include algebra of summation, optimization, probability theory, joint probability distribution, conditional expectations, hypothesis testing and an introduction to data analysis using statistical software. Concepts will be emphasized using economic examples. Does not count as COB 291 for COB 300.
fields.prerequisites: MATH 205 , MATH 231 , MATH 235 or equivalent; and either COB 191 , MATH 220 , MATH 318 or equivalent.

fields.title: Special Topics in Economics
fields.description: Examination of special topics in theoretical or applied economics not covered in the current economics curriculum. Specific topics to be determined by the instructor.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: History of Economic Thought
fields.description: Major contributions within the history of economic thought are studied in relation to both the historical circumstances within which they arose and the role each played in shaping contemporary, competing economic doctrines.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Environmental Economics
fields.description: An analysis of the problems of the environment, their causes and alternative proposed methods of solution. Air and water pollution will be stressed as case studies of environmental problems.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 201 .

fields.title: The Economics of Women and the Family
fields.description: Examines facts and theories pertaining to the various economic roles of women in America. The economics of marriage, divorce and childbearing are examined as are empirical and theoretical explanations of occupational and wage differentials between the sexes.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 201 .

fields.title: Economic History of the United States
fields.description: A survey of the economic growth and development of the United States from Colonial times to the present.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Comparative Economic Systems
fields.description: An examination of the distinguishing characteristics, institutions and performances of the various types of major economic systems in the world today.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Money and Banking
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to examine the economic role of money, banking and monetary policy within current institutional settings and under alternative theories explaining the interrelationships between money, the financial system and economic activity.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Public Finance
fields.description: Introduction to the field of public finance including theories and principles of taxation, government expenditure, public debt, and fiscal administration. Studies interrelationships between federal, state and local finance, shifting and incidence of tax, and the burden of public debt.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Game Theory
fields.description: Examines interdependent decision making in economics and other social sciences, and covers both non-cooperative and cooperative games. Topics may include applications of game theory to industrial organization, law and economics, public choice, political economy, evolutionary biology, international affairs and theories of justice.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Behavioral Economics
fields.description: An introductory course in behavioral economics that combines insights from psychology with economics. Using data from field and lab experiments, we will examine the explanatory power of the standard economic model and learn new frameworks that incorporate psychologically realistic assumptions grounded in observed behavior. Among the topics studied are decision-making under uncertainty, intertemporal choice and others regarding preferences. The course will conclude by examining implications this approach to economic analysis has for public policy.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 201 .

fields.title: Health Economics
fields.description: This course explores the structure, conduct, and performance of hospitals, physician practices, pharmaceutical and medical device manufacturers, and long-term care facilities. The demand for healthcare and insurance is presented using economic theories of risk and uncertainty. Economic evaluation of healthcare treatments and contemporary policies are examined.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Intermediate Microeconomic Theory
fields.description: Intermediate analysis of the determination of price, resource allocation and product distribution in a free enterprise economy.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in the following courses: ECON 200 and ECON 201 ; and either ECON 284 , COB 291 , or MATH 236 .

fields.title: Intermediate Macroeconomic Theory
fields.description: Intermediate-level analysis of the major approaches to the determination of economic aggregates, with emphasis given to structuring a common analytic framework.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in the following courses: ECON 200 and ECON 201 ; and either ECON 284 , COB 291 , or MATH 236 .

fields.title: Economics of Natural Resources
fields.description: Emphasizes availability of exhaustible resources and optimum utilization rates. Examines questions of intertemporal allocation and costs of growth.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Industrial Organization
fields.description: An examination of contemporary U.S. industrial concentration both in the aggregate and within particular industries with emphasis on public policy implications. Alternative theories of the firm are considered in relation to different market structures.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Labor Economics
fields.description: Study of the economics of labor markets. Attention is given to the structure and operation of labor markets, wage determination, employment, unions, and contemporary labor problems and policies.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Economic Development
fields.description: A study of the characteristics of under-development, theories of economic development and the underlying causes for varying standards of living among the world's people. Considerable time will be spent on studying social and cultural factors that influence economic growth and their potential effect on the economic progress of the less-developed countries.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: International Trade and Trade Policies
fields.description: An examination of the classical and modern theories of international trade, the effects of such trade on the domestic economy, the effects of barriers to free trade and an appraisal of U.S. commercial policy since 1948.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: International Finance and Payments
fields.description: Examines international financial markets, instruments and institutions; determination of spot and forward exchange rates, interest arbitrage, hedging and speculation; and alternative policies for achieving equilibrium in international payments.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Urban Economics
fields.description: A detailed examination of the economic aspects of urbanization with emphasis on metropolitan land use and location theory. Urban problems considered include housing, poverty, labor markets and municipal finances.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Mathematical Economics
fields.description: Course will provide basic mathematical tools for microeconomic and macroeconomic analysis. Topics covered include linear algebra, univariate and multivariate differentiation, economic interpretation of the derivatives, constrained and unconstrained optimization, expected utility model, and dynamic analysis of economic models.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in the following courses: ECON 200 and ECON 201 ; and either ECON 284 , COB 291 , or MATH 236 .

fields.title: Econometrics
fields.description: This course covers the application of single- and multi-variable linear regression models to economic outcomes, with emphasis on hypothesis testing, causal effect estimation and data analyses using statistical software.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in the following courses: ECON 200 and ECON 201 ; and either ECON 284 , COB 291 , or MATH 236 .

fields.title: Economics Internship
fields.description: Academic credit for an approved internship experience. Registration for the course must be concurrent with the internship. An application showing how all requirements for the internship will be met must be approved prior to registration. May be taken on a credit/no credit basis only.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Career Preparation in Economics
fields.description: Students participate in a number of activities designed to enhance career preparedness and job search outcomes in economics as approved by the economics program (including attending workshops and registering to be informed of job opportunities).
fields.prerequisites: ECON 331 , ECON 332 , ECON 385 and senior standing.

fields.title: Advanced Topics in Economics
fields.description: Examination of special topics in theoretical or applied economics not covered in the current economics curriculum. Specific topics to be determined by the instructor.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 331 and ECON 332 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Political Economy
fields.description: Evaluation and critique of mainstream and nontraditional economic paradigms. The interaction of economics and politics in the United States as it affects the distribution of wealth and domestic and international economic policies.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 , ECON 201 , and junior or senior standing.

fields.title: Theory of Public Choice
fields.description: Examines the justification for and nature of public sector activity in a market-based mixed economy. Emphasis is placed on theories of market failure, voting models, conditions of production and provision in the public sector, and models of bureaucratic behavior.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 326 or ECON 331 .

fields.title: Experimental Economics
fields.description: This course focuses on using incentivized experiments, whereby subjects make financially-motivated decisions in controlled environments, to identify causality, test and develop theories, and explore behavioral phenomena related to economic issues. Students will study and apply the methods and data analysis tools commonly used in experimental economics to a broad range of economic topics. Established experimental results from previous and current economic research will also be thoroughly examined.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 327 or ECON 331 .

fields.title: Monetary Theory
fields.description: Examines alternative theories of the relationships between money, interest rates, price levels, employment and output in order to assess the effectiveness of monetary policy for economic stabilization.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 332 .

fields.title: Advanced Microeconomic Theory
fields.description: Examines theories of general equilibrium and the distribution of income, welfare economics, capital theory and information theory.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 331 .

fields.title: Advanced Macroeconomics
fields.description: This course studies macroeconomics at an advanced level. Topics covered in this course may include short-run dynamics of an economy, theory of economic fluctuations, models of long-run economic growth, role of fiscal and monetary policies, and comparative macroeconomic analysis of the U.S. and other economies.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 332 .

fields.title: Economic Growth
fields.description: Economic growth is at the heart of economics: improving standards of living in the long run. Students will study models of economic growth, their applications and the empirical evidence across countries. Particular emphasis will be placed on recent advances in the area. Students will apply data analysis methods commonly used in economic growth to a broad range of topics.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 332 .

fields.title: Economics of Regulated Industries
fields.description: A study of the rationale, methods and impact on industry behavior of government regulations including public utility regulation and antitrust policies relating to monopoly and competition in the United States.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 385 or permission of the instructor; and ECON 331 or ECON 345 (to use ECON 345 , students must have permission of the ECON 455 instructor).

fields.title: Regional Economics
fields.description: A study of local and subnational economics viewed as integral parts of a unified system. Emphasis will be given to the basic economic forces associated with regional growth and decline and related public policy considerations.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 200 and ECON 201 .

fields.title: Applied Time Series Analysis
fields.description: This is an advanced level class in Econometrics with an emphasis on time series techniques. This course covers a broad range of time series methods commonly used in research and industry for generating short-term forecasts for important economics and financial variables. Some of the topics covered are time series decomposition methods, smoothing methods, ARIMA, ARCH/GARCH and VAR.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "B-" in ECON 385 .

fields.title: Advanced Econometrics
fields.description: Theory and application of statistical techniques to study empirical relationships among economic variables. This course will cover a range of econometric techniques to estimate economic models including panel data, limited dependent variable, and simultaneous equation models. In addition, the course will cover the assembly and analysis of requisite data sets, and the preparation and presentation of empirical results.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "B-" in ECON 385 .

fields.title: Economic Consulting
fields.description: A research-oriented, senior-level course that provides students an opportunity to integrate theoretical knowledge, quantitative techniques and writing skills through research on a set of simulated consulting projects.
fields.prerequisites: ECON 331 , ECON 332 , ECON 385 and senior standing.

fields.title: Senior Capstone Seminar in Economics
fields.description: This course is a writing-intensive seminar offering a student the opportunity to integrate many of their undergraduate studies in economics. Its substantive content will emphasize applying the methods of theoretical and empirical analyses employed by all economists. The seminar will be structured so as to contain embedded assessment measures of the learning objectives specified by the department of economics, including those related to command of basic economic theory and of quantitative methods used in quantifying empirical relationships and testing hypothesis.
fields.prerequisites: Senior standing and minimum grade of "C" in the following courses: ECON 331 , ECON 332 and ECON 385 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Economics
fields.description: Designed to give capable students in economics an opportunity to complete independent study under faculty supervision. Admission by recommendation of the instructor and written permission of the director of economics prior to registration. May not be used toward fulfillment of the 400-level requirement for a major in economics.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Year course. See catalog section "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: The Study of the Future: An Interdisciplinary Approach
fields.description: Introduces the students to an interdisciplinary study of the future within the context of education. Various topic areas, such as population, science/technology, lifestyle, economics, international relations, energy and religion will be explored in terms of future trends and how education responds to these trends and their impacts.

fields.title: Critical Questions in Education [C1CT]
fields.description: This course provides an overview of the U.S. American public education system. Specific emphasis will be placed on the role, funding and history of education as they relate to social justice, equity and the diversity of U.S. American society. May be used for general education credit.
fields.prerequisites: If you have already completed, or are currently registered for, a Critical Thinking (Madison Foundations) class, then you must secure permission to receive credit for a second Critical Thinking class.

fields.title: Social Foundations of Exceptionalities
fields.description: This course examines the social, cultural, and educational contexts - through the lifespan - of individuals with exceptionalities. Specific focus will be given to the study of historical perspectives, models, theories, philosophies and trends in the field of special education. In addition, the role of culture, environment, family and individual differences will be explored.

fields.title: Learning, Behavior and Engagement in Context [C5SD]
fields.description: This course examines development and sociocultural dynamics, informed by 21st century skills, with a retrospective focus on how past developmental experiences impact present and future learning. Students will apply knowledge and research about human development to identify best practices for learning and resilience. This course may be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Foundations of Education in the United States
fields.description: This course addresses understanding of American education, philosophical approaches to education, the history of education, and the socio-cultural changes in U.S. society with characteristics of today's schools and with current educational issues.

fields.title: Comparative Intercultural Education
fields.description: Students will study and compare educational goals, practices, policies and beliefs in countries and cultures around the world. Content is grounded in social, cultural, historical and economic processes that are influenced and influence cultural understandings and systems of education.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 200 .

fields.title: Foundations of Curriculum and Instruction
fields.description: This is an introductory course that examines the historical, sociological, philosophical, and psychological perspectives that influence and support the curricular and instructional structures of general education. Throughout the course the implementation of those structures through a systematic process of planning for effective classroom instruction and evaluation will be examined. Connections to how they reflect an understanding of various models of learning and cognition and their implications for educational practice will be established.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. SPED majors: EXED 200 .

fields.title: Critical Studies in Education, Race, Culture and Politics
fields.description: This course engages students in critical studies of educational outcomes and practices for minority populations in contemporary and historical contexts.

fields.title: Teaching in a Diverse Society
fields.description: This course will examine how personal and professional values, attitudes, beliefs, and behaviors affect teaching and learning. The pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of similar unique characteristics of Pre-K to 12 grade students and their families, including culture, race, ethnicity, heritage language and learning abilities, gender socialization, and sexual orientation.

fields.title: Instructional Technology
fields.description: In this course, learners will establish a foundational understanding of technology and media as a means to empower pedagogical practice and set conditions for learning. The course is intended to help develop awareness of, and appreciation for, a range of technical skills and reflective practices that may be applied in daily life and in future course work and careers. Learners will create an ePortfolio of digital media developed in this course.

fields.title: Problems in Education
fields.description: Workshop experiences for the development and training of teachers.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 200 .

fields.title: Digging into History and Education at James Madison's Montpelier
fields.description: Students will learn about, reflect on and critique the ways in which systemic racism influences American society, U.S. education systems and their own lives. The course is organized to promote race reflection through critical explorations of the ways race and racism are inscribed within places and spaces. Students will critically engage with course texts and materials, unearth artifacts on an archaeological dig at Montpelier, explore numerous exhibits at Montpelier and other local historic sites in and around Orange County, Virginia, and confront structural racism while planning anti-racist K-12 curriculum.

fields.title: Perspectives in Environmental Education
fields.description: This course illuminates the role of educators in presenting environmental topics in learning communities. Activities will include principles for formal classrooms and other educational settings, such as museums, parks and zoos. In a local classroom /learning environment, participants will collaborate with practicing educators to teach learners about local environmental topics.

fields.title: Undergraduate Teaching Assistantship in Education
fields.description: Undergraduate students in education majors will serve as teaching assistants in large-format education courses. Students will perform essential duties, including facilitating classroom discussions, maintaining accurate class records and assisting the instructor with class lectures.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 200 .

fields.title: Student Teaching
fields.description: Enables students to apply, in the public school classrooms and the comprehensive child development programs, those skills and attitudes acquired in all components of teacher education. Under the guidance of university supervisors, students are provided activities designed to familiarize them with the classroom teacher's role.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 160 and EDUC 200 .

fields.title: Special Topics in Education
fields.description: This course offers an in-depth examination of selected topics which are of current importance in the field of education. This course may be repeated for credit when course content changes.
fields.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing and consent of the instructor.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Independent research topic initiated and completed by qualified upper-division students. See catalog descriptions entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Independent research topic initiated and completed by qualified upper-division students. See catalog descriptions entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Independent research topic initiated and completed by qualified upper-division students. See catalog descriptions entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Workshop in Education
fields.description: Workshop experience relative to the current needs evident in elementary and secondary school programs. No more than six credit hours earned in workshops in education may be applied to a major program in education or no more than three hours may be applied to a minor program in education.

fields.title: Digging into History and  Antiracist Education at James Madison's Montpelier
fields.description: Students will learn about, reflect on and critique the ways in which systemic racism influences American society, U.S. education systems and their own lives. The course is organized to promote race reflection through critical explorations of the ways race and racism are inscribed within places and spaces. Students will critically engage with course texts and materials, unearth artifacts on an archaeological dig at Montpelier, explore numerous exhibits at Montpelier and other local historic sites in and around Orange County, Virginia, and confront structural racism while analyzing, planning and sharing anti-racist K-12 curriculum.

fields.title: Cross Cultural Education
fields.description: The course provides students with knowledge of the effects of socio-cultural variables in an instructional setting.

fields.title: Educational Technology
fields.description: Develops concepts and skills related to educational technology including selecting, producing, evaluating and using traditional forms of media and newer information technologies, including computers and videodiscs, to enhance delivery of instruction.

fields.title: Issues in Education
fields.description: An in-depth study of selected issues related to working with individuals in diverse learning communities such as industry, community colleges, prek-12 classroom and other educational contexts.

fields.title: Changing Contexts of American Schools
fields.description: This course focuses on the nature of educational change in American schooling. Emphasis will be placed upon contemporary issues facing education, their historical and philosophical roots and the implementation of educational change.

fields.title: Evaluation in Education
fields.description: The course is designed to help practicing educators improve their development and use of assessment tools and techniques. Attention will also be given to analyzing and interpreting assessment results and investigating newer developments in the evaluation of learning and instructional programs.

fields.title: Inquiry in Education
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to help students develop skills, insights and understanding that will enable them to become intelligent and critical consumers of educational inquiry and productive participants in the inquiry process.
fields.prerequisites: Learning design and technology students: LDT 610 .

fields.title: Seminar in Educational Inquiry
fields.description: Studies of topics related to educational inquiry. Emphasis on inquiry designs and skills specific to students' areas of inquiry interests.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 630 .

fields.title: Seminar in Inquiry
fields.description: This seminar will allow graduate students to discuss their learning environment based inquiry projects. They will problem solve issues that arise in the implementation of their projects as well as analyze data and draw appropriate conclusions from their findings. From those conclusions, they will generate implications for and connections to their reading.

fields.title: Learning Theories and Practice
fields.description: This course focuses on the theories and research that guide the understanding of diverse learners, processes of learning and development, the role of the teacher, the design and delivery of instruction, the processes and strategies of teaching, and research-based decision-making.

fields.title: Curriculum Theory and Issues
fields.description: Curriculum theory and issues focus on the historical, philosophical, sociological and political perspectives involved with decisions about teaching and learning. Reflection on purposes, content, design and assessment of educational programs form the core of curriculum studies.

fields.title: Cultural Immersion Practicum
fields.description: This graduate-level course explores the global, cultural and community forces that shape educational systems and informal learning environments. Designed for educators and leaders, the practicum fosters cultural humility and global competence through immersive engagement in diverse sociocultural contexts. Students critically examine how identity, power and systemic structures (political, economic, historical, socio-cultural, environmental) influence educational experiences across settings. Learning agreements, co-developed with instructors, guide individualized pathways through preparatory materials and in-country activities such as homestays, school visits, community service and site-based learning. Through reflective practice and scholarly inquiry, students synthesize their experiences into meaningful academic products that demonstrate personal growth and professional relevance. Students may earn a maximum of six credits for this course.

fields.title: Reading and Research
fields.description: Opportunities for directed reading and research in areas of special interest. Reading and research may be done only in the major field of study.
fields.prerequisites: EDUC 630 and written permission of the advisor and coordinator.

fields.title: Internship in Education
fields.description: This internship provides a context in which to demonstrate and integrate the skills, knowledge and dispositions that are essential for success as an educator in prek-12, community college, industry, business or other learning environments. Participants will experience the full range of conditions and tasks expected of an educator and are expected to develop and demonstrate competencies in teaching with the supervision and support of an experienced educator or trainer.

fields.title: Comprehensive Continuance
fields.description: Continued preparation in anticipation of the comprehensive examination. Course may be repeated as needed.

fields.title: Thesis Research
fields.description: This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.

fields.title: Introduction to Global Education
fields.description: This course is an introduction to global issues shaping education policy and practice around the world. Students are invited to examine their own identities and actions and their implications for global issues at the local and transnational levels. Course readings, co-curricular activities and instruction are designed to promote an attainable global perspective in order to support the development of global competencies in future course taking and educational praxis. A portfolio of Global Education assignments, essays and curriculum materials will be established.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED Global Concentraiton.

fields.title: Child Development: Birth Through Adolescence
fields.description: Skills for observing, recording and interpreting the behavior of children ages three through 12 will be developed so that adult intervention and guidance is appropriate and meaningful.

fields.title: Global Diversity in Elementary Education
fields.description: This course will examine how personal and professional values, attitudes, beliefs and behaviors affect teaching and learning. The pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of unique characteristics of Pre-K to 12th grade students and their families, including culture, race, ethnicity, heritage, language, learning abilities, gender socialization and sexual orientation. In this globalized version of the course, students will also develop global competencies by examining local and global issues, engaging in open and critical conversations with oneself and others, and acting for collective well-being and sustainable development. The course integrates the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) to foster a deeper understanding of global challenges and their relevance to elementary education.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration and ELED 200 . Corequisite: ELED 272 and ELED 278 .

fields.title: Practicum in Early and Elementary Education
fields.description: Field experiences in grades PK-6 will provide for extensive observation and experience with learners in elementary classrooms and the opportunity to assist teachers in daily activities. Through direct observation and interactions with children in classroom settings, candidates will examine and reflect on how children develop and learn, exploring their own personal attitudes, assumptions and behaviors towards students and their families are influenced by class, cultural and linguistic backgrounds.

fields.title: Introduction to Early and Elementary Education
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce elementary education students to teaching children in grades PK-6. Based on developmental and learning theories, the course focuses on building relationships with and among learners, establishing learning environments, guiding behavior, and providing instruction and assessment. Through observations and participation in practicum, seminars, workshops and lectures, students will construct an understanding of how teachers meet the developmental and learning needs of children by planning, implementing and assessing appropriate curriculum and instruction.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major: Teacher Ed flag 01.
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: ELED 208 and ELED 310 , or ELED 270 and ELED 278 .

fields.title: Child Development in a Global Context: Birth Through Adolescence
fields.description: This course introduces a lifespan approach to human growth and development with emphasis on the social, physical, emotional and cognitive domains. Students will examine key theories, educational philosophies and research methods in the social sciences and child development. They will also develop skills for observing, recording and interpreting children's behavior to apply appropriate and meaningful guidance. In addition, the course emphasizes the professional development of future educators by fostering reflective and culturally responsive practice. Global perspectives are integrated throughout the course, encouraging students to consider cultural diversity, environmental sustainability and global interconnectedness in their understanding of children's growth and learning. Students will also connect local classroom practices to broaden global citizenship values and strengthen cross-cultural competence as part of their preparation for teaching in diverse contexts.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration and ELED 200 .

fields.title: Diversity in Elementary Education
fields.description: This course will examine how personal and professional values, attitudes, beliefs and behaviors affect teaching and learning. The pre-service teachers will develop an understanding of unique characteristics of Pre-K to 12th grade students and their families, including culture, race, ethnicity, heritage, language, learning abilities, gender socialization and sexual orientation.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major.

fields.title: Practicum with a Focus on Learners and Learning
fields.description: This field experience, taken in the fall of junior year, provides candidates with a classroom of students and a mentor teacher with whom to practice building relationships with learners and conduct extensive observations of learners and learning, as well as practice the teaching of content related to their concurrent methods courses (either language arts, mathematics and science OR language arts, mathematics and social studies) with small groups of students. Accompanying monthly seminars will focus on reflecting on themes and experiences in the field and making content connections to methods courses.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major; Teacher Ed flag 02. ELED majors: ELED 272 .
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: ELED 332 and ELED 333 , or ELED 372 and ELED 373 .

fields.title: Practicum with a Focus on Curriculum Integration and Guiding Behavior
fields.description: This field experience, taken in the spring of junior year, provides candidates with a classroom of students and a mentor teacher with whom to practice the teaching of content related to their concurrent methods courses (either language arts, mathematics and science OR language arts, mathematics and social studies) with small groups of students as well as in full class contexts. The accompanying monthly seminar explores the integration and construction of meaningful curriculum in elementary education contexts and in classroom management as well as reflection along with field-based partners.
fields.prerequisites: Accepted to teacher education.

fields.title: Children and Science
fields.description: This course is a study of content, processes, pedagogy and materials for teaching science in the elementary classroom. Knowledge of cognitive development as applied to the selection of content and methodology for elementary learners will be examined.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 272 .
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: ELED 321 , ELED 333 and LED 300 .

fields.title: Children and Mathematics I
fields.description: The first of two courses that provides students with knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. This course will focus on mathematical instruction connected the following mathematical strands: Number and number sense, computation and estimation, and patterns, functions and algebra.
fields.prerequisites: ELED 272 .

fields.title: Children and Social Studies
fields.description: This course focuses on the content, processes, pedagogy and materials for teaching social studies in the elementary classroom. Knowledge of cognitive development as applied to the selection of content, methods, materials and strategies for organizing the learning environment for elementary learners will be examined.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 321 and LED 300 .
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: ELED 322 , ELED 343 and LED 350 .

fields.title: Children and Mathematics II
fields.description: This is the second course in a series providing students with knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning about geometry, measurement, data analysis and probability.
fields.prerequisites: ELED 321 and LED 300 .
fields.corequisites: ELED 322 ; ELED 334 and LED 350 , or ELED 374 , ELED 375 and LED 370 .

fields.title: Children and Science in a Global Context
fields.description: This course is a study of content, processes, pedagogy and materials for teaching science in the elementary classroom. Knowledge of cognitive development as applied to the selection of content and methodology for elementary learners will be examined. Students explore methods for fostering scientific literacy within a global context, emphasizing interconnected challenges such as sustainability and public health. The course also examines diverse cultural perspectives on scientific knowledge and practices to create more inclusive classrooms.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration and ELED 272 .

fields.title: Children and Mathematics I in a Global Context
fields.description: This is the first of two courses that provides students with knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. This course will focus on mathematical instruction connected to the following mathematical strands: number and number sense, computation and estimation, and patterns, functions and algebra. In this globalized version of the course, students will also develop global competencies by examining how mathematics is taught differently around the world, and engaging in open and critical conversations with oneself and others to foster a deeper understanding of different mathematical strategies and how to teach them.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration and ELED 272 .

fields.title: Children and Social Studies in a Global Context
fields.description: This course focuses on the content, processes, pedagogy and materials for teaching globally-aware social studies in the elementary classroom. Knowledge of cognitive development as applied to the selection of inclusive and global content, culturally sustaining methods, materials, and strategies for organizing the learning environment for elementary learners will be examined.
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration, ELED 321 and LED 300 .

fields.title: Seminar in Global Education Praxis I
fields.description: In this course students will explore the needs and challenges of elementary school learners and reflect on what they've learned about teaching young children in a global context. Throughout the semester, students will be prompted to reflect on their experiences with teaching in a global context. Reflections will focus on understanding the complexities inherent in teaching as well as their own personal beliefs, strengths and areas for growth. Students will revisit and expand upon the portfolio begun in ELED 200 .
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration, ELED 321 and LED 300 .

fields.title: Elementary Education Final Practicum
fields.description: Upon completion of this course, teacher candidates will be able to build upon the unique strengths and contributions of K-6 students in order to create and teach lessons in various subject areas as well as reflect on that process.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 322 and ELED 343 .

fields.title: Children and Mathematics: Number, Operations, Algebraic and Geometric Reasoning
fields.description: The first of two courses that provides students with knowledge, skills and understanding of design and implementation for effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning and pre-numerical stages through the acquisition of advanced numerical processes and operations and connections to geometric and algebraic reasoning.
fields.prerequisites: MATH 107 , MATH 108 , MATH 207 and LED 366 .

fields.title: Mathematics Content and Pedagogy for Elementary Education I
fields.description: This is the first of two courses that helps prospective elementary education teachers (PreK-6) develop mathematical content and pedagogical knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning in the following mathematical strands: number and number sense, computation and estimation, and patterns, functions and algebra.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag).

fields.title: Mathematics Content and Pedagogy for Elementary Education II
fields.description: This is the second of two courses that helps prospective elementary teachers (PreK-6) develop mathematical content and pedagogical knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning of geometry, measurement, data analysis and probability.
fields.prerequisites: Applied to Teacher Education (01 Flag); ELED 444 .

fields.title: Planning Instruction and Assessment
fields.description: Elementary education teacher candidates will learn the process of planning, implementing curriculum and using instructional strategies and assessments that promote and monitor students' understanding of content beyond memorization. Students will design units of instruction that utilize evidence-based practices for active engagement strategies, specifically for providing an inclusive environment for a diverse student population. Students will gain the knowledge and skills necessary to use assessments that allow for data-driven instructional decisions and inform subsequent teaching and learning.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 322 and ELED 343 .

fields.title: Home, School, Communities
fields.description: Study of the role of the teacher in relating to and working with families, school personnel and communities. Methods of involving stakeholders and providing effective communication among groups are emphasized. Resources for supporting parents and engaging community stakeholders are examined.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 450 .
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: LED 462 , or ELED 475 and LED 473 .

fields.title: Seminar in Global Education Praxis II
fields.description: In this course, students will explore challenges and opportunities in developing a globally focused praxis for teaching content and skills to diverse elementary school learners. Students will integrate learning in teaching placements with content from education courses taken in the ELED major. Throughout the semester, students will be prompted to reflect on their experiences with teaching in a global context. Reflections will focus on understanding the complexities of planning curricula that expand students' worldviews and promote critical global citizenship. Students will revisit and expand upon the portfolio begun in ELED 200 and expanded in ELED 375 .
fields.prerequisites: Declared ELED global concentration and ELED 450 .

fields.title: Student Teaching in Elementary Education
fields.description: This internship provides a context in which to demonstrate and integrate the skills, knowledge and dispositions that are essential for success as an elementary classroom teacher. Under the guidance of a university supervisor, students are expected to reflect on the teaching role as they assume the full responsibilities of a teacher in grades PreK-6. Students majoring in elementary education must complete this course twice for a total of 16 credit hours.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major; Teacher Ed flag 03. ELED majors: ELED 322 and ELED 343 .

fields.title: Guiding Student Behavior: Responsive Classroom Management
fields.description: This course presents an overview to classroom management for the early childhood and elementary classroom teacher. It includes an historical look at the guidance tradition, a review of traditional approaches to classroom management and a focus away from punishment toward proactive strategies. Best practices in classroom management will be presented from an inclusive perspective for teachers of all children.
fields.prerequisites: ELED or B.I.S./ELED major. ELED majors: ELED 322 and ELED 343 .
fields.corequisites: ELED majors: ELED 450 . Also open to B.I.S./ELED majors.

fields.title: Special Studies in Elementary Education
fields.description: Designed to give students opportunities to complete independent research on educational problems under faculty guidance. The plan for the study must be presented to the department head in prescribed form for approval prior to registration.
fields.prerequisites: Accepted to teacher education.

fields.title: Special Topics in Elementary Education
fields.description: This course is designed to allow elementary education teacher candidates to explore issues in education that particularly interest them. Special topics will be designed by faculty that reflect current issues and problems in education. Students will choose the topic that meets their needs.

fields.title: Creativity and the Arts in Elementary Education
fields.description: This course examines theories related to the development of creativity and their application to classroom instruction. In addition students will study and practice ways to integrate a wide variety of expressive arts (music, poetry, painting, drama, dance, etc.) into the elementary education curriculum.

fields.title: Children and Mathematics II:  Data, Chance, and Space
fields.description: The second of two courses that provides students with knowledge, skills, and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for grades PreK-6. Emphasis is on children's mathematical learning about geometry, measurement, data analysis and probability.

fields.title: Planning, Instruction and Assessment in the Elementary Education Curriculum
fields.description: Elementary education teacher candidates will learn processes of planning, implementing curriculum, and using instructional strategies and assessments that promote and monitor students' understanding of content beyond memorization. Students will design units of instruction utilizing active engagement strategies for an inclusive environment of diverse students. Students will gain knowledge and skills necessary to use assessments to inform instructional decision-making.

fields.title: Practicum with A Focus On Inquiry
fields.description: This field experience encourages candidates' construction of knowledge through the design and implementation of formal inquiry regarding practices in elementary education. The implementation and refinement of teaching practices essential for creative, child-centered, content-rich and culturally sensitive teaching will be examined throughout the practicum and accompanying seminar.

fields.title: Seminar in Inquiry
fields.description: This seminar will allow graduate students to discuss the efforts of their inquiry projects. They will problem solve issues that arise in the implementation of their projects as well as analyze data and draw appropriate conclusions from their findings. From those conclusions, they will generate implications for and connections to their teaching.

fields.title: Inquiry in Elementary Education
fields.description: Focus on inquiry as the basis for learning, philosophical foundations of qualitative and naturalistic methodology and instruction in the use of qualitative methods in the study of education and to inform practice.

fields.title: Seminar in Education Inquiry
fields.description: Focus on the application of education inquiry and its application to teaching.
fields.prerequisites: ELED 632 .

fields.title: Families, Schools and Communities
fields.description: Study of the role of the teacher in relating to and working with families, school personnel, and communities. Methods of involving stakeholders and providing effective communication among groups are emphasized. Resources for supporting parents and engaging community stakeholders are examined.

fields.title: Internship in Teaching
fields.description: This internship provides a context in which to demonstrate and integrate the skills, knowledge and dispositions that are essential for success as an elementary classroom teacher. Under the guidance of a university supervisor students are expected to reflect on the teaching role as they assume the full responsibilities of teacher in grade PreK-6.

fields.title: First Year Engineering Seminar
fields.description: This seminar course introduces the engineering curriculum and career options to first-year students and describes how various elements of the curriculum and available electives relate to the goals and objectives of the program. This course also contextualizes the engineering profession with practical examples to help students develop strategies for success. The activities in the course are aimed at assisting students in successfully making the transition from high school to college.

fields.title: Engineering Skills and Decisions
fields.description: This project-based course equips first-year engineering students with fundamental skills needed to solve engineering problems. The course emphasizes processes associated with making evidence-based decisions in engineering fields. This course covers the following topics: processes of decision making, engineering documentation, data analysis, visualization and engineering orthographic drawing. Students are permitted a maximum of two attempts for this course in consideration for full admission to the Engineering major (excluding final letter grades of W, WP, and WF).
fields.prerequisites: Students are permitted a maximum of two attempts in ENGR 112 (excluding grades of W, WP and WF).

fields.title: Statics and Introductory Solid Mechanics
fields.description: This course introduces the fundamental and governing principles of systems of forces acting on rigid bodies, beams and columns as well as the analysis of truss, frame and machine structures. Topics include external and internal equilibrium of rigid bodies; systems of force and moment vectors; centroids; friction; loading that results in uniaxial, shear, flexure and torsion stresses and strains; and strength of materials. ENGR 212 and ENGR 212L must be taken concurrently.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the Engineering major, MATH 236 , PHYS 240 and a minimum grade of "C-" in ENGR 112 .

fields.title: Statics and Introductory Solid Mechanics Laboratory
fields.description: This laboratory course is designed to complement and supplement ENGR 212 course topics with experiential learning through experiments, projects and in-depth problem solving. ENGR 212 and ENGR 212L must be taken concurrently.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the Engineering major, MATH 236 , PHYS 240 and a minimum grade of "C-" in ENGR 112 .

fields.title: Engineering Project Management
fields.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of project management. Students will identify project requirements, develop a work breakdown structure and network diagram, and apply resources to develop a project schedule.
