fields.description: This lecture series class is geared toward an open forum for students to interact and discuss issues related to hospitality leadership and innovation. The course consists of one hour of lecture or discussion per week, with opportunities to interact with professionals outside of class.

fields.title: Overview of Hospitality and Tourism Management
fields.description: This course exposes students to the areas of lodging, food and beverage, tourism and entertainment management, special events and meeting planning, and club and resort management. Emphasis is on hospitality industry scope, organization and economic impact; includes familiarization with industry terminology and individual and business contributors to the field of hospitality and tourism management.
fields.prerequisites: Hospitality Management major or permission of the program director.

fields.title: Foundations of Leadership of Hospitality Management
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to leadership in Hospitality Management and the Mega Industry. The primary focus will be leadership theory and skill application with a focus on personal awareness.
fields.prerequisites: Hospitality Management major or permission of the program director.

fields.title: Foundations of Hospitality, Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: An introduction to the basis for the professions that make up the School of Hospitality, Sport and Recreation Management. A focus on these professions in governmental, voluntary, private and commercial settings is incorporated. Both the economical significance and the professional preparation for success in the industry is both introduced and practiced.

fields.title: Foundations of Ethics and Law in Hospitality, Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: An introduction to ethics and law within the sport, hospitality and recreation industry. The ethical portion introduces students to select theories of ethics, ethical issues and an ethical decision-making model. The legal portion introduces students to basic legal terminology and concepts while concentrating on negligence and employment issues.

fields.title: Tourism in a Global Context
fields.description: This course examines tourism as a global industry and human activity that promotes and facilitates understanding of historical and cultural values, and of international institutions that characterize the broader global system.

fields.title: Special Event Management: Le Gourmet
fields.description: This course is designed to provide students with a practical hands-on application of event planning for non-profit fundraising. In this course students will actively plan and execute the Hart School's major annual fundraising event, Le Gourmet.

fields.title: Hospitality Professional Work Experience
fields.description: This applied hospitality course consists of experiential exercises followed by class discussion and actual work experience as an employee within the hospitality field. Role-playing and cases are used as learning activities where the instructor acts as a facilitator to learning. Debriefing is used extensively as a way of creating essential theory. Students must successfully complete ServSafe Food Protection Manager Certification and Training for Intervention Procedures (TIPS). Students complete approximately 100 hours of hospitality-related practical experience.
fields.prerequisites: Hospitality Management major or permission of the program director.

fields.title: Disney Internship
fields.description: The paid, semester-long internship program allows students to live just outside Walt Disney World Resort in Florida or the Disneyland Resort in California while earning college credit at Disney parks and resorts through a combination of on-the-job experience, shadowing and seminars.
fields.prerequisites: Permission of the hospitality management program director.

fields.title: Cost Control and Budgeting
fields.description: Introduction to cost control, budgeting and financial analysis as it relates to the hospitality industry. Students work as a team to create a detailed business plan using MS Excel.
fields.prerequisites: Hospitality Management major or permission of the program director.

fields.title: Culinary Arts and Menu Management
fields.description: This course covers application of basic food preparation and menu development. The focus is on preparing students to understand gastronomy and communicate with culinary professionals. This course includes the development of effective menus, plate presentation, preparation methods, flavor development and food service trends. Lab fee applies. Uniform required.
fields.prerequisites: HM 222 or permission of program director.

fields.title: Hospitality Data Analytics
fields.description: This course introduces students to the fundamental concepts and practical applications of data in the hospitality industry. Students will explore how data is generated, structured and interpreted, with a focus on deriving meaningful insights for decision-making in hospitality management. Core topics include data literacy, essential analytical techniques and an introduction to artificial intelligence fundamentals. By the end of the course, students will gain the knowledge and skills needed to confidently apply data-driven approaches across other hospitality management courses and professional settings.

fields.title: Special Studies in Hospitality Management
fields.description: A special studies course designed to explore areas of current topical concern in the lodging, food and beverage, travel and tourism, and entertainment industries. May be used for general education credit. Course content will vary.
fields.prerequisites: Hospitality Management major or permission of the program director.

fields.title: Practical Work Experience
fields.description: Required 600 hours of approved hospitality and tourism work experience. Credit/no credit only. All work sites must be approved.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum of 45 credit hours complete, HM 201 , HM 203 , HM 111 and HM 222 .

fields.title: Country Club Management
fields.description: This course is an application of business concepts to the private equity club and full-service resort industry. Industry cases are used to facilitate discussion of similarities and differences among private equity clubs, full service resorts and other hospitality business in the areas of culture, asset management and operations.
fields.prerequisites: Junior standing

fields.title: Introduction to Event Management
fields.description: This course is designed to explore conferences, conventions, expositions, meetings and special events as they relate to the responsibilities of a planner, selection criteria for host venues, legal and ethical issues, negotiating process, program design, budgeting, contracts, marketing, logistics and evaluation. Practical hands-on experience through projects may occur.

fields.title: Lodging, Clubs and Resort Operations and Technology
fields.description: This course offers an in-depth look at full-service hotels, clubs and resorts through the eyes of a general manager. The course will focus on operations, engineering, housekeeping, uniformed services, front office, reservations and revenue management. Different hospitality technology platforms and software programs will be used to expose students to hospitality technology.

fields.title: Internship in Hospitality Management
fields.description: Students will complete 200 hours of approved hospitality work experience. CR/NC only. All worksites must be pre-approved. In addition, students must validate 600 hours of professional work experience in the services industry as a prerequisite to this course.
fields.prerequisites: HM 222 and HM 251 and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Italian Culture and Wine
fields.description: An introduction to the fundamentals of wine making, wine tasting and glossary of terms provide a framework for visual, olfactory and gustative analysis. The historical value of wine, together with its cultural, economic and social meaning in Italy, are explored. Course taught in Florence, Italy. Lab fee applies. Student must be enrolled in JMU in Florence Program.

fields.title: Italian Gastronomy
fields.description: This course is designed to teach students the applied approach to match wine and food from different parts of the world using flavors, textures and components present in food and wine in complementing strategies. Emphasis will be placed on menu planning, cooking methods and tasting wines with food in a formal dining room. Course offered in Florence, Italy. Lab fee applies. Student must be enrolled in JMU in Florence Program.

fields.title: Profit Optimization and Revenue Management
fields.description: In this course, students will apply and analyze data to effectively manage rates and capacity applied in many service industries, including hospitality. The focus of this course is to help students learn how to apply revenue management principles to maximize profitability in lodging, clubs, and the food and beverage sectors.
fields.prerequisites: HM 321 and HM 322 .

fields.title: Hospitality Law
fields.description: The course focuses on the application of the law to the hospitality industry including rights and obligations of guests and lodging, food service, club, event management and association operators. The identification of potential legal problems and formulation of preventive measures to limit/prevent liability are emphasized.
fields.prerequisites: HM 111 and junior standing.

fields.title: Beverage Management and Marketing
fields.description: The course is designed to enhance knowledge in the identification and evaluation of beverages typically served in hospitality establishments. Special attention is given to alcoholic and non-alcoholic beverages with regard to price/quality relationships; channels of distribution and marketing; trends and current issues faced by the industry; and service ethics.
fields.prerequisites: Must be 21 years of age or older and declared HM major, HM 444 or permission of director.

fields.title: Advanced Event Management
fields.description: This course examines event planning and management within a project management framework. The course is designed to provide hands-on experience in event planning. Students will work to plan and execute an event from start to finish with instructor oversight. Students will demonstrate, by executing an event, the core competencies required of a successful event manager.
fields.prerequisites: HM 321 , HM 322 , HM 371 and permission of the instructor or director.

fields.title: Napa and Sonoma Wine and Culture
fields.description: Napa and Sonoma are the premier wine growing regions in the United States. The wines influence wines across the US and around the world. The ability to impressively learn about the wine, food, and culture that influence the region can only be fully accomplished by visiting. Students are able to visit wineries and speak with owners, visit growers and speak with the farmers, visit nurseries and discuss varietals.
fields.prerequisites: HM Major, 21 years old the first day of class and permission of the director.

fields.title: Hospitality Ethics
fields.description: Ethical issues and actions that have occurred, or are currently occurring, in the hospitality industry are examined from multiple perspectives. Examining recent scandals, real-world scenarios, news stories and common ethical dilemmas will enable a student to recognize an ethical dilemma, understand the components of the dilemma and make an ethical decision.
fields.prerequisites: HM 111 and junior standing.

fields.title: Hospitality Human Resources Management
fields.description: This course examines the identification and exploration of the information needs of the hospitality manager in making policy and personnel decisions. Different philosophies and processes for locating, attracting, hiring and training a qualified staff are examined. Emphasis is placed on the work environment within the service industry. Employment law will be emphasized as a part of the course.
fields.prerequisites: HM 321 , HM 322 and HM 333 ; or permission of the director.

fields.title: Hospitality Seminar
fields.description: This senior capstone course is designed to assist in transitioning from being a university student to holding a leadership role within the hospitality industry. The interactive course draws upon the umbrella curricular goals of the hospitality management program in communication, ethics, finance and leadership. Senior assessment may also occur.

fields.title: Supervisory Hospitality Internship
fields.description: Students will complete 200 hours of approved hospitality supervisory experience. All work sites must be pre-approved.
fields.prerequisites: Senior standing and HM 333 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Hospitality and Tourism Management
fields.description: Designed to give capable students in hospitality and tourism management an opportunity to complete independent study under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Special Topics in Hospitality and Tourism Management
fields.description: This course is designed to allow explorations of areas of current topical concern, or to exploit special situations. Course content will vary. For current course content, consult the advisor.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Year course. See catalog section "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Human Resource Development Leadership Lab
fields.description: Hands-on practicum of leadership strategies and techniques designed to give each student a better appreciation for the dynamics of leadership in intimate, physically challenging and stressful environments, both indoors and out. Students operate in teams which are formed and reorganized on a continuous basis, surrounded by peers at several levels of leadership experience and training. Collaborative learning is enhanced when students apply what they learn in class by describing relevant lessons learned though experiences outside the classroom. The focus of this course is to provide students with the opportunity to lead and follow in an observed setting and receive constant feedback and mentoring on their demonstrated leadership skills. Students learn though leading as well as through a critical reflection, inquiry, dialogue and group interaction. Everyone is responsible for contributing to the learning process.

fields.title: Introduction to Leadership
fields.description: An introduction to: various leadership styles and their effect on organizations; insight into the leaders' roles and responsibilities within the context of the organization; character- and values-based leadership; basic leadership actions; the importance of self improvement in the areas of time management, health and fitness, goal setting, academic accomplishment and communications; group dynamics, and the development of interpersonal skills.

fields.title: Developing Multicultural Competency for Effective Facilitation
fields.description: This course will provide students with a deeper understanding of social identities, and they will gain the necessary skills to facilitate training, programs and dialogues focusing on areas of diversity, multiculturalism, inclusion and access. Students enrolled in this course will be prepared to become a diversity educator in the Diversity Education Empowerment Program sponsored by the Center for Multicultural Student Services at James Madison University.

fields.title: Introduction to Workplace Learning
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to cover the emergence and advancement of the field of human resource development and provide essential skills for the process of planning, implementing and evaluating workplace learning.
fields.prerequisites: Must be declared as an Individualized Study major.

fields.title: Leadership Styles Theory and Application
fields.description: Explores the dimensions of creative and innovative leadership strategies and styles by examining team dynamics and two historical leadership theories that form the basis of the leadership framework (train and behavior theories). Students practice aspects of personal motivation and team building in the context of planning, executing and assessing team exercises and participating in leadership skills labs. Focus is on continued development of the knowledge of leadership values and attributes through an understanding of institutional structures, duties and responsibilities of organizational/institutional leaders, and leadership in small organizations. Case studies provide tangible context for learning leadership skills, values, actions and attributes as they apply to a contemporary setting.
fields.prerequisites: HRD 100 and HRD 101 .

fields.title: Introduction to Human Resource Development
fields.description: An introduction to the role and scope of human resource development with particular emphasis on required competencies for HRD professionals. Critical moral and ethical issues are introduced.

fields.title: Leadership in Organizational Settings
fields.description: An examination of the principles of leadership and their application within organizational settings. Emphasis will be placed on the critical appraisal of the facets of leadership through the use of cases and readings.

fields.title: Leadership in the Workplace
fields.description: Leadership, motivation and management: how do they relate to workplace learning? This course explores such themes and examines various leadership theories. In addition, learners will develop an understanding of the competencies and skills needed to succeed in a leadership role in HRD.
fields.prerequisites: Must be declared as an Individualized Study major.

fields.title: Designing Workplace Learning
fields.description: Through authentic workplace scenarios and case studies, adult learners will analyze jobs and tasks to identify performance gaps or improvement needs. Applying systems thinking, students will design and develop effective HRD solutions, such as detailed performance improvement plans or targeted training programs, tailored to address specific workplace challenges. This course empowers learners to make strategic HRD recommendations that enhance workforce effectiveness and align with organizational objectives.
fields.prerequisites: Must be declared as an Individualized Study major.

fields.title: Performance and Task Analysis in Human Resource Development
fields.description: Provides the basic skill level for students in the area of performance analysis and subsequent assessment. Particular emphasis is placed on actual analysis and assessment situations with application to program and curricular design.
fields.prerequisites: Declared HRD minor or Adult Degree Program students and HRD 240 , HRD 245 and LDT 370 .

fields.title: Human Resource Development Internship
fields.description: A structured internship experience designed to provide students with the opportunity to contribute within an actual work setting the role and scope of human resource development efforts. Minimum 400-hour experience approved by the program coordinator. The minor does not provide internships.

fields.title: Learning in the Workplace
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to develop adult learners by focusing on adult learning theories, cognitive and noncognitive learning processes, and diverse cultures and systems of knowing and learning in the workplace.
fields.prerequisites: Must be declared as an Individualized Study major.

fields.title: Seminar in Leadership
fields.description: Designed to provide senior-level students with the opportunity to face some of the dilemmas of leadership. Students will be encouraged to critically examine leaders and organizations to draw from real events the ambiguities of leadership. Course will involve extensive reading, case work and a range of guest speakers.
fields.prerequisites: HRD 245 .

fields.title: Learning in Adulthood
fields.description: This course is a study of the learning processes of the adult learner with an emphasis on adaptations of the instructional process to accommodate the differences inherent in the adult learning environment. Practical applications to actual adult learning situations are included.
fields.prerequisites: Declared HRD minor or Adult Degree Program student; and LDT 370 .

fields.title: Development of Materials and Programs
fields.description: This course is designed to provide students with the basic skills necessary to design and develop performance-based training programs and courses. Emphasis will be placed on the actual design and development of training materials while working with an actual client.
fields.prerequisites: Declared HRD minor or Adult Degree Program student; and LDT 370 and HRD 380 .

fields.title: Introduction to Humanitarian Affairs
fields.description: A geographical overview of poverty, armed conflict, hunger, disease, and natural disasters and how they can lead to humanitarian crises. It includes a study of human rights along with a look at international efforts to address, and international organizations that deal with, humanitarian crises.

fields.title: Introduction to Natural Disasters Response
fields.description: This course is designed to give students an overview of the various types of natural disasters; a look at the world regions that are most vulnerable to each type of disaster; and, a preview of disaster planning, management, relief and response as related to natural disasters.

fields.title: Legal Issues in Humanitarian Affairs
fields.description: This course prepares students interested in humanitarian response with basic information on the legal issues of humanitarian law. It covers principles of domestic and international law relevant to the practice of humanitarian response, including international humanitarian law, the law of armed conflict, international human rights law, international criminal law and other legal topics relevant to humanitarian affairs practitioners.
fields.prerequisites: Junior standing.

fields.title: Human Rights in Theory and Practice
fields.description: This course will explore the nature and value of human rights by investigating some major debates over their status and meaning, and by examining some of the ways people have tried to secure human rights in practice.
fields.prerequisites: Humanitarian Affairs minors only.

fields.title: Special Topics in Humanitarian Affairs
fields.description: Focused, in-depth study of specific areas or subjects related to Humanitarian Affairs. Topics will provide background and skills important for humanitarian work. Can be repeated as course content changes.

fields.title: GIS for Humanitarian Assistance
fields.description: In responding to humanitarian crises, governments and aid organizations must deploy aid workers, deliver essential services, set up temporary settlements, and distribute items such as water and food that are needed for survival. Spatial analysis and maps are critical to the success of these efforts. In this course, students learn the basics of Geographic Information Systems (GIS) for humanitarian assistance and learn how relief organizations use GIS in their work.
fields.prerequisites: GEOG 215 .

fields.title: Humanitarian Affairs Field Experience
fields.description: The HUMN 490 course offers students an opportunity to gain experience and practical skills, preferably in an "international setting," either in the U.S. or abroad, and to apply knowledge and skills acquired through the Humanitarian Affairs program. This course must be completed in a setting approved by the student's advisor and the humanitarian affairs minor committee.
fields.prerequisites: HUMN 201 and junior status.

fields.title: Great Works [C2L]
fields.description: An intensive examination of great literary works that focus on key issues of knowledge and reality, meaning and purpose, ethics, and aesthetics. Discussion, analysis and intensive writing are required. Texts will vary by section and instructor. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Great Works - London [C2L]
fields.description: An intensive examination of great literary works that focus on key issues of knowledge and reality, meaning and purpose, ethics, and aesthetics. Discussion, analysis and intensive writing are required. Texts will vary by section and instructor. Course is taught in London as part of Study Abroad Program. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Foundations of Western Culture [C2HQC]
fields.description: This course is a study of the roots of our Western tradition in Greek, Roman, Medieval or Renaissance culture. Students examine the interrelationships among history and literary works; the fine arts; philosophical and religious thought and intellectual contexts. Content will vary depending on section and instructor. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Modern Perspectives [C2HQC]
fields.description: An interdisciplinary study within the modern period of arts and humanities. Students will examine the interrelationships among history and the arts, philosophy, religion and the intellectual ideas of the time. Topics will vary by section. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: British Media and Society
fields.description: Study the history, nature and impact of mass media in the United Kingdom. Emphasis on the impact modern media has on society, and society has on media. Consideration of similarities and differences in mass media in the United States and Great Britain. Consideration of the relationship between mass media and the arts. Focus on 20th century mass media in London, one of the world's preeminent and most influential centers. London term only.

fields.title: Global Cultures [C2HQC]
fields.description: This course is an interdisciplinary study of cultures or regions commonly referred to as non-Western. Students examine diverse responses to enduring human questions at the intersection of local and global cultures. The course offers ways to critically engage comparative views on global cultures and in so doing broaden students' understanding of those cultures and their own. Sections may address themes that span multiple cultural spaces (such as sports or the environment) or focus on regions. Section topics vary by instructor. Only approved topics may count for general education arts and humanities credit.

fields.title: Issues and Trends in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the issues and trends in the inclusive education of infants, toddlers and young children. This course will discuss the historical, philosophical, social and legal background for current practices in the field, evidence-based and recommended practices in early childhood inclusive education, and how to use this information in your professional practice as an early childhood educator.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: EXED 200 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 303 and IECE 321 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 303 , IECE 321 and IECE 322 .

fields.title: Initial Field Experience in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This practicum supports IECE 300 . Students will further their understanding of the issues and trends impacting young children and their families in our community and evaluate their own perspectives and skills as they pertain to working with young children and families from diverse backgrounds, with diverse abilities, and in diverse settings.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to teacher education pre-professional licensure program.

fields.title: Development of Young Children Birth Through Age 8
fields.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the development of infants, toddlers and young children with and without exceptionalities. Skills for observing, recording and interpreting the behavior of the young child as a basis for adult intervention and guidance are developed.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: EXED 200 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 300 and IECE 321 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 , IECE 321 and IECE 322 .

fields.title: Initial Field Experience in IECE Part 1
fields.description: This first course of the intial field experience provides candidates opportunities to use their knowledge of child development to observe and assess children and then plan meaningful learning environments and experiences for those children in a preschool setting. Students in the IECE concentration in the Bachelors of Individualized Study will complete this practicum setting within their current work environment.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: EXED 200 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 300 and IECE 303 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 , IECE 303 and IECE 322 .

fields.title: Curriculum and Instruction in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This course explores, analyzes and evaluates curriculum and methodology related to the design and management of a nurturing, supportive and challenging inclusive learning environment for children ages birth - 8 years. Emphasis is on the physical environment, design and selection of curricular components, the role of play in the curriculum, skills for professional intervention and interaction, and use of technology to facilitate young children's learning.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 300 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 331 , IECE 355 and IECE 466 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 , IECE 303 and IECE 321 .

fields.title: Assessment of the Young Child
fields.description: This course provides students with an understanding of how to use different assessment techniques and strategies to drive educational decision-making for young children with and without disabilities. Students will be introduced to the different purposes of assessment (e.g., instructional planning, delivery, progress monitoring, eligibility) and apply informal and formal assessment techniques that align with the purposes. Students will learn to link assessment to instructional and individualized education plan goals, choose and design valid and reliable assessments, and use assessment results to make educational decisions and provide formative and summative feedback to students.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 450 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 429 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 431 , IECE 460 and IECE 462 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 456 , IECE 460 and IECE 461 .

fields.title: Initial Field Experience in IECE Part 2
fields.description: This second initial field experience is designed to support all courses by giving students experience in an early elementary classroom. Students will observe young children, collect data, assist classroom teachers and interact appropriately with the individuals within the learning environment. Students will analyze the school environments for access for all young children.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: EXED 200 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 300 and IECE 303 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 , IECE 303 and IECE 322 .

fields.title: Foundations of Inclusive Emergent and Early Literacy for Inclusive Early Childhood Education (IECE)
fields.description: This is the first course in a two-course sequence designed to provide pre-service inclusive early childhood teachers with the foundation of literacy development. This course explores both the science and art of teaching emergent and early literacy, providing a strong foundation in literacy development for children from birth to age 5. Grounded in theory and research, the course examines how young children acquire early literacy skills and the dynamic, reciprocal nature of literacy learning between parents, educators and students. Students will investigate key concepts in early literacy acquisition, including the importance of oral language development, phonological awareness, print concepts and early writing. The course emphasizes evidence-based instructional strategies and developmental perspectives, equipping educators to support and enhance the emergence and continued growth of literacy in diverse learners. Through practical applications and reflective practice, participants will learn to create responsive, engaging and developmentally appropriate literacy environments that foster lifelong learning.

fields.title: Intermediate Field Experience in IECE Part 1
fields.description: This first intermediate field experience is designed to support methods courses by giving students experience in an early elementary classrooms. Students will observe young children, collect data, assist classroom teachers and interact appropriately with the individuals within the learning environment. Students will analyze the school environments for access by all young children. Students are required to receive satisfactory experience in this field placement to continue in the program.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 322 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 450 , IECE 456 and IECE 464 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 355 , IECE 464 and IECE 466 .

fields.title: Intermediate Practicum II
fields.description: This second intermediate field experience provides candidates opportunities to use their knowledge of child development and assessment to create learning environments and experiences for children. Candidates will learn more about the adult's role in supporting children and managing behavior.

fields.title: Teaching Early Childhood Learners with Complex Care Needs (IECE)
fields.description: This course is designed to give early childhood special educators exposure to working with children (birth through eight) who have disabilities that include significant medical issues. The role and function of early childhood special educators as team members are addressed both in IEPs and IFSPs (early intervention). The role of related technology, assistive technology and Augmentative and Alternate Communcation (AAC) will receive extensive attention, as will issues of etiology and remediation. This course is taken while students are student teaching; therefore, there will be direct application of skills being learned.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 470 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 466 .

fields.title: Intermediate Field Experience in IECE Part 2
fields.description: This second intermediate field experience is designed to support methods courses by giving students experience in an early elementary classroom. Students will observe young children, collect data, assist classroom teachers and interact appropriately with the individuals within the learning environment. Students will analyze the school environments for access for all young children.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 450 .

fields.title: Contemporary Family Issues in Inclusive Education
fields.description: This course will examine how students' own cultural values shape their interactions with children and families as well as provide concrete, practical strategies for effective and culturally competent interactions with children and families.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 322 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 324 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 421 , IECE 456 and IECE 464 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 470 .

fields.title: Foundations of Literacy (PK-3) for Inclusive Early Childhood Education (IECE)
fields.description: This is the second course in a two-course sequence designed to provide pre-service inclusive early childhood teachers with the foundation of literacy development. This course provides a comprehensive exploration of the science of literacy, focusing on how children acquire and develop literacy skills across a variety of learners in PK-3 classrooms. Grounded in evidence-based research, the course examines the cognitive and neurological processes involved in literacy development and acquisition, including an in-depth look at the reading brain and how it adapts to written language. Students will engage with foundational frameworks such as the Simple View of Reading, which emphasizes the dual importance of decoding and language comprehension, and will analyze the five pillars of literacy - phonemic awareness, phonics, fluency, vocabulary and comprehension. Additionally, the course will explore Scarborough's Reading Rope, illustrating the complex, interwoven strands that contribute to skilled reading. The course also emphasizes the role of assessment in guiding instructional decision making and monitoring progress, equipping educators with tools to evaluate literacy skills effectively. By the end of the course, students will be prepared to apply scientifically grounded literacy practices to support all learners in achieving reading proficiency in the primary literacy classroom (PK-3).
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 322 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 429 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 421 , IECE 450 and IECE 464 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 324 , IECE 460 and IECE 461 .

fields.title: Instructional Practices in Numeracy
fields.description: This course helps prospective early childhood teachers develop the knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective, developmentally appropriate mathematics instruction for young children, birth to age eight, with and without exceptionalities. Emphasis is on appropriate mathematical content, teaching strategies and manipulative materials from a developmental perspective with special emphasis on adaptations designed to meet the needs of all children.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 450 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 429 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 324 , IECE 431 and IECE 462 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 324 , IECE 456 and IECE 461 .

fields.title: Advanced Field Experience in IECE Part 1
fields.description: The advanced field experience provides candidates opportunities to use their knowledge of child development to plan meaningful learning experiences with kindergartners and first graders. Candidates will learn the teacher's role in supporting children to construct understandings about the natural and social sciences, social studies, literacy and to use mathematical thinking. Candidates will begin implementing instructional strategies learned in all methods courses. This course precedes student teaching in the fall.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 324 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 429 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 470 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 324 , IECE 456 and IECE 460 .

fields.title: Instructional Practices in Natural Sciences for Young Children
fields.description: This course is designed to prepare highly qualified inclusive early childhood teachers who will engage all students in scientific content and processes through the effective use of evidence-based practices.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 450 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 466 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 324 , IECE 431 and IECE 460 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 429 .

fields.title: Instructional Practices in Social Studies for Young Children
fields.description: This course provides students with the knowledge, skills and understanding to design and implement effective social science programs for all young children, birth to age eight. Focus is on appropriate social science content, teaching strategies and materials from a developmental perspective with a special emphasis on adaptations designed to meet the needs of children with disabilities. Students will use technology to support access to the learning environment and curriculum.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE majors: IECE 322 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 300 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 421 , IECE 450 and IECE 456 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 355 , IECE 421 and IECE 466 .

fields.title: Managing Classrooms and Guiding Behavior
fields.description: This course examines research and professional literature on effective strategies for guiding young children's behavior and managing groups. This course uses experiences in IECE 331 as a foundation for reflection, dialogue and development of a personal philosophy of classroom management.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 300 .
fields.corequisites: IECE majors: IECE 322 , IECE 331 and IECE 355 . B.I.S./IECE: IECE 355 , IECE 421 and IECE 464 .

fields.title: Individualized Behavior Intervention for Young Children
fields.description: This course is designed to provide application and evaluation of group management techniques and individual interventions that teach and maintain emotional, behavioral and social skills. Students will study various systematic behavioral interventions to support the behavior and learning of individuals with disabilities accessing the general education curriculum including positive behavioral supports, functional assessments of behavior and teaching social skills. A variety of data collection procedures to inform their professional practice will be examined. Students will be applying evidence-based practices related to positive behavior supports, assessment of challenging behaviors and data collection to inform instructional practice and document student response to interventions that improve behavior such that academic learning can occur.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 324 .

fields.title: Advanced Field Experience in IECE Part 2
fields.description: The advanced field experience provides candidates opportunities to use their knowledge of child development to plan meaningful learning experiences with second and third graders. Candidates will learn the teacher's role in supporting children to construct understandings about the natural and social sciences, social studies, literacy and to use mathematical thinking. Candidates will begin implementing instructional strategies learned in all methods courses. This course precedes student teaching in the spring.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 470 .

fields.title: Student Teaching in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This student teaching experience provides students with opportunities to apply, in learning environments for young children, the knowledge, skills and dispositions acquired throughout their teacher licensure program. Under the guidance of university supervisors and professionally licensed cooperating teachers, the student teacher gradually assumes full responsibility as the responsible inclusive early childhood educator. Students majoring in inclusive early childhood education must complete this course twice.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 324 .

fields.title: Seminar in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This seminar accompanies IECE 480 (Student Teaching) and provides students with the opportunity to reflect on, evaluate and improve their experiences as pre-professional educators of young children. Students will evaluate and build their own resiliency, identify ethical dilemmas, and engage in joint problem-solving and ethical decision-making related to their student teaching experience. Students will enhance their abilities to collaborate with families and other service providers.
fields.prerequisites: Minimum grade of "C" in requisites. IECE 324 .

fields.title: Special Topics in Inclusive Early Childhood Education (IECE)
fields.description: This course provides an in-depth examination of selected topics which are of current importance in the field of education. May be repeated for credit when course content changes.
fields.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Teacher as Researcher
fields.description: This course will facilitate students' understanding of the purpose of research, develop a knowledge base of qualitative and quantitative research, recognize the role of research to inform and guide teaching practice for all young children and their families, evaluate research in inclusive early childhood education, and understand the ethics involved in research and practice.

fields.title: Effective Teaching in Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This course will require students to review principles of curriculum design and assessment, and examine research related to best practice for early childhood settings. Students will apply their understanding of children, curriculum and assessment to develop a systematic approach to planning and assessing learning that is standards based and developmentally appropriate.
fields.prerequisites: Permission of the instructor or admission into the graduate program.

fields.title: Practicum in the Education of Young Children
fields.description: This practicum places students in a setting serving either preschoolers or infants and toddlers. Settings may include home, community, and school based programs. Students will demonstrate their knowledge of typical and atypical development, appropriate learning environments, assessments, and activities, and the importance of play. Students will work directly with professionals and families.
fields.prerequisites: Permission of the instructor or admission into the graduate program.

fields.title: Individualized Behavior Intervention for Young Children
fields.description: This course provides the student with exposure to and knowledge of various systematic, individualized behavioral interventions as they apply to young children. The student will develop skills in using these behavior interventions, as appropriate, with young children exhibiting difficulties in learning, behavior and/or social skills.

fields.title: Seminar in Inclusive Early Childhood Education Student Teaching
fields.description: This seminar accompanies IECE 680 and provides students with the opportunity to reflect on, evaluate and improve their experiences as pre-professional educators of young children. Students will evaluate and build their own resiliency, identify ethical dilemmas, and engage in joint problem solving and ethical decision making related to their student teaching experience. Students will enhance their abilities to collaborate with families and other service providers.
fields.prerequisites: IECE 612 , IECE 613 and IECE 614 .

fields.title: Teacher as Leader
fields.description: This course examines the role of the inclusive early childhood educator as a leader. Students will discuss and develop knowledge and skills for advocacy, collaboration, ethical behavior, and professionalism.
fields.prerequisites: IECE 620 and IECE 680 .

fields.title: Creativity and Play
fields.description: This course allows students to examine play theories, research and creativity in terms of human growth and development. Students will explore pedagogical issues with a focus on all children in the context of formal and informal settings. Students will use play observations and assessment to select appropriate methods and materials to support young children's creativity, play and representations.
fields.prerequisites: IECE 620 and IECE 680 .

fields.title: Student Teaching in Inclusive Early Childhood Education
fields.description: This student teaching experience provides students with opportunities to apply, in learning environments for young children, the knowledge, skills and dispositions acquired throughout their teacher licensure program. Under the guidance of university supervisors and cooperating teachers, student teachers gradually assume full responsibility as the inclusive early childhood educator.
fields.prerequisites: IECE 612 , IECE 613 and IECE 614 .

fields.title: Interdisciplinary Scholarship: Introduction to the Independent Scholars Major at JMU
fields.description: IND 200 is designed to introduce students to the Independent Scholars major, and to the concepts of interdisciplinary study. Students will explore interdisciplinary research in a range of contemporary areas of study, including scientific, environmental, political, social, and cultural perspectives. Students will also gain familiarity with the possibilities for individualized study at JMU. Successful completion of the course will involve the development of proposals for individualized curricula.

fields.title: Independent Scholars Senior Project
fields.description: This is a three-semester course sequence involving independent research based on the student-designed curriculum, to be completed by all independent scholars majors. The course is offered as parts A, B and C for one, three, and two credits per semester, respectively.

fields.title: Independent Scholars Senior Project
fields.description: This is a three-semester course sequence involving independent research based on the student-designed curriculum, to be completed by all independent scholars majors. The course is offered as parts A, B and C for one, three, and two credits per semester, respectively.

fields.title: Independent Scholars Senior Project
fields.description: This is a three-semester course sequence involving independent research based on the student-designed curriculum, to be completed by all independent scholars majors. The course is offered as parts A, B and C for one, three, and two credits per semester, respectively.

fields.title: Individualized Study Major Program Development
fields.description: This introductory course is designed to prepare students for transition into higher education programs. Specific content includes focusing a concentration, creating an individualized program, technology in higher education, accessing career resources, career decision making skills, self-awareness, life planning and identifying college level experiential learning. Students will apply the principles of academic writing, use technology and available resources to successfully navigate within higher education, and demonstrate effective communication skills to include critical thinking and analysis.
fields.prerequisites: Individualized Study majors only.

fields.title: Portfolio Development Workshop
fields.description: A short course designed to support students for transition into higher education programs. Specific content includes identifying college-level experiential learning, documenting learning outcomes achieved from experience, documenting learning, determining credit request and organizing a portfolio assessment.
fields.prerequisites: Individualized Study majors only.

fields.title: Orientation to Learning Services
fields.description: A short orientation course designed to prepare students for transition into higher education programs. Specific content includes using the university library, accessing university support services, managing time, developing appropriate study techniques, participating in cultural and workplace diversity exercises, implementing goal-setting strategies, and participating in wellness, nutrition, and stress management programs.

fields.title: Researching, Writing and Document Prior Learning
fields.description: This course provides an opportunity for students to analyze and articulate college-level learning they have acquired outside a classroom context. Specific content includes identifying college-level learning, writing narrative evaluations of learning, integrating multiple sources of learning and disciplinary theory, producing and arranging sufficient documentation of learning, and organizing a portfolio for assessment. At the end of the class, students who have completed all of the assignments will have the components of a portfolio ready for submission for credit evaluation. May not be repeated.
fields.prerequisites: Individualized Study majors only and successful completion of IS 200 .

fields.title: Service Learning
fields.description: Leadership, citizenship, and professional competencies may be acquired through community service experiences. Documented service learning competence will be assessed by the Center for Leadership, Service, and Transition and credit awarded, as appropriate.
fields.prerequisites: IS 203

fields.title: Selected Topics
fields.description: In-depth study of selected topics with current importance and interest to lower division students that are not otherwise covered in the regular course offerings of academic departments/schools. Course content will vary.

fields.title: Special Studies
fields.description: Designed to give students an opportunity to do lower-division independent study in selected interdisciplinary areas under the supervision of a faculty member in the appropriate department/school.

fields.title: Sponsored Learning
fields.description: This course provides a structured learning activity related to a student's area of study and sponsored by an employer, volunteer agency or other appropriate organization. This course functions like a student-organized internship. The course materials guide the reflective process. This course may be repeated for a maximum of six credits.

fields.title: Cooperative Studies
fields.description: Two or more upper-division students may elect to study cooperatively in a selected area of current importance and interest under the supervision of a faculty member in the appropriate department/school.

fields.title: Special Studies
fields.description: Designed to give students an opportunity to do upper-division independent study in selected interdisciplinary areas under the supervision of a faculty member in the appropriate department/school.

fields.title: Individualized Study Project
fields.description: In this course, a student undertakes an in-depth study of an interdisciplinary topic directly related to the student's area of concentration. A final oral report is required. This course may be repeated for a maximum of six credits.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Multiple-semester course.

fields.title: Design Matters
fields.description: As modern challenges grow more complex and ambiguous, design thinking has emerged as a powerful method for addressing them across business, social and cultural contexts. While traditionally linked to visual elements - like products, fashion and interiors - design now includes the creation of services, systems and strategies. More than a static concept, it is an active process focused on developing meaningful solutions. Through this course, students will learn the fundamentals of the design thinking methodology by applying creative problem-solving techniques such as research, ideation and prototyping.

fields.title: Industrial Design Studio
fields.description: This course takes the fundamentals of INDU 200 , INDU 210 and INDU 220 and combines them into industrial design students' first individual holistic design endeavor. Projects will build on the basic skills of design thinking, visual communication and digital tools with deep investigations into concept development, research methods and aesthetics. This course will train students to use and build technical skill sets (sketching, prototyping, presentation) while developing creative skill sets for design process, research and concept development. The expectation is that students will establish a design process (built on learned techniques) that works for them and can be applied over and over. This course will challenge students to make design decisions at every level, in the interest of successful design.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 200 , INDU 210 and INDU 220 .

fields.title: Portfolio Review
fields.description: Portfolio review required to enroll in industrial design courses at upper division standing. May be repeated once for pass/fail standing.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 200 , INDU 210 and GRPH 101 .

fields.title: Making Is Thinking
fields.description: This studio course will introduce students to historic, contemporary and emerging materials through making. This course introduces students to wood shop equipment, machine shop equipment, soft goods lab equipment, thermoforming and the laser cutter. Quality, craftsmanship and shop safety are emphasized. The skills developed will provide students with the opportunity to create professional phototypes and visual tools to aid in their presentation/design development. Materials covered include: wood, metal, plastics, polymers, textiles and ceramics. Through a historic survey of product design, manufacturing will be introduced but is not the main focus of this course. Students will engage in a variety of written assignments and hands-on making projects. Student success in this course requires combination learning consisting of visual, aural, read/write and kinesthetic (VARK) learning in an observational setting.
fields.prerequisites: FDS 102 , FDS 104 and FDS 106 .

fields.title: Materials and Processes for Manufacturing
fields.description: This lecture course will build on history, contemporary and emerging materials through the manufacturing processes of both small scale and industrial scale products. Materials covered include: wood, metal, plastics, polymers, textiles and ceramics. Manufacturing processes covered will be expanded from historic to future technologies used in a variety of product design development. Students will engage in a variety of written assignments and field trips to local manufacturing facilities. Student success in this course requires combination learning consisting of visual, aural, read/write and kinesthetic (VARK) learning in an observational setting.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 210 .

fields.title: Visual Communication for Industrial Design I
fields.description: This course introduces core design visualization techniques that enable students to express design thinking and generate more creative concepts through sketching. By translating a variety of ideas into visual form, students enhance communication within the design process. Because products ultimately exist in three dimensions, students also learn technical drafting to represent their envisioned manufacturing methods and facilitate prototyping. This course cultivates the ability to conceptualize and depict three-dimensional products in 2D, reinforcing foundational skills essential for industrial design practice.
fields.prerequisites: FDS 102 , FDS 104 and FDS 106 .

fields.title: Visual Communication for Industrial Design II
fields.description: This course expands on the foundational skills acquired in INDU 220 , focusing on advanced CAD modeling, photorealistic rendering, visual storytelling and digital fabrication. Students refine or revisit prior projects to develop complex geometries and realistic lighting and materials using advanced rendering tools such as KeyShot. The course also explores AI-powered concept generation to broaden creative ideation. Additionally, students will be introduced to digital fabrication techniques, including 3D printing and VR/AR modeling, to extend their ability to prototype and visualize designs in immersive environments. By the end, students will have produced professionally polished visuals and narrative-driven presentations that showcase strong design communication skills.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 200 , INDU 210 and INDU 220.

fields.title: Topics in Industrial Design
fields.description: Study of selected topics in industrial design at the introductory level. May be repeated when course content changes. See MyMadison for current topics.

fields.title: Product Design
fields.description: This course expands on foundations learned in INDU 200 and INDU 202 and emphasizes a research-driven design process as it applies to the design of objects, including commercial products, packaging design, furniture and more. Students will use quantitative and qualitative research methods and analyze market segments and/or users.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Transportation Studio
fields.description: A study of transportation system design utilizing a multi-disciplinary effort. Students will engage with civil engineers, city planners, urban designers, community members and various stakeholders to understand transportation needs and develop creative solutions.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Professional Practice in Industrial Design
fields.description: This course prepares students for entry into the professional field of industrial design by focusing on the development of a comprehensive design portfolio and essential career-readiness skills. Students will learn to curate, present and communicate their work effectively, while also gaining insight into professional expectations, ethics, job search strategies and the business of design. Emphasis will be placed on critique, refinement and preparation for employment, freelance or graduate study. Course topics may include the development of professional contacts, interviewing skills, portfolio development and the preparation of résumés, press releases and design contracts. Students develop a comprehensive package to prepare for employment based on improved skill sets and capabilities. In-class learning is augmented by site visits to manufacturing facilities, design offices in the area and remotely via Zoom.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 202 .

fields.title: Independent Studies in Industrial Design
fields.description: Independent activity at the intermediate level, such as research or studio practice, under faculty supervision. Projected studies in any area of the school's offering must be arranged with the instructors who will direct them. Offered only with the consent of the instructor.

fields.title: Topics in Industrial Design
fields.description: Study of selected topics in art, art history, graphic design, interior design, or industrial design at the intermediate level. May be repeated when course content changes. See MyMadison for current topics.

fields.title: Systems and Services
fields.description: This studio course aims to engage students in a systems based approach to problem solving. Students will design and test concepts and solutions that focus on interaction and experience. The course emphasizes problem framing, system and service prototyping, graphic design and illustration, user interaction/user experience, and end-user engagement.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Social Innovation and Social Entrepreneurship
fields.description: This advanced studio explores design problems and solutions ranging from sanitation and poverty to environmental degradation and access to basic human services. Students will work individually and on teams to target specific areas of need and develop proposals to create products, systems and services to address those needs while generating revenue.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Industrial Design Advanced Special Topics Studio
fields.description: Study of selected topics in industrial design at the advanced level. May be repeated when course content changes.

fields.title: Senior Thesis Studio
fields.description: Industrial design students with senior standing submit a proposal focused on developing a semester long studio project.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 and senior standing; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Swing Studio Option
fields.description: Students may take a six credit hour studio in ARCD or the equivalent in any one other SADAH studio disciplines (i.e., ART 240 and ART 340 ). The ID program coordinator must approve proposals for swing studio options in advance. Art and design elective courses taken for the ID advanced studio requirement may not be double-counted as swing studios.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Independent Studies in Industrial Design
fields.description: Independent activity, such as research or studio practice, under faculty supervision. Projected studies in any area of the school's offering must be arranged with the instructors who will direct them. Offered only with the consent of the director.

fields.title: Studio Assistant
fields.description: An on-campus program monitored on an individual basis designed to provide practical studio experience in the visual arts. Students will learn safe studio practices and management skills, including material use, inventory control and the proper operation of equipment found within various individual classroom studios.

fields.title: Topics in Industrial Design
fields.description: Study of selected topics in art, art history, graphic design, interior design, or industrial design at the advanced level. May be repeated when course content changes. See MyMadison for current topics.
fields.prerequisites: INDU 208 .

fields.title: Internship in Industrial Design
fields.description: An off-campus program prepared and monitored on an individual basis. Internships are designed to provide practical experience in the arts.

fields.title: Introduction to Information Technology
fields.description: This introduction to the field of information technology is designed to prepare students for a successful career, with an emphasis on developing skills with computers, hardware and software, problem-solving, troubleshooting, studying, and time management. The course also compares information technology with related fields such as computer science, computer engineering and information systems. Topics include networking, databases, computing systems and platforms, cybersecurity, web and mobile systems, and application programming.

fields.title: Data Structures and Advanced Programming
fields.description: This course covers applied data structures, introductory algorithm analysis and advanced programming techniques in the Python programming language. Topics include dictionaries, objects, sets, multisets, stacks, queues and priority queues, as well as their applications in the information technology discipline.
fields.prerequisites: IT major and a minimum grade of "B-" in CS 149 .

fields.title: Computational Structures and Logic
fields.description: This course introduces discrete mathematical concepts and their applications within the IT discipline. The structures studied may include functions, relations, sets, logic, matrices, elementary number theory, basics of counting, graph theory, discrete probability and digital logic. Students will explore the fundamental principles, theorems and techniques related to these structures and apply them to practical applications in the field of IT.
fields.prerequisites: IT major and a minimum grade of "B-" in CS 149 .

fields.title: Information Security and Privacy
fields.description: This course teaches computer security principles and incident prevention and management. It covers the information assurance dimensions of availability, integrity, authentication, confidentiality and non-repudiations to ensure secure transmission, storage and processing of information.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the IT major; MATH 231 or MATH 235 or equivalent; and a minimum grade of "C" in IT 160 and IT 201 .

fields.title: Digital Electronics
fields.description: This course introduces students to digital systems, logic design and the underlying hardware of computer systems. Topics include number systems and binary representations, digital logic gates, various combinational logic blocks, and sequential circuits as well as an introduction to programmable logic devices and basic computer architecture. Design and analysis of circuits will be covered in theory as well as practiced in the laboratory using appropriate industry tools and equipment.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the IT major; MATH 231 or MATH 235 or equivalent; and a minimum grade of "C" in IT 160 and IT 201 .

fields.title: Introduction to Telecommunications and Computer Networking
fields.description: This course introduces students to telecommunications and computer networking concepts. Students learn interactively and collaboratively how networked applications and services are implemented and secured using wireless and wired networks, network services, and protocols. Topics include command-line administration, virtualization, packet analysis, physical/network/transport addresses, the internet, network services and network applications. Students will perform hands-on exercises integrating and troubleshooting networked applications, network techniques, methods and services.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the IT major; MATH 231 or MATH 235 or equivalent; and a minimum grade of "C" in IT 160 and IT 201 .

fields.title: Database Administration
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to database administration focused on securing and maintaining modern database systems in various hosting environments. Through hands-on exercises, students gain knowledge of database deployment and administration, including backup and recovery.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the IT major and a minimum grade of "C" in IT 160 and IT 201 .

fields.title: Projects in Information Technology
fields.description: This course will cover new topics in Information Technology that are of interest to students but not otherwise covered in the curriculum. May be repeated for credit when the course content changes. This course differs from IT 480 in that it is intended for first year, sophomore and junior level students.
fields.prerequisites: First year, sophomore or junior standing IT students only. Topics selected may dictate further prerequisites; students should consult the instructor prior to enrolling for the course.

fields.title: Web Technologies
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to web technologies including languages, the client-server architecture, networking, database concepts and web services. Students learn how to develop web applications that are dynamic, secure and usable.
fields.prerequisites: IT 240 and IT 215 .

fields.title: Societal and Ethical Issues in Information Technology
fields.description: This course is a survey of professional, societal and ethical issues in information technology. Topics include professional responsibilities, privacy, intellectual property, risk identification and evaluation, IT governance, economic and availability factors of IT work, and environmental issues. Students develop skills in assuming and defending positions on societal and ethical issues through oral presentations and written reports.

fields.title: Operating Systems Administration
fields.description: This course introduces students to configuring, deploying and administering computer operating systems. Topics include system configuration, file systems, security, administration, network interfacing, multitasking, multiuser systems, device driver installation and analysis of operating system performance. Students will perform hands-on exercises administering an operating system.

fields.title: Community Projects
fields.description: Students will apply information technology to projects from community partners, including education, government, business and industry. Students will use the skills they have developed to address real-world problems requiring technology solutions. Students will be divided into teams and each team will be responsible for one part of the semester-long project.
fields.prerequisites: IT 301 and a minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Advanced Networking for Information Technology
fields.description: This course presents a practical study of the underlying principles of networking and how these principles are deployed to provide efficient and secure networks for providing voice, data, video and mobility applications. Through hands-on exercises, students gain knowledge of network components, network protocols, network interfaces, network architectures/technologies, network facilities (wired and wireless), network services, network analysis and troubleshooting, network management and policies, network security, and networked applications.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C" in IT 201 or CS 227 , and a minimum grade of "C" in IT 215 .

fields.title: Computer Cyber Crime, Forensics and Auditing
fields.description: This course provides students an introduction to computer crime, relevant laws, agencies and standards. Topics include auditing, logging, forensics and related software, as well as legal principles such as chain of evidence, electronic document discovery, eavesdropping and entrapment. Students will perform hands-on exercises with forensics tools.

fields.title: Data Science and Machine Learning
fields.description: This course provides an overview of data science and machine learning for the Information Technology field. Students will learn how to extract data from sensing devices and use machine learning techniques for data analysis. Students will also learn about skills and tools available for data science.
fields.prerequisites: IT 240 and either MATH 220 or MATH 232 or MATH 235 .

fields.title: Mobile Applications
fields.description: This course is a project-based introduction to fundamental principles of application development for the mobile device environment, emphasizing design and programming paradigms that stem from the use of mobile devices. Topics include user interfaces, event-based programming, inter-process communications, networking, mobile-specific capabilities and performance in a resource-restricted environment. Students will perform hands-on exercises to develop and deploy a mobile application.
fields.prerequisites: IT 240 and a minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Server Administration
fields.description: This course will introduce students to the management of web servers. Topics include administration activities and domains for computing systems, including configuration, deployment, performance analysis, backup and recovery. Students will perform hands-on exercises administering a web server.
fields.prerequisites: IT 311 and a minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Interactive Computing Systems
fields.description: This course examines design and evaluation of effective user interfaces of a computing system, beginning with principles for designing an IT product for user interaction separate from interactive software development. The development process includes iterative life cycle management, systems analysis, design, usability specifications, design representation techniques, prototyping, formative user-based evaluation and connectivity with other IT designs. The course emphasizes an integrative and cross-disciplinary approach with a primary emphasis on usability methods and the user interaction development process.

fields.title: Data Visualization Fundamentals and Techniques
fields.description: This course provides an introductory examination of data visualization through lectures, applied learning activities, readings and hands-on experience with current visualization tools. It also introduces a theoretical framework that covers different types of data, including temporal, geospatial, topical and network data, and their analysis and visualization. Students will improve their data and information literacy, strengthen data visualization skills and build analytic abilities relevant to visualization problems. They will also gain an overview of various data types and examine visualizations and workflows that aim to answer "when" (temporal data), "where" (geospatial data), "what" (topical data) and "with whom" (trees and networks) questions. The course is intended for students with little or no prior background in data visualization and is targeted to those interested in using visualization in their own work and future academic studies.
fields.prerequisites: CS 240 with a minimum grade of "C-" or IT 340 .

fields.title: Internship in Information Technology
fields.description: Students participate in an internship related to information technology outside of the university.
fields.prerequisites: IT 311 , a grade of "C-" in IT 333 and prior approval from IT faculty.

fields.title: Applied Cryptography
fields.description: This course presents techniques in cryptography with analysis of its historical and societal consequences and an emphasis on meeting the needs of the information technology field. Topics include elementary combinatorics and number theory such as modular arithmetic and prime numbers, classical ciphers and accompanying attacks, and rotary machines as well as modern encryption schemes including public channel cryptography, secret-key ciphers, hash functions, side-channel attacks and post-quantum cryptography.
fields.prerequisites: IT 203 and IT 201 .

fields.title: Cloud Computing and IoT Networks
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to the network architectures of cloud computing and the Internet of Things (IoT). Topics include software and hardware components including sensors and detectors for cloud and IoT computing as well as their applications. Students will perform hands-on exercises using IoT applications.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Capstone Project Design
fields.description: This is the first course in a two-course sequence. Students will work in groups to propose an IT-based solution to address a problem or need in the community.

fields.title: Capstone Project Implementation
fields.description: In this second course in a two-course sequence, students will work in groups to implement and integrate their design, manage the project as a team, and prepare an oral and written report on the work.

fields.title: Advanced Cybersecurity
fields.description: This course focuses on the underlying principles of cybersecurity as applied to information and infrastructure network systems and services. Emphasis is placed on gaining hands-on knowledge in network access control, user authentication and authorization, intrusion and prevention systems, and network boundary protection. The course provides a hands-on introduction to the principles of cybersecurity penetration testing.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Internetworking
fields.description: This course will introduce students to technologies and protocols typically used for interconnection of networks. Interconnections of networks deals with routing and establishing an end-to-end information transfer path among end nodes (clients and servers).
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Network Applications Development
fields.description: In this course, students will learn about the design and implementation of network-based applications, focusing on both the application layer and the transport layer of the TCP/IP protocol stack. Students will learn about the design and implementation of network-based applications using languages and architectures such as sockets, Java and Python. Students learn concepts in distributed processing, including synchronization of interprocess communication and management of replicated data. Students analyze performance issues related to distributed applications.
fields.prerequisites: A minimum grade of "C-" in IT 333 .

fields.title: Wireless Networking and Security
fields.description: This course provides an introduction to wireless networking and wireless LAN security and forensics. Radio frequency fundamentals are introduced with emphasis on applications and services.
