fields.description: This course will analyze the root causes of global poverty and critically examine a range of approaches designed to improve conditions for the world's poor. Topics include nutrition and agriculture, healthcare, education, gender equality, water and sanitation, environmental management, and microfinance. Throughout the course, students will read policy documents, work with poverty-related data and analyze a variety of real-world case studies to illustrate key ideas.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Refugees and Humanitarian Response
fields.description: This course will examine the practical and ethical challenges facing refugees and humanitarian actors in the contemporary world. We will survey the causes of forced migration, explore global trends in displacement and humanitarian aid and analyze the laws and institutions that facilitate (or inhibit) refugee protection. We will consider the challenges that refugees face throughout their journey, from border crossings, to refugee camps, to resettlement communities, as well as the practical and ethical tradeoffs that humanitarian actors must weigh in providing assistance and protection. The course will include a community engagement component related to refugee resettlement in Harrisonburg.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Environmental Justice
fields.description: This course provides students with an interdisciplinary introduction to environmental justice. Emphasizing how contemporary environmental issues are profoundly rooted in social, political, and economic conditions, students will apply principles and conceptions of justice to ecological challenges and sustainability efforts in local, national, and global contexts.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Terrorism
fields.description: This course is a survey of the evolution of the phenomenon of terrorism and an analysis of its causes, strategies and forms. This course also discusses the consequences of terrorism in terms of government responses to terrorist threats (homeland security and counter-terrorism) and the economic and political costs of such responses. An interdisciplinary approach linking history, sociology, criminology and political science is used to make sense of this multifaceted phenomenon.
fields.prerequisites: Justice studies major or criminal justice minor; for justice studies majors: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 ; for criminal justice minors: JUST 210 or CRJU 215 ; or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Justice in Literature, Film and Art
fields.description: This class provides an opportunity for students to consider the ways in which issues related to the Justice fields are expressed in literature, film, and/or art and the ways in which such media may influence or create our conceptions of justice.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Ethics and International Politics
fields.description: This course investigates the significance of ethical questions in the theory and practice of contemporary international politics, introducing a variety of normative approaches that shape the issues of peace and conflict, morality and justice in global affairs. Practical case studies will also be used to address issues of policy relevance, with particular attention paid to the American experience.
fields.prerequisites: INTA or POSC majors, or JUST majors who have completed JUST 235 .

fields.title: Rebuilding Post Conflict Societies
fields.description: This course examines the social, economic, security and political problems faced in rebuilding societies that are emerging from a period of intense and prolonged conflict. This course presents an overview of the scope of this multidimensional challenge as well as strategies that have been used to address them. In the course of doing so, evaluation standards are discussed that can be used to measure the success, failure and justness of the newly emerging political system.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: War and Justice
fields.description: This course is an empirical and normative investigation of the relationship between war and justice. Empirically, it examines the causes of war and the ways in which wars end. From a normative perspective it raises the questions of when are wars just; how should a just war be fought; and what is a just peace.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Genocide in the 20th Century
fields.description: This course is an interdisciplinary examination of the various definitions, causes, structure and consequences of genocide. We will study some of the major 20th century genocides (Indigenous peoples, Armenia, USSR, Jewish Holocaust, Cambodia, Bosnia/Kosovo, Rwanda, and Darfur) using the following conceptual schemes: social death, structural violence, oppression, and mass murder.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Global Social Movements
fields.description: This course introduces justice studies students to the origins, development and outcomes of global social movements. It involves a comprehensive approach, which entails an in-depth examination of the main theories explaining the rise of social movements, as well as an empirical focus on global dynamics of popular mobilization. Special attention will be devoted to the examination of the global justice movement.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Global Futures
fields.description: Explores possible future directions that the global system may take in selected issue areas such as energy, democratization, food supplies, and infectious diseases. Emphasis is on active learning strategies, introducing the analytical tools used for analysis of international trends and addressing questions of how to respond in a manner that promotes global justice.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Disability and Justice
fields.description: An interdisciplinary exploration of justice and disability which examines issues such as the historical and theoretical contexts of disability, the social and rhetorical construction of disability, disability legislation and public policy, disability and the criminal justice system, and disability rights movements and inclusion as they relate to larger civil and human rights movements in the US & globally. The course highlights the importance of disability in broader conversations about justice.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Sexual Orientation, Law and Justice
fields.description: This course explores considerations of justice in shaping law and policy related to sexual orientation. The concept of sexual orientation is a relatively recent development in academic, legal, medical and other policy contexts in the United States and globally. Topics addressed in the course include the dehumanization, criminalization, medicalization and oppression of sexual orientation minorities, and legal and regulatory interventions and movements for social justice, criminal justice reform and human rights.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 .

fields.title: Gender Identity, Law and Justice
fields.description: This course explores considerations of justice in shaping law and policy related to gender identity. The concept of gender identity is a relatively recent development in academic, legal, medical, and other policy contexts in the United States and globally. Topics addressed in the course include the dehumanization, criminalization, medicalization, and oppression of transgender, non-binary, and gender-expansive populations and legal and regulatory interventions and movements for gender self-determination, social justice, criminal justice reform, and human rights.
fields.prerequisites: JUST major prereqs: JUST 200 & one other 200-level JUST course, excluding JUST 225 . SJS minor: JUST 221 or 223 . WGSS minor: WGSS 200 & permission of minor coordinator. QUST minor: permission of instructor.

fields.title: Peace Studies
fields.description: A study of the evolution, theory and practice of peace studies. The course focuses on how we wage and resolve conflict, how we effect social change, and how we provide for security through nonviolent means.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST course.

fields.title: Legal Research and Information Literacy
fields.description: This course will provide a thorough insight into how to study law. Students will acquire fundamental legal skills such as how to read a case and identify and differentiate ratio decidendi and obiter dicta, understand the codification of law in a common law jurisdiction, and learn how to accurately research legal topics utilizing and citing primary and secondary legal sources. The course will focus on domestic (U.S.) legal research, involving both state and federal jurisdictions, in addition to investigating international examples and legal instruments.
fields.prerequisites: For justice studies majors: JUST 200 and one other 200-level JUST class, excluding JUST 225 ; for criminal justice minors: JUST 210 or CRJU 215 .

fields.title: Justice Research Methods
fields.description: This course provides students with the tools necessary for conducting independent research in the area of Justice Studies. Both quantitative and qualitative methods are covered. A term project, in which the skills covered in the course are applied, is a significant part of the class.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 , one other 200-level JUST course (excluding JUST 225 ), MATH 220 and one 300-level JUST course.

fields.title: Senior Seminar in Justice Studies
fields.description: This is the capstone course of the Justice Studies major. Students are expected to enter JUST 400 with a proposed area of study, and will spend the semester in developing a thesis. Class discussion and review of individual projects, along with oral presentation of work, are integral parts of the course. Students are expected to produce a piece of original scholarship related to their study in the major.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 , JUST 399 and senior JUST major.

fields.title: Internship in Justice Studies
fields.description: In this course, students integrate professional experiences as interns with justice studies coursework. In addition to working with an agency or organization, students will produce academic work which examines the connections between their area of study and the context of the internship. By application only.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 , JUST 399 , minimum GPA (in major and cumulative) of 2.0, and permission of instructor.

fields.title: Advanced Research in Justice Studies
fields.description: This course is designed to give students a context in which to pursue advanced research in a Justice Studies context. It is especially appropriate for students interested in graduate study in the field.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and JUST 399 , or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Nelson Institute Seminar
fields.description: Students enrolled in this course will be assigned to consider a contemporary problem Justice Studies. Working individually and in teams, students will first study the problem, and then propose workable solutions.
fields.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing only.

fields.title: Practicum in Community-Based Research
fields.description: This course provides students with an intensive, collaborative community-based research experience working in partnership with a community organization or group. Students will integrate and apply principles and conceptions of justice and methods of scholarly inquiry to a community-identified problem. This course may be taken only once for credit.
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and JUST 399 , or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Research Assistantship in Justice Studies
fields.description: Students will work as research assistants under faculty supervision. Students may take this course only by invitation from a faculty member in justice studies and may register for this course only through departmental approval. No student may take more than three credits of JUST 405 .
fields.prerequisites: JUST 200 and two other 200-level JUST courses, excluding JUST 225 ; one 300-level JUST course; invitation of the instructor; and permission of the department head.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Year course. An independent research topic initiated and completed by qualified majors wishing to graduate with distinction.

fields.title: Lifetime Fitness and Wellness (2,2) [C5W]
fields.description: This course is designed to help students adopt and maintain the behaviors associated with an active and healthy lifestyle. Through this course students will learn the importance of maintaining wellness through a physically active lifestyle. Through lectures and labs, students study and develop the behavioral patterns consistent with the current knowledge base in fitness and wellness. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Mindfulness for Health and Wellness
fields.description: This course is designed to provide students with an introduction to formal and informal mindfulness practices. Students will study and practice multiple mindfulness techniques while building a personal resource pool to help develop a daily habit of mindfulness to increase overall personal wellness. Instructional methods will involve a combination of online lectures and applied exercises.

fields.title: Practice in Kinesiology
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce students to basic and beginner topics in kinesiology and movement. Topics will be chosen each semester and reflect current literature and best practice. This course may be repeated once for credit (for a maximum of 6 credits) when course content changes.

fields.title: Introduction to Kinesiology as a Profession
fields.description: This course is designed to help students better understand: the breadth and depth of the discipline of kinesiology and the possible professional career applications that fall beneath the kinesiology discipline umbrella.
fields.prerequisites: First-year or sophomore standing.

fields.title: Biological Foundations of Kinesiology
fields.description: This course is designed to offer an introduction to the biological scientific foundations within the discipline of kinesiology. This survey course includes coverage of topics including applied anatomy and physiology, biomechanics, and exercise physiology.
fields.prerequisites: Kinesiology majors, coaching education minors, pre-athletic training minors, pre-physical therapy minors, or pre-occupational therapy minors only.

fields.title: Introduction to Coaching
fields.description: Through experiential learning activities and discussions, students are introduced to the role of the sport coach as well as the professional, interpersonal and intrapersonal knowledge needed to effectively coach.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 202 .

fields.title: Skill Laboratory: Rhythmic and Dance Activities
fields.description: The skill laboratories are designed for participants who will be in the role of educating others in a particular area of movement. The skill laboratory, Rhythmic & Dance Activities, provides a) basic movement skills, b) analysis of movement, c) developmentally appropriate progressions & teaching ideas, d) curriculum development, and e) micro-teaching opportunities.

fields.title: Skill Laboratory: Teaching Fitness and Wellness in Schools
fields.description: The skill laboratories are designed for participants who will be in a role of educating others in a particular area of movement. The skill laboratory, Teaching Fitness & Wellness in the Schools, provides a) basic movement skills, b) analysis of movement, c) developmentally appropriate progressions & teaching ideas, d) curriculum development, and e) micro-teaching opportunities.

fields.title: Skill Laboratory: Individual and Lifetime Activities
fields.description: The skill laboratories are designed for participants who will be in a role of educating others in a particular area of movement. The skill laboratory, Individual & Lifetime Activities, provides: a) basic movement skills, b) analysis of movement, c) developmentally appropriate progressions & teaching ideas, d) curriculum development, and e) micro-teaching opportunities.

fields.title: Skill Laboratory: Court and Field Games
fields.description: The skill laboratories are designed for participants who will be in a role of educating others in a particular area of movement. The skill laboratory, Court & Field Games, provides: a) basic movement skills, b) analysis of movement, c) developmentally appropriate progressions & teaching ideas, d) curriculum development, and e) micro-teaching opportunities.

fields.title: Skill Laboratory: Wilderness and Adventure Education
fields.description: The skill laboratories are designed for participants who will be in a role of educating others in a particular area of movement. The skill laboratory, Wilderness & Adventure Education, provides: a) basic movement skills, b) analysis of movement, c) developmentally appropriate progressions & teaching ideas, d) curriculum development, and e) micro-teaching opportunities.

fields.title: Exercise Physiology
fields.description: This course is designed to help the student explore and understand the physiological changes that occur during an acute bout of exercise and as a result of chronic physical training. Students will study the role various (e.g. cardiovascular, respiratory, nervous, neuro-endocrine, and renal etc.) systems play in maintaining homeostasis during physical activity. In addition, the physiology of physical performance under a range of environmental conditions will also be examined.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: Exercise Physiology Laboratory
fields.description: This course involves laboratory experiences related to core concepts of exercise physiology.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: Motor Development and Learning
fields.description: This course provides understanding of motor development from early childhood through adulthood. The focus is on the constraints to development and the interaction between the environment, task and learner. The course provides an understanding of the learning processes underlying performance. Emphasis is given to the application in both teaching and coaching settings.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the Kinesiology exercise science concentration or declared to the Kinesiology PHETE concentration.

fields.title: Historical and Philosophical Foundations of Sport and Physical Activity
fields.description: This course includes an introductory analysis of selected historical periods and philosophical theory concerning the development of ideas about sport and physical activity from Ancient Greece and Rome to contemporary United States cultures.

fields.title: Psychological Foundations of Sport and Performance
fields.description: This course focuses on exploring psychological concepts related to participation and performance in sport and exercise contexts. This course is not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 353 or KIN 426 .
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration or declared to the Kinesiology PHETE concentration. Not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 353 or KIN 426 .

fields.title: Human Biomechanics
fields.description: This course involves studies of anatomical, physical and mechanical factors, as these factors affect human movement.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: Human Biomechanics Laboratory
fields.description: This laboratory course is designed to complement and supplement the lecture course KIN 306 . The course will focus on enhancing the students' laboratory experiences in biomechanics.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: School Health Content
fields.description: An overview of select topics in health education content necessary to implement a comprehensive health education program, geared toward child and adolescent populations.

fields.title: The Profession of Teaching Health and Physical Education
fields.description: This course introduces the roles of the teacher and the learner and the pedagogical content knowledge of health and physical education. An in-depth examination of the unique position and qualifications of the specialist in physical education and health. Systematic observations will occur.

fields.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription
fields.description: This course will examine the principles of exercise testing and prescription as they apply to fitness, performance and health. The role of health-related components of fitness in performance and health of apparently healthy adults will be examined.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: Exercise Testing and Prescription Laboratory
fields.description: This laboratory course is designed to complement and supplement the lecture course KIN 321 . The course will focus on enhancing and providing practical opportunities to apply the students' exercise testing skills and prescription development knowledge.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration.

fields.title: Social Aspects of Sport
fields.description: This class is designed to familiarize students with the concepts of sport as they relate to individuals and the larger society in which they live and the ways in which this relationship is reciprocal, with both people impacting the world of sport and sport impacting individual, social, cultural, economic and political developments. Students learn the tools needed to think in a critical way about sports in society and make informed choices about sports and participation.

fields.title: Developing Mental and Life Skills through Sport and Physical Education
fields.description: This course explores current sport psychology theories, models and concepts. Students examine mental and life skills and apply the information to their coaching and/or teaching context. Not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 305 or KIN 426 .
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration, declared to the Kinesiology PHETE concentration or coaching education minors. Permission of the instructor. Not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 305 or KIN 426 .

fields.title: Practicum in Exercise Science
fields.description: This practicum in exercise science provides the student with supervised experience in their field of study. This course may be repeated in different settings. Instructor permission is required.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration; major GPA of 2.0 or higher; and permission of instructor.

fields.title: School Health Content for PHETE
fields.description: An overview of selected topics in health content required for teacher candidates preparing to teach health education in public schools. Special emphasis will be on issues relevant to teaching these topics in schools.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 309 .

fields.title: Measurement and Evaluation in Kinesiology
fields.description: The administration and interpretation of measurement and evaluation procedures in kinesiology and recreation.

fields.title: Adapted Physical Education
fields.description: This course explores the disability categories listed in IDEA and ensures the acquisition of content knowledge and instructional strategies to successfully implement inclusive and adapted physical education programs. Practicum experience is included.
fields.prerequisites: Acceptance to PHETE program.

fields.title: Assessment in Elementary Physical Education
fields.description: This course is an introductory study of developmentally appropriate, authentic and formal assessment techniques unique to elementary physical education.
fields.prerequisites: Acceptance to PHETE program.

fields.title: Instructional Methods in Elementary Physical Education
fields.description: This course introduces students to effective teaching strategies and allows application through peer microteaching and teaching students in a school setting. Students will apply the affective, cognitive, and psychomotor principles in class management, unit and lesson planning, and instructional techniques. Principles of self-evaluation and reflective teaching are reinforced.
fields.prerequisites: Acceptance to PHETE program.

fields.title: Elementary Curriculum in Physical Education
fields.description: This course is designed to explore the theory and application of games, dance, and gymnastic activities compatible with the developmental characteristics of elementary children and the educational objectives of elementary schools. Students will engage in a practicum experience within an elementary school.
fields.prerequisites: Acceptance to PHETE program.

fields.title: Advanced Principles of Group Exercise Leadership
fields.description: Theories, principles and procedures involved with leading group fitness classes. Students will gain knowledge and experience in class design and choreography development. Programming for children, older adults, pregnancy and aquatic exercise will be included. Practical and written assessments will occur throughout the semester. Participation in group exercise classes is a requirement. Students will have the opportunity to enroll in the AFAA Primary Group Exercise Certification.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 100 , KIN 202 , or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Exercise and Nutrition in Chronic Disease
fields.description: This interdisciplinary course examines the evidence-based relationship between exercise and diet patterns and behaviors, and major chronic diseases. Students will understand the epidemiology and pathogenesis of prevailing chronic diseases. Emphasis will be placed on developing exercise and dietary strategies to reduce the burden of chronic disease.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration; KIN 302 and KIN 321 .

fields.title: Concepts of Strength and Conditioning
fields.description: This course examines theory and application of coaching concepts in strength/conditioning training, including program design, testing and specific techniques for the physical development of athletes. It is designed for students interested in working with athletic populations. This course also prepares students for NSCA certification.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration or coaching education minor; KIN 100 or HTH 100 ; KIN 202 .

fields.title: Psychological Foundations of Exercise and Health Behavior
fields.description: This course will focus on the theoretical and practical applications of behavior change related to healthy lifestyles with an emphasis on physical activity. In addition, course content will include a detailed investigation into the psychological and environmental factors associated with adoption and maintenance of healthy behaviors including a regular physical activity program. This course is not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 305 or KIN 353 .
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the exercise science concentration; KIN 302 . Not open to students who have previously earned credit in KIN 305 or KIN 353 .

fields.title: Advanced Topics in Exercise Science and Leadership
fields.description: This course is designed to allow students to study specific topics in exercise science and leadership. Topics will be chosen each semester and reflect current research in exercise science related to clinical exercise physiology, human performance and methodologies or trends in exercise science/leadership. May be repeated once (maximum 6 credits) for credit when course content changes.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 302 and KIN 302L .

fields.title: Special Topics in Adapted Physical Education
fields.description: This course provides an in depth look into specific areas within the field of adapted physical education and adapted physical activity. This application-based course provides hands-on experiences that will allow students to work with individuals with disabilities in a variety of settings. Graduate students will also be asked to analyze and provide feedback on the instructional behaviors of the undergraduate student instructors.

fields.title: Exercise Across the Lifespan
fields.description: An advanced course in exercise science that examines aspects of physical activity and exercise as they relate to specific phases of the human lifespan. This course will address the importance of physical activity for children, pregnant women, and older adults and will include an in-depth study of aspects of exercise physiology that are unique to these populations.

fields.title: Environmental Exercise Physiology
fields.description: An advanced course in exercise physiology that examines how human physiological systems respond and adapt to exercise performed in challenging environmental conditions (i.e. high altitude, diving, hot, cold).
fields.prerequisites: KIN 302 and KIN 302L .

fields.title: Physiology of Endurance Performance
fields.description: This course aims to provide students with an understanding of how to utilize endurance training to maximize athletic performance. Various factors that limit endurance performance and examine methods to overcome these factors will be explored. Emphasis will be placed on the role of seasonal periodization and program planning to maximize the long-term development of athletes. Supplemental factors that may also aid performance, such as equipment, nutrition, and ergogenic aids will be discussed.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 302 and KIN 302L .

fields.title: Exercise, Cardiovascular Disease and ECG Assessment
fields.description: This course is designed to provide students with a foundational information related to electrocardiography, diagnostic exercise testing and the effects of exercise on specific cardiovascular diseases.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 302 .

fields.title: Exercise Immunology
fields.description: Students will develop an in-depth understanding of the human immune system and how it is impacted by exercise. Specific focus will be placed on examining the relationship between immune function, exercise and risk of infections. Additional aims will be to explore physiological and molecular mechanisms that determine immune function and how they are impacted by acute and chronic exercise.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 302 .

fields.title: Strength and Conditioning II: Advanced Training Methods and Concepts
fields.description: This course focuses on advanced training techniques and program design for athletes as well as utilizing sport science to monitor the adaptational process. This includes physical test selection, administration, scoring and interpretation of results. The practical portion of the course includes demonstrating and coaching peers through advanced training techniques as well as administering and performing physical tests. Designed for students interested in working with athletic populations and preparing to sit for NSCA-CSCS certification examination.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 425 and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Strength and Conditioning III: Philosophy, Leadership and Managerial Responsibilities
fields.description: This course focuses on the practical, managerial and leadership elements critical to strength and conditioning professionals' everyday operations. This includes developing mission and purpose statements, creating policies and procedures, determining facility design and maintenance, hiring/managing staff, and leading by example. Discussions center around those entering the strength and conditioning profession or a similarly related field. Designed for students interested in a career in strength and conditioning and/or working with athletic populations and preparing to sit for NSCA-CSCS certification examination.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 425 and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Advanced Respiratory Physiology in Exercise Science
fields.description: This course will provide an in-depth exploration of respiratory system function and its critical role in exercise and performance. Through a combination of laboratory data and current research, students will evaluate cardiorespiratory performance and apply physiological concepts to exercise training.
fields.prerequisites: Fully admitted to the Exercise Science Concentration and KIN 302 .

fields.title: Principles of Coaching Methods
fields.description: This course will focus on methods of teaching sport skills, organizing and running effective practices, evaluating athletes, and developing season plans based on long-term athlete development. Developing team culture, working with multiple stakeholders and creating a safe practice environment are also included. Overall, students will further develop core competencies in coaching practice and will gain practical experience in the field.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 205 .

fields.title: Internship in Coaching
fields.description: This course offers a sequence of selected experiences in coaching, which provides the student with supervised experience to develop their coaching effectiveness.
fields.prerequisites: Coaching education minor, successful completion of all courses in the minor, minor GPA of 2.0 or higher and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Practicum in Sport Communications
fields.description: A sequence of selected practicum experiences which provides the student with supervised practicum experience in Sport Communications.

fields.title: Student Teaching in Physical Education
fields.description: A supervised teaching experience at the elementary school setting that provides teacher candidates with opportunities to experience the classroom environment, grow professionally, and develop their pedagogical skills.
fields.prerequisites: Acceptance into student teaching.

fields.title: Internship in Exercise Science
fields.description: This professional experience in exercise science affords students the opportunity to apply theory and methodology in their field of study under qualified supervision from the cooperating agency and the university. May be repeated for a maximum of 12 credits.
fields.prerequisites: Cumulative GPA of 2.0 or higher; KIN 381 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Special Studies in Kinesiology and Recreation
fields.description: Designed to give superior students in physical education an opportunity to complete independent study and/or research under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Students will work with a faculty member to conceptualize a research project and then compose a proposal of the project with anticipated methods.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Students will carry out the data collection for the proposed project under the guidance of their faculty mentor.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: Students will compose the final project report, in manuscript format and according to departmental guidelines.

fields.title: Motor Learning and Development
fields.description: This course provides understanding of motor development from early childhood through adulthood. The focus is on the constraints to development and the interaction between the environment, task and learner. The course provides an understanding of the learning processes underlying performance. Emphasis is given to the application in both teaching and coaching settings.

fields.title: Technology in Health and Physical Education
fields.description: Addresses technological issues related to education and explores a variety of educational technologies available to enhance the instruction of physical and health education. An action plan for the utilization of educational technologies will be developed.

fields.title: Instructional Methods in Middle and  Secondary Physical Education
fields.description: A detailed study that builds upon the undergraduate instructional methods in physical education with developmentally appropriate teaching and management techniques for middle and secondary physical education. An in-depth review of the theoretical framework of the teaching styles and application of such in a practical setting are vital components.

fields.title: Professional Issues for Prospective Physical and Health Educators
fields.description: An in-depth examination of current issues and research on teaching and teachers in physical and health education.

fields.title: Special Topics in Adapted Physical Education
fields.description: This course provides an in depth look into specific areas within the field of adapted physical education and adapted physical activity. This application-based course provides hands-on experiences that will allow students to work with individuals with disabilities in a variety of settings. Graduate students will also be asked to analyze and provide feedback on the instructional behaviors of the undergraduate student instructors.

fields.title: Adapted Physical Education and Sport
fields.description: This course examines the disability categories listed in IDEA and ensures the acquisition of pedagogical content knowledge to implement inclusive and adapted physical education and sport programs. Practicum experience is included.

fields.title: Assessment and Measurement in Physical Education
fields.description: This course is an advanced study of developmentally appropriate authentic and formal assessment techniques unique to elementary physical education.

fields.title: Methods of Teaching in Elementary Physical Education
fields.description: This course provides advanced teaching and learning strategies for implementation within an elementary physical education setting. Students will apply the affective, cognitive and psychomotor principles in class management, unit and lesson planning, and instructional techniques. Principles of self-evaluation and reflective teaching are reinforced.

fields.title: Curriculum and Instruction in Elementary Physical Education
fields.description: This course explores advanced theory and application of games, dance and gymnastic activities compatible with the developmental characteristics of elementary children and the educational objectives of the elementary school.

fields.title: Environmental Exercise Physiology
fields.description: This is an advanced course in exercise physiology that examines how physiological systems respond and adapt to exercise performed in challenging environmental conditions (i.e. high altitude, diving, heat, cold and polluted environments).
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Athlete Skill Development: Applying Learning Principles to Coaching
fields.description: This course introduces students to learning principles from motor learning, educational theory and sport pedagogy to support athlete skill development. Students will have opportunities to apply the learning principles to their practice plans, reflect on ways to improve practices and engage in micro-coaching to improve athlete learning and performance.

fields.title: Strength and Conditioning for Sport Coaches: From Strategy to Practice
fields.description: This course equips sport coaches with the knowledge, skills and experiences needed to effectively administer strength and conditioning programs within their coaching environments. Designed for adult learners, the course blends strategic thinking with practical, day-to-day coaching challenges. Learners will explore multifaceted problems of practice such as injury prevention, load management and long-term athlete development, and apply evidence-based solutions in real-world contexts. Through cognitive apprenticeships and applied tasks, coaches will develop a nuanced understanding of strength and conditioning, including how to integrate physical training into sport settings, communicate its value and adapt to athlete needs. The course emphasizes self-directed learning, contextual decision making and tangible takeaways that coaches can immediately apply in their practice.

fields.title: Coaching Athletes for Mental Excellence: A Theory-to-Practice Approach
fields.description: This course integrates sport psychology theory with practical coaching strategies designed to help athletes strive for peak performance. Emphasizing a whole-athlete approach, coaches learn to incorporate objectives like focusing under pressure, resilience and sustainable motivation to promote competitive success and long-term personal development. Through case studies and reflective practice, coaches will learn to apply psychological principles in real-world coaching contexts.

fields.title: Physical Activity Epidemiology
fields.description: The impact of physical activity on health will be examined with epidemiological evidence. This course will cover the principles of epidemiology research and review seminal studies that have led to our current understanding of the relationship between physical activity and health. Students will be able to critique current physical activity recommendations and public health initiatives through an understanding of the evolution and limitations of past and present studies.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Exercise Across the Lifespan
fields.description: An advanced course in exercise science that examines aspects of physical activity and exercise as they relate to specific phases of the human lifespan. This course will address the importance of physical activity for children, pregnant women, and older adults and will include an in-depth study of aspects of exercise physiology that are unique to these populations.

fields.title: Physiology of Endurance Performance
fields.description: This course studies physiological aspects of athletic performance in endurance-based sports. Physiological traits associated with high levels of performance (such as VO2max, lactate threshold, movement economy) will be discussed, with respect to their influence in specific sport settings. Principles of endurance training methods will also be discussed, with specific application to program planning for athletes.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Theories and Practices of Weight Management
fields.description: An examination of the physiological, psychological and environmental theories of obesity. Current trends in obesity research are emphasized. Case studies and laboratories are utilized to provide students with practical experience in constructing a weight loss program.

fields.title: Curriculum Design in Health and Physical Education
fields.description: An advanced study that builds upon the undergraduate elementary curriculum course by focusing on the middle and secondary student, curriculum models, and the development of effective and futuristic physical education units and programs that meet the needs of the populations.

fields.title: Teaching for Student Success in Health and Physical Education
fields.description: The diversity of student populations in schools relates to differences in ability, socioeconomic status, cultural background, race, religious beliefs, sexual orientation and gender. This is an in-depth study of appropriate teaching methods that celebrate diversity and inclusion. Experiences will serve to diminish fears and the perpetuation of stereotypes, and to allow opportunities to plan and implement activities in which all students are challenged and successful.

fields.title: Analysis of Teaching and Learning
fields.description: An in-depth look at assessing and improving teaching. A systematic approach to improving teaching techniques and assessments of student learning will be discussed and implemented in a practical setting.

fields.title: Methods in School Health for PHETE
fields.description: This course provides an overview and application of methods for teaching health in the school grades 6-12. Teacher candidates will develop skills in planning, instructional methods, classroom management and reflective teaching. To provide for the application of theory a teaching practicum is incorporated within the course.

fields.title: Qualitative Analysis of Movement
fields.description: This is an advanced course that examines the systematic analyses of selected motor skills and human movements. Students will develop observational skills and techniques to detect and correct errors impacting motor performance for a K-12 learner.

fields.title: Advanced Fitness Testing and Exercise Prescription
fields.description: This course provides students with the knowledge and skills required for administering and evaluating aspects of physical fitness (e.g., cardiorespiratory, muscular, flexibility, body composition) and quality of life. Additionally, this course prepares students with the knowledge and skills required for developing and implementing a comprehensive and effective exercise prescription, including goal setting and methods to obtain goals.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Advanced Exercise Assessment and Electrocardiography
fields.description: This course helps students develop expertise in administering and interpreting 12-lead and single-lead electrocardiograms (ECG) at rest and during exercise. The course helps students develop proficiency in various exercise testing protocols, along with a comprehensive understanding of normal and abnormal physiological responses to exercise across diverse clinical conditions (e.g., cardiovascular, pulmonary, metabolic pathologies).
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Exercise Management in Chronic Disease
fields.description: This course studies the benefits, risks and strategies for exercise testing and programming for persons with respiratory, neuromuscular, skeletal and immunological diseases, as well as psychological disorders. Prevalence, economic ramifications, pathophysiology, clinical manifestations, assessment, pharmacology, potential benefits, and risk of exercise and exercise programming strategies are emphasized.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Cardiorespiratory Exercise Physiology
fields.description: This is an advanced course in exercise physiology that provides an in-depth analysis of the cardiopulmonary system and acute responses to exercise. This course will cover the basic anatomy and physiology of the cardiopulmonary system. Emphasis will be placed on principles of ventilation, diffusion, blood flow, ventilation-perfusion relationships between the pulmonary and cardiovascular systems, gas transport by the blood, mechanics of breathing, and control of ventilation. The course will focus on how these key principles are impacted by acute exercise as well as the adaptations that occur in response to exercise training.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Muscular and Hormonal Aspects of Exercise
fields.description: This course is designed to help the student explore and understand in detail the role that the muscular and endocrine systems play in challenging/maintaining homeostasis during physical activity.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Metabolic Aspects of Exercise
fields.description: This is an advanced course in exercise physiology that examines the acute responses and chronic adaptations of metabolic systems with exercise. This course will examine topics including the biochemistry of energy supply, metabolic responses to exercise and adaptations to training and how various factors (such as nutrition) can influence these responses/adaptations. Emphasis will be placed on the mechanisms underlying metabolic responses/adaptations to exercise and on the metabolic determinants of human physical performance.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Research Techniques
fields.description: Skill in the initiation, conduct and interpretation of research. Laboratory procedures in physical education, recreation, exercise science, and athletics are included as well as historical, philosophical and descriptive methods. Special emphasis is given to laboratory, experimental, field and action research.

fields.title: Reading and Research
fields.description: Directed reading in designated areas and specialized interests. Investigating, researching and reporting. Course may not be repeated.

fields.title: Internship in Kinesiology
fields.description: This course provides students with a practical experience in a variety of settings, including sports performance, research, cardiac rehabilitation, K-12 school physical and health education setting, physical therapy, exercise testing and prescription, program administration, or other professional responsibilities in wellness/fitness. Specific assignments are based on student needs.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the kinesiology graduate program.

fields.title: Secondary Internship in Health and Physical Education
fields.description: A supervised teaching experience at the middle or high school level in both health and physical education settings. Enables the teacher candidate an opportunity to apply effective teaching techniques and innovative forms of instruction and organization at the secondary level.

fields.title: Directed Research in Kinesiology
fields.description: Advanced research in kinesiology under the direction of a graduate advisor. Course will be graded on an S/U basis. Course may not be repeated.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 655 and permission of instructor.

fields.title: Comprehensive Continuance
fields.description: Continued preparation in anticipation of the comprehensive examination. Course may be repeated as needed.

fields.title: Thesis Continuance
fields.description: This course offers continued study, research and writing in the area of thesis concentration. This course may be repeated as needed.

fields.title: Thesis Research
fields.description: This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.
fields.prerequisites: KIN 655 or equivalent; and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Elementary Korean I
fields.description: This course covers the fundamentals of Korean through listening, speaking, reading and writing. This course provides practice in pronunciation and development of comprehension.

fields.title: Elementary Korean II
fields.description: This course builds on the foundations established in KOR 101 through listening, speaking, reading and writing activities. This course provides practice in pronunciation and development of comprehension.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 101 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Korean I
fields.description: A thorough review of grammar, vocabulary building, conversation, composition, and reading.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 102 or permission of the instructor. A student cannot earn credit for KOR 231 after completing KOR 232 .

fields.title: Intermediate Korean II
fields.description: A thorough review of grammar, vocabulary building, conversation, composition, and reading.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 231 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Language for Living
fields.description: This course is designed to enhance students' practical communication skills in Korean, preparing them for everyday interactions in personal, academic and professional contexts. Building on the foundations established in KOR 232 , this course emphasizes real-life language use through topics related to daily life, social events and work. Students will engage in speaking, listening, reading and writing activities designed to improve fluency and cultural understanding. The course prepares students to navigate various real-world situations while deepening their knowledge of Korean social customs and language norms.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 232 ; or by placement exam or by permission of instructor.

fields.title: Contemporary South Korean Culture and Society
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce students to Korean culture and society with a focus on major social and historical changes related to contemporary Korean culture. The course will explore diverse themes relevant to understanding Korea today, such as a brief history of Korea, modernization, multiculturalism, gender and education issues, lifestyle as well as traditional and contemporary popular culture. This course will combine lectures with analysis and discussions of various media such as texts, literature, films, newspaper articles as well as audio-visual artifacts including Korean news, films, TV dramas and pop songs in class. Instruction is in English.

fields.title: Culture and Communication in Context
fields.description: This course is designed to develop students' reading and writing skills through the exploration of Korean cultural themes. Students will engage with short, accessible texts and visual materials that introduce traditional and contemporary aspects of Korean society. The course emphasizes formal and informal written communication, helping students gain confidence in expressing themselves in written Korean while gaining insights into social structures, media and cultural practices. Through reading, writing and discussions, students will improve their cultural literacy and written communication skills.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 232 ; or by placement exam or by permission of instructor.

fields.title: Korean Short Stories
fields.description: This course is designed to enhance students' reading comprehension and to explore the unique Korean cultural and social worldviews through folktales. Each reading will introduce useful phrase and idioms, as well as diverse themes of stories including filial piety, morality, greed and love. The course also uses audio and visual materials such as story recordings, paintings, maps and short films. Students will engage in a variety of activities such as discussions, presentations and compositions to achieve effective learning outcomes. Readings are in Korean. Instruction is in Korean and English.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 232 ; or by placement exam or by permission of instructor.

fields.title: Special Topics in Korean Literature
fields.description: This course studies a particular topic in Korean literature. It may cover all or a specific Korean literature genre. This course may be repeated if content varies.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 300 or KOR 320 ; or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Special Topics in Korean Culture
fields.description: Students will study a particular topic in the culture of Korea. Course may be repeated if content varies. Instruction is in English.

fields.title: Special Topics in Korean Linguistics
fields.description: Students will study a particular topic in Korean linguistics. Topics could include an introduction to Korean sociolinguistics or psycholinguistics. Course may be repeated if content varies.
fields.prerequisites: KOR 300 or KOR 320 ; or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Independent Study in Korean
fields.description: The course allows students an opportunity to pursue independent study in Korean under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Elementary Latin I
fields.description: This is an introductory course for students who intend to acquire only a reading knowledge of classical and medieval Latin. It includes systematic study of the fundamentals of grammar.

fields.title: Elementary Latin II
fields.description: This is the second part of an introductory course for students who intend to acquire only a reading knowledge of classical and medieval Latin. It includes systematic study of the fundamentals of grammar.
fields.prerequisites: LAT 101 .

fields.title: Intermediate Latin I
fields.description: An introduction to Latin literature. The further study of Latin grammar and the elements of Latin prosody are also presented.
fields.prerequisites: LAT 102 or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Latin II
fields.description: An introduction to Latin literature. The further study of Latin grammar and the elements of Latin prosody are also presented.
fields.prerequisites: LAT 231 or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Independent Study in Latin
fields.description: This course allows students to pursue individual study in Latin under the supervision of the instructor.

fields.title: Introduction to Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies [C2HQC]
fields.description: An introductory interdisciplinary survey of basic theoretical concepts to analyze the Latin American, Caribbean and U.S. Latinx experience, with special focus on how historical processes in Latin America and the Caribbean gave rise to specific and varied cultural production and forms in the region. May be used for general education credit.

fields.title: Internship in Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies
fields.description: Provides Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies minors with work experience in career fields they are interested in pursuing. A journal, internship report, research paper, bibliography and evaluation from the intern provider are required. May count as an elective for the LAXC minor.

fields.title: Topics in Latinx Studies
fields.description: This course introduces students to key issues in the interdisciplinary field of Latinx Studies, which examines the communities, cultures, histories and experiences of people of Latin American descent in the United States. The topic for each semester will be announced on MyMadison. Course topics will highlight the historical and contemporary issues that shape the political, social and cultural practices, as well as the lived experiences of Latinxs in the United States. The course will encompass various approaches to the field of Latinx studies, potentially including media studies, political science, literature, history, anthropology, sociology, communication and more. LAXC 300 will begin with a brief introduction that asks "What is Latinx Studies?" The course will then examine a range of topics including colonialism, race, ethnicity, class, gender, sexuality, migration, language, media, representation, participation and resistance. Students will critically engage with written text and various media that encourage them to examine Latinx communities in all their diversity and complexity.
fields.prerequisites: LAXC minors; or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Latina/o/x Politics: Origins and Futures
fields.description: The course will focus on the Latina/o/x populations in the United States and how the category of 'Latino' came into existence. Furthermore, students will learn how Latina/o/x identity has evolved over time as well as become politically salient within 21st century politics. The goal is for the student to develop a broad, conceptual understanding of how the term 'Latino' came into existence as well as how individuals who identify as 'Latina/o/x' have politically organized throughout history.
fields.prerequisites: POSC 225 .

fields.title: Borderlands Policy: Latina/o/x Politics in Context
fields.description: This course is centered on the policies surrounding the U.S. and Mexico border, with a focus on the effect these policies have had on Latina/o/x populations. Students will examine peer-reviewed studies of immigration policy, public opinion and political rhetoric, as well as individual accounts of the immigrant experience. By the end of the course, students will have an increased understanding of how border policy has historically evolved and the Latino/a/x population reactions across time.
fields.prerequisites: POSC 225 .

fields.title: Independent Study in Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies
fields.description: Designed to give capable students in Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies an opportunity to complete independent study under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Special Topics in Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies
fields.description: In-depth examination of selected topics of current importance to the field of Latin American, Latinx and Caribbean Studies. May be repeated for credit when course content changes.

fields.title: Foundations of Data Leadership
fields.description: This course provides an overview of the history of leadership scholarship, leadership theory and behaviors associated with ethical and effective leadership.

fields.title: Systems Thinking in Data Literacy, Design and Analysis
fields.description: This course discusses the core components of systems thinking, complexity leadership strategies, the role of data in complex systems and systems analysis and design.

fields.title: Strategic Leadership Communications
fields.description: In this course, students will examine communications strategies that use data to build consensus, engage stakeholders and enhance mission fulfillment across a variety of organizational environments. This is an advanced seminar focusing on persuasion theory and communication methodology relevant to strategic communication in diverse cultural settings. Emphasis is placed upon message analysis in cross-cultural contexts at various communication levels including interpersonal, small group, organizational and public. The course considers communication strategies and tactics embedded in adversarial belief systems. This seminar will use lecture-discussion, case studies, guest speakers and team projects.

fields.title: Statistical Modeling for Leadership Decision-Making
fields.description: This course aims to equip future leaders with the essential statistical tools required for informed decision-making. Students will be introduced to statistical modeling techniques relevant to a variety of sectors such as non-profit, government and industry. This course emphasizes how statistical models can be employed in strategic planning and leadership to make ethical and effective decisions.

fields.title: Data Visualization and Interpretation for Leaders
fields.description: This course aims to teach future leaders how to interpret and present data effectively to inform decision-making. Students will learn about best practices in data visualization, storytelling with data and how to make data-driven arguments more compelling. The course will utilize a range of software tools to create visualizations that are both informative and persuasive.

fields.title: Optimizing Leadership with Big Data
fields.description: This course empowers future leaders to harness data tools, including AI, for strategic and effective leadership in government, nonprofit organizations and industry. Students will develop the skills to generate data or pull it from governmental datasets. Students will also learn to interpret and communicate data insights, using data manipulation, statistical analysis, and communication to drive informed decision-making and inspire high-performing organizations and agencies. Leaders will learn how to craft and implement big-data and advanced-analytics strategies, from building core analytical knowledge and fostering data-driven cultures, to leading analytics talent and communicating results and data informed strategies.

fields.title: Data Ethics and Ethical Decision-Making
fields.description: In this course, students will examine ethical leadership, ethical data gathering, analysis and interpretation, and using data to inform ethical leadership practices and decisions. Class discussions will focus on the role of data in policy and decision-making, including ethical questions around the datafication of society and AI. Through case studies in healthcare, energy and environmental policy, social welfare, and administrative decision-making, students will engage with real-world applications of data science concepts and examine their impacts.

fields.title: Technological Leadership for Public Good
fields.description: This course focuses on leadership perspectives best suited to complex, big data environments as well as core and emerging research in this area. Utilizing human-centered design and UX design principles, this course helps students to leverage data and digital technologies to improve organizational and societal policies, programs and services.

fields.title: Leading with Data in Cross-Cultural Environments
fields.description: This course examines cross-cultural leadership preferences that impact how leaders make decisions regarding human resources and organizational management. The course also explores models of how leaders communicate and implement decisions across a variety of geographic and workplace contexts including in-person, remote and hybrid environments as well as the differing role of technology in those settings.

fields.title: Data Leadership Capstone
fields.description: In this capstone course, students will apply the principles learned throughout the program to a real-world technology leadership challenge. The outcome will be a comprehensive data strategy to address the problem.

fields.title: Introduction to Leadership Studies and Ethics
fields.description: This doctoral survey course covers the history, philosophy, theories and concepts of organizational leadership. This course will differentiate between the roles of the manager and the leader and provide the student with the foundations of organizational leadership. This course provides an opportunity to examine pertinent leadership theories, to develop a personal understanding of leadership and to explore the relations of leaders and followers.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the Strategic Leadership Studies graduate program or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Topics in Leadership Studies
fields.description: Designed to give students an opportunity to complete a brief independent investigation of a leadership topic. May be repeated with a different topic.

fields.title: Special Studies in Strategic Leadership
fields.description: In-depth study of a current topic in the field of Strategic Leadership Studies. Content varies depending on the topic and instructor. May be repeated for different special studies.

fields.title: Advanced Research Methods in Leadership Studies
fields.description: This course focuses on principles of research design and planning in strategic leadership studies at the doctoral level.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the Strategic Leadership Studies graduate program or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Advocacy for Change Leadership
fields.description: This course is designed to enable students to understand the distinction among civic participation organizations and political advocacy.

fields.title: Effective College Teaching
fields.description: For PhD candidates who seek employment as faculty members, this course is important to the degree. As new PhDs, they will be expected to show effectiveness in this area from the beginning of their careers. Increasingly, colleges and universities are looking to hire new PhDs who have had a teaching course and/or supported teaching experience for effective university classrooms. This course is designed to present specific theories and strategies for teaching effectively in the collegiate classroom and assists students in showing rigor and effectiveness in teaching from the beginning, thus promoting job placement. This course gives students the opportunity to take the higher-level knowledge and skills and apply them to teaching/learning situations.

fields.title: Mixed Methods Research for Leadership Studies
fields.description: Mixed methods research (MMR) is a popular approach in leadership studies and its associated disciplines (e.g., postsecondary education, non-profit studies, organizational sciences, etc.) given its distinctive ability to answer research questions that benefit from the integration of quantitative and qualitative data. This doctoral-level class will provide the opportunity to learn about the opportunities (and challenges) confronting mixed-methods research, with the overall objective being to equip students with the ability to independently design, conduct and disseminate mixed-methods research in leadership studies and its associated applications.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 705 .

fields.title: Advanced Learning Theories and Instructional Models
fields.description: This course focuses on the design, delivery, assessment and supervision of instruction in schools, across schools, throughout the school division and in the community.

fields.title: Advanced Curriculum Theory and Instructional Issues
fields.description: This course focuses on the determination, development, implementation, assessment and revision of curriculum and its relationship to the design, delivery, assessment and supervision of instruction in schools, across schools, throughout the school division and in the community.

fields.title: Foundations of Postsecondary Education
fields.description: Encompasses the practice, theory and empirical underpinnings of postsecondary education. Approaches may draw upon cultural, political, economic, historical, social and global aspects.

fields.title: Leading Educational Organizations
fields.description: Analyze, apply study of ethics, values and leadership concepts. Apply four ethical paradigms of justice, care, critique and profession. Integrate and apply knowledge of educational laws, personnel supervision and education finance. Analyze change theory as related to cognitive and social processes and apply to school and organizational change. Analyze the impact of personnel motivation, work performance and evaluation on school culture. Evaluate sociopolitical influences on leadership in schools.

fields.title: Organizational Theory
fields.description: This course provides a broad overview of the field of organizational science and key components that unite and divide the field drawing upon an overview of various social science disciplines such as organizational development, change, climate, and culture.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 701 .

fields.title: Organizational Behavior and Leadership
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce students to the principles of organizational transactions, internal and external, with a focus on leading organizational change. The course links communication theory and research to effective practices, emerging issues, evaluation and experiential learning opportunities in organizational practice.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 750 .

fields.title: Organizational Change and Strategic Human Resource Management
fields.description: This course examines the key theories, purposes and roles of organizations in today's world. The main focus is on the design and structure of organizations based on their mission, environments, complexity, size and span. Differences between public, private and governmental organizations are examined. Organizational culture and its effect on ethics, change leadership and innovation are studied. Designing for performance, sustainability and innovation are foci of this course.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 750 .

fields.title: Research in Organizational Leadership
fields.description: This course focuses on principles of research design and planning in organizational science and leadership. Students will conduct a defensible research topic, research plan, data collection, selection of methodology and implications.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 605 , PSYC 606 , PSYC 608 and LEAD 754 .

fields.title: Strategic Leadership Decision Making
fields.description: This doctoral level course is designed to develop organizational leaders' practices related to and theoretical understanding of policy, accountability and assessment in organizations and in organizational science generally.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 606 .

fields.title: Proseminar in Principles of Nonprofit Organizations
fields.description: The first course in the concentration is designed to enhance students' understanding of how third-sector organizations differ in economic, legal and political terms from government and for-profit organizations. The course fosters understanding of the theoretical, organizational and practice space occupied by various types of nonprofit organizations within the sector as well as their purposes, and the current status of service provision.

fields.title: Civil Society and the Nonprofit Sector
fields.description: This doctoral survey course explores the synergy between civil society and the nonprofit sector by tracing the theoretical and historical perspectives of each. The role of cultural and political context in the development of civil society and the nonprofit sector are presented from a leadership perspective through emphasis on voluntary associations and their potential role in fostering social transformations across national and transnational boundaries.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 760 .

fields.title: Organizational Governance
fields.description: The roles, structure, functions and composition of organizational boards and their relationship to organizational leadership and performance are investigated. Strategies for improved board performance and accountability are explored.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 760 .

fields.title: Philanthropy and Resource Development
fields.description: A doctoral seminar exploring the historical, economic, political, social and psychological foundations of philanthropy in American society as well as the ethical, legal and financial aspects of organizational resource development. The role of leadership strategies for acquisition, maintenance and stewardship of resources including various organizational stakeholders is emphasized. The course includes perspectives from theory, empirical research and practice.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 760 .

fields.title: Leadership and Accountability for Nonprofit Organizations
fields.description: This course presents methods of accountability, impact assessment and evaluation in nonprofit organizations in light of myriad stakeholders. The role of leadership in determining and implementing processes of internal and external evaluations is explored.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 760 , LEAD 761 , LEAD 762 , LEAD 763 and PSYC 606 or equivalent.

fields.title: Empirical Approach to Leadership Training and Development
fields.description: This course involves instruction in the design, practice and evaluation of leadership development in a variety of settings. Empirical research on the use and effectiveness of leader development efforts will be reviewed. Students will analyze case studies of effective organizations and a variety of assessment and development activities will be completed as part of the course. Also students will respond to a sample request for proposals for leadership development.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 605 or permission of instructor.

fields.title: Policy Development and Analysis in Postsecondary Education
fields.description: Current issues of higher education are analyzed and future trends are discussed. Various approaches to policy development and their applications are examined from institutional, state, federal, legislative and international perspectives.

fields.title: Postsecondary Dynamics
fields.description: This course closely examines the dynamic relationship (and, within this, relationships) between students and postsecondary organizations.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 740 .

fields.title: Leadership and Accountability I
fields.description: This doctoral level course presents methods of accountability, impact assessment and evaluation. The course takes an interdisciplinary approach to accountability and program evaluation in business, higher education and nonprofit organizational settings and the stakeholders commonly found in these settings. The role of leadership in determining and implementing processes of internal and external evaluations is explored.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 701 and LEAD 705 .

fields.title: Leadership and Accountability II
fields.description: This doctoral-level course focuses on complex quantitative, evaluative research designs used in leadership studies. The content of the course includes conducting statistical analyses associated with experimental and quasi-experimental intervention evaluative designs.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 805 .

fields.title: Doctoral Leadership Research I
fields.description: This doctoral-level course focuses on complex quantitative, correlational research designs used in leadership studies. The content of the course includes both parametric and non-parametric correlational designs.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 701 and LEAD 705 .

fields.title: Doctoral Leadership Research II
fields.description: This doctoral-level course focuses on the application of advanced quantitative, correlational statistics research methods used in leadership studies.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 810 .

fields.title: Advanced Leadership Dynamics
fields.description: This course and work experience represents the final pre-dissertation stage for the leadership studies doctoral program. As a capstone course and experience, it is designed to integrate prior knowledge (both tacit and explicit) and current work experiences with more advanced leadership concepts and applications.
fields.prerequisites: Admission to the Strategic Leadership Studies graduate program or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Externship in Advanced Leadership
fields.description: The externship represents the culmination of the student's formal course of study and is an applied learning opportunity. The instructor for LEAD 891 serves as the externship supervisor and oversees all aspects of the externship. The student can expect to spend an average of 35 hours per credit hour working within or for another organization.

fields.title: Dissertation Continuance
fields.description: Continued study, research and writing in the area of dissertation concentration. This course does not count toward fulfilling the required hours for the degree; it may be repeated as needed.
fields.prerequisites: LEAD 900 .

fields.title: Doctoral Dissertation
fields.description: Provides advanced research required of all doctoral candidates. Course is graded on an S/U/I basis. Students must take a minimum of 12 credit hours of LEAD 900 to fulfill program requirements. Up to 6 additional credit hours may be taken, but these cannot be used to fulfill program requirements.

fields.title: Education Law and Equity
