fields.description: A thorough review of grammar, vocabulary building, conversation, composition and reading.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 231 or per placement exam score.

fields.title: Language for Living
fields.description: This advanced communication and culture course is designed to bridge basic language study with upper-level coursework in the Spanish language and culture. It is intended for students who have begun to develop advanced skills in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational communication and are interested in delving deeper into the study of Spanish-speaking countries, their histories and their cultures. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 , or per placement exam score.

fields.title: Pop Culture through Language
fields.description: This class examines popular culture in Spanish-speaking cultures in a variety of forms and media: history, politics, literature, sport, music, cinema, fashion, comics and media. By focusing on pop culture and different media, this course teaches the critical analysis of textual and visual imagery in their historical and cultural context. Students will be able to learn the main pop culture references that are recognized nationally and internationally. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 , or per placement exam score.

fields.title: Spanish for Social Work
fields.description: Cross-cultural competence in social work requires a keen understanding of language and culturally sensitive interactions. This course provides specialized language education to increase cultural sensitivity with diverse Spanish-speaking populations and their corresponding environments. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 .

fields.title: History of Spanish Culture and Society
fields.description: This course examines the history of Spanish culture and society from the Romans until the present. It offers a review of historical and contemporary figures. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: History of Spanish Culture and Society - Spain
fields.description: A history of Spanish culture and society from the Romans until nowadays. Review of historical and contemporary figures. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 .

fields.title: Latin American Cultures
fields.description: This course studies the geographical, historical and cultural development of Latin America from pre-Columbian times to the present. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Introduction to Spanish Linguistics
fields.description: This course will introduce students to the fundamental components of linguistics (phonology, morphology, syntax, pragmatics and semantics) using data from the Spanish language. The topics and approach of this course consider the social and dialectal varieties of Spanish and the change of Spanish over time, including the present use of Spanish in the United States. The course requires no previous knowledge of linguistics, but presupposes familiarity with Spanish at the 300 credit level or higher.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Contrastive Linguistics
fields.description: In this course students analyze the main grammatical differences between Spanish and English with the focus on producing accurate and idiomatic translations into both languages.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Translation Competencies
fields.description: In this course, students will develop linguistic competencies required in translation, including reading comprehension, summary writing, text analysis and use of mono- and bilingual dictionaries. Students will learn some basic electronic tools and word processing skills for translators, and practice several types of translation, including direct translation, inverse translation and back translation. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Sounds of Speech
fields.description: This course introduces students to Spanish linguistics, with special emphasis on Spanish phonetics. Students will engage with theoretical concepts and practical applications to understand the phonological structures and sounds that make up the Spanish language. Class activities and assignments aim to enhance overall language proficiency, including listening, reading, speaking and pronunciation skills. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Culture and Communication in Context
fields.description: This Spanish course focuses on building proficiency in the language with an emphasis on oral and written expression to facilitate further study of the culture. Students will learn how to use the appropriate language in culturally specific contexts and develop intercultural competence. The course's essential question is "How do Spanish-speaking peoples communicate on subjects that are at the heart of their societies?" Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Culture and Communication in Context (for Heritage Speakers)
fields.description: This course takes the place of SPAN 320 for the heritage speaker of Spanish (someone who has learned Spanish from family members and/or at home), with mostly oral (and not written) experience. It provides an opportunity for the student to expand their existing proficiency and to develop more formal language skills. Emphasis will be placed on reading, writing and presenting. Topics of current Latino issues will keep students interested and engaged.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Language Landscapes
fields.description: This Spanish course introduces students to the regions or countries where the language is spoken, the features of the area, and the ways of life there. The course examines the identities, customs and events that influence the lives of people living in these culturally and linguistically defined areas and explores the diverse cultural landscapes that shape their lives. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Business Spanish
fields.description: This course presents basic business and commercial Spanish vocabulary and terminology. It focuses on trade customs and commercial communication, including interviews, letter writing and simultaneous interpretation. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Business Spanish-Spain
fields.description: This course presents basic business and commercial Spanish vocabulary and terminology. It focuses on trade customs and commercial communication, including interviews, letter writing and simultaneous interpretation. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 .

fields.title: A Journey through Literature
fields.description: This course is designed to prepare students in literary analysis of the novel as well as short stories, poetry and drama. All necessary terminology will be studied. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: A Journey through Literature - Spain
fields.description: This course is designed to prepare students in literary analysis of the novel as well as short stories, poetry and drama. All necessary terminology will be studied. This course is mandatory for all Spanish majors before taking any other literature class. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 .

fields.title: Spanish for Public Safety
fields.description: This course presents basic Spanish legal vocabulary and terminology. It emphasizes the practical application of the Spanish language in routine and high-risk law enforcement situations and explores cultural issues that are important for law enforcement personnel. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish for Medical Professionals I
fields.description: This course focuses on the basic Spanish language and vocabulary required in the fields of medicine and health sciences. Students practice their oral Spanish skills in various simulated medical situations in preparation for future professional application in the medical environment. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish for Medical Professionals I
fields.description: This course focuses on the basic Spanish language and vocabulary required in the fields of medicine and health sciences. Students practice their oral Spanish skills in various simulated medical situations in preparation for future professional application in the medical environment. Instruction is in Spanish.

fields.title: Latin American Short Story
fields.description: In this course, students read and analyze representative short stories from Latin America. Students report on selected authors. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Latin American Short Story - Spain
fields.description: Reading and analysis of representative short stories from Latin America. Student reports on selected authors. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 335 .

fields.title: Spanish Short Stories
fields.description: In this course, students study literary Spanish short stories from the Middle Ages to the present, including a selection of texts by prominent authors such as Don Juan Manuel, Cervantes, Alarcón, Bécquer, Zorrilla and Clarín. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish Language and Culture Abroad
fields.description: This is an advanced communication and culture course designed to bridge basic language study with upper-level coursework in Spanish literature and culture. It is intended for students who have begun to master advanced skills in interpretive, interpersonal and presentational communication and are interested in examining nuances of the Spanish language and Spanish-speaking cultures while studying abroad.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 212 or SPAN 232 , or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Advanced Conversation
fields.description: Discussions deal with topics of current interest. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 320 or SPAN 321 .

fields.title: Spanish in the United States
fields.description: This course will study the present situation of Spanish in the United States, how Spanish has been shaped by social forces in the US and how Spanish, in turn, shapes these forces. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Aspects of Contemporary Spanish Culture and Society
fields.description: This course will study the history, culture and society of Spain during the 20th and 21st centuries. Emphasis will be placed on the changes in Spain after Franco. Instruction in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or by placement exam or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Latinx Music Cultures
fields.description: This course explores the heterogeneity of Latina/o/e/x identities and cultures through music from the 20th and 21st centuries. Study of Latina/o/e/x music will be framed by cultural studies through concepts such as hybridity, transculturation, border identities, cultural imperialism and colonialism. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Stories and Histories: The Generation of 1898
fields.description: This course examines major Spanish writers who engaged with their nation's defeat in the 1898 Spanish-American War. Students will read, analyze and discuss works from Azorín, Pío Baroja, Valle-Inclán, Antonio Machado, Maeztu and Unamuno. This group of intellectuals varied in their writing styles but shared a broad commitment to the cultural and aesthetic renewal of Spain. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Stories and Histories: Latin American Novel
fields.description: In this course, students will read and analyze representatives of Latin American novelists of the 20th century. Students report on selected authors. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Voices of Today: Wounds and Words in Post-War Spain
fields.description: This course provides an exploration of key artistic and literary works in Spain during the 20th century. Emphasis is placed on the intersection of Spanish history, society and culture, focusing on the Post War period, Franco's dictatorship (1939-75) and the role of historical memory in shaping both the artistic expressions and the collective consciousness of Spain. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Voices of Today: Latin American Poetry
fields.description: In this course, students will read and analyze representatives of Latin American poets. Students will report on selected authors. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Transformative Texts
fields.description: The purpose of this course is to acquaint students with historical periods in Spanish literature and culture through the study of key influential texts. Analyses of these texts (i.e. essays, novels, plays, films, paintings and comics) will be grounded in key political, scientific and artistic movements. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Voices of the Past: Works of the Golden Age
fields.description: This course offers a study of literary genres and their development through the Spanish Golden Age, culminating in Cervantes. This may include works by Cervantes or Fernando de Rojas. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 322 or SPAN 335 .

fields.title: Advanced Business Spanish
fields.description: This course presents advanced business and commercial Spanish vocabulary and terminology. By focusing on topics such as the origin of business and companies, company constitution and organization, human resources, labor law and commercial law, marketing, products, services, and the sale of consumer goods, students compare the business environment of Latin America with that of the United States. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Translation Strategies
fields.description: This course discusses aspects of translation theory such as skopos, translation loss, translation gain and language bias. Students learn several translation strategies at the phrase and sentence levels and practice these strategies thoroughly before investigating terminology, terminology mining and terminology management. Instruction is in English and Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Introduction to Interpretation
fields.description: This course presents an overview of the interpreting profession. It introduces students to the main techniques they need to become competent interpreters in the various sectors of interpreting. Instruction is given in English and Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Introduction to Medical Interpretation
fields.description: The course fulfills the program content standards, instructional methods standards and programmatic standards recommended by the National Council on Interpreting in Health Care's (NCIH) National Standards for Healthcare Interpreter Training Programs. The curriculum is designed to meet the examination requirements of both the NCIH and the Certification Commission for Healthcare Interpreters (CCIH) which administers a national certification program for all healthcare interpreters. The areas covered in the course include: basic concepts of medical interpreting; the Code of Ethics and National Standards; best practices that support the Code of Ethics and National Standards; understanding the role of culture and cultural competence in interpreting; identifying appropriate situations for advocacy and "cultural brokering;" building interpreter skills and knowledge (positioning, note-taking, memory use, etc.); and practicing the modes of interpretation: consecutive, simultaneous and sight translation/interpreting. The focus of the course is to build proficiency in the three modes of interpreting and to learn and apply the ethical standards of the profession in healthcare interpreted-mediated settings. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Introduction to Legal Interpretation
fields.description: The course will provide students with knowledge of the US legal system and the interpreting process. The areas covered include knowledge of the structure of the courts (federal and state systems), stages of the legal process (e.g., pre-trial proceedings, trials and post-trial proceedings), ethical principles and standards of professional conduct of interpreters, and the ability to apply this knowledge in practical case scenarios. Students will develop basic skills in the three modes of interpreting: simultaneous, consecutive and sight interpreting used in legal settings. Students will also learn basic note-taking skills for the enhancement of memory recall during consecutive interpretation. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Special Topics in Spanish Literature
fields.description: This course offers a study of a particular topic in Spanish literature. It may cover all or a specific Spanish literature genre. This course may be repeated if the content varies. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Special Topics in Spanish-Speaking Cultures
fields.description: Students will study a particular topic in the culture of Hispanic countries. This course may be repeated if the content varies. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Special Topics in Spanish Linguistics
fields.description: Students will study a particular topic in Spanish linguistics. Topics could include an introduction to Spanish sociolinguistics and psycholinguistics. This course may be repeated if the content varies. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Women in Hispanic Literatures
fields.description: This course studies women in literature in the Hispanic world. The focus is on women authors, female characters in literature or both. The course may include works from Spain or Latin America from any time period. Students examine feminist literary criticism, canon formation and other critical topics. Emphasis may vary according to the instructor. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish Theater
fields.description: This course focuses on refining Spanish language skills to facilitate further study of Spanish language and culture. To this end, the course will focus on studying of plays from various centuries and staging and performing selected scenes. Students will engage in improvisations and games with classmates to study all aspects of theater. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish-Language Cinema
fields.description: This course studies the structure of the cinema and vocabulary related to film. The course will cover topics in Spain and Latin America. Instruction in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish for Medical Professionals II
fields.description: This course provides future medical professionals with further practice in Spanish in the medical context. Students learn advanced medical vocabulary and anatomical terminology, develop their reading comprehension skills, and acquire greater fluency through student presentations and classroom discussions on the latest medical techniques and advances. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Culture and Medicine in Latin America
fields.description: This course enables students to acquire greater linguistic proficiency and cultural competence in the medical context through classroom discussions and reading comprehension. Students analyze how different kinds of inequalities (e.g., gender, racial, economic, etc.) affect health care in Latin American countries; examine popular and religious beliefs applied to medicine in Latin America; and research a medical challenge or success in a specific Latin American or Caribbean country. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Culture and Medicine in Spain
fields.description: This course enables students to acquire greater linguistic proficiency and cultural competence in the medical context through classroom discussions and reading comprehension. Students analyze historical and contemporary medical discoveries and discuss medical protocols and practices in the Spanish medical system. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Spanish in Healthcare: Policy and Practice in Latinx Health
fields.description: In this course students learn about the health and language policies of the US for Spanish-speaking patients. Some of the topics that will be discussed are how language affects health, health policy in the United States, language concordance in healthcare, and the role of medical interpreters for the Latinx community health. Students will work in groups for a final project to develop an academic poster. Instruction is in Spanish and English.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Business and Society in Latin America
fields.description: This course explores the development of Latin American society in the business and economic contexts and investigates areas such as importation and exportation, the health and education systems, banking and financial institutions, agriculture, and the textile, fashion, wine, motion picture, music, and media industries. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Business and Society in Spain
fields.description: This course investigates several sectors of the Spanish economy, including the food industry, industrial port activity, importation and exportation, the petrochemical industry, the leisure industry, and the wine making industry. Students tour several important multinational companies in Salamanca, Spain, and attend presentations given in Spanish by staff of those companies. This course is taught in Salamanca, Spain. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Independent Study in Spanish
fields.description: This course allows students an opportunity to complete independent studies under faculty supervision. Instruction is in Spanish.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 ; or permission of the instructor.
fields.corequisites: SPAN 300 , SPAN 301 , SPAN 320 , SPAN 321 or SPAN 322 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Spanish Art - Spain
fields.description: A study of the art and architecture of Spain from medieval times through the present. Concentration on specific artists, as well as general movements in the history of Spanish art.

fields.title: Business Spanish Internship
fields.description: This course gives students the opportunity to practice the theoretical knowledge, linguistic skills and cross-cultural competencies learned in SPAN 330 . With permission of the business Spanish minor coordinator, students work as volunteers or interns in the public service, private industry or business management sector, locally or abroad. Faculty-supervised course work required for completion: monthly reports (3), final paper (reflections/lessons learned) and presentation, and performance evaluation by agency or organization.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 330 .

fields.title: Spanish Internship Abroad
fields.description: This course will provide students with experiential learning opportunities within the Hispanic field while participating in a study abroad program. The internship course is designed to provide practical experience in fields such as government, business, industry, health sciences, nursing, administration, education, translation, non-profit or the arts, where they can apply their language skills. Examples of internship work may include working for a company in the student's field of interest abroad, completing a translation project or working as an interpreter. A journal, internship report, research paper, reflection or evaluation from the internship provider is required. Credits earned correspond to the internship hours completed. This course may be applied as an elective in the Spanish major or minor.
fields.prerequisites: One SPAN course at the 300-level or above and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Spanish Internship
fields.description: This course will provide students with experiential learning opportunities within the Hispanic field. The internship course is designed to provide practical experience in fields such as government, business, industry, health sciences, administration, education, translation or the arts, where they can apply their language skills. Examples of internship work may include working for a company in the student's field of interest abroad; serving as a research assistant for a professor; completing a translation project or working as an interpreter. A journal, internship report, research paper, bibliography or evaluation from the internship provider is required. Credits earned correspond to the internship hours completed. Up to six credits may be applied as electives in the Spanish major or minor.
fields.prerequisites: SPAN 300 .

fields.title: History and Evolution of the Spanish Language
fields.description: This course delves into the transformation of the Spanish language from its Latin roots, emphasizing the influence of other languages and key historical periods. Students will trace the etymology of significant terms, analyze historical texts, and investigate the language's evolution across different eras. The course also examines the major historical, social and cultural forces shaping modern Spain and Latin America, highlighting the intersection of linguistic and historical developments. Through these explorations, students will develop educational materials that incorporate authentic historical texts into Spanish language instruction, deepening their understanding of the linguistic and cultural heritage of the Hispanic world.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Cultural Expressions in Spanish Art and Society
fields.description: This course examines Spain's rich artistic and cultural expressions from the 20th and 21st centuries. Students will explore vital artistic styles, significant musical works and notable films, contextualizing them within their historical and geographical frameworks. The course emphasizes visible and less visible cultural manifestations, including attitudes, lifestyles and popular traditions such as festivals. Additionally, students will develop educational materials to effectively present these cultural elements in Spanish as a Foreign Language (ELE) classrooms, enhancing appreciation for the diversity and heritage of the Spanish-speaking world. This course is taught in Salamanca.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Fundamental Texts of Spanish Literature
fields.description: This course invites students to engage critically with Spanish literature by writing reflective texts that analyze various literary works. Students will utilize Spanish and Latin American literary, journalistic and digital texts as valuable sources of information to explore the language, ideology, and historical, social, and cultural contexts of their authors. Students will learn to apply key interpretive techniques and methods for conducting analyses, critical commentaries, and reviews of literary works. The course emphasizes the importance of locating necessary reference sources for analyzing Spanish texts across various periods and authors. Additionally, students will gain an understanding of the different stages in the development of Spanish and Latin-American literature, fostering a deeper appreciation for its richness and diversity.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Understanding Language Development for Spanish Teachers
fields.description: This course aims to help students develop the skills necessary to teach Spanish grammar as a foreign language. This course will also equip students with the proper terminology and concepts of Spanish grammar to become better teachers.

fields.title: Advance Language Development for Spanish Teachers
fields.description: This course focuses on the design of teaching and learning activities for Spanish grammar using various methodological approaches. Students will learn to identify and utilize appropriate reference sources to address gaps in rule application. The course also emphasizes the importance of selecting and presenting grammatical rules effectively. In addition, students will learn how to use authentic texts for classroom development and create original materials for practicing specific aspects of Spanish grammar, enhancing their ability to teach Spanish in diverse educational settings. This course is taught in Salamanca.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Studies on Spanish Variation
fields.description: This course focuses on critically examining variation in the Spanish language, encouraging students to write reflective texts on the subject. Participants will develop a concrete proposal for a Spanish as a Foreign Language (ELE) class, demonstrating linguistic proficiency and pedagogical expertise while adhering to specific parameters. The course will also emphasize creating teaching materials incorporating examples of geographical and sociolinguistic variation. Additionally, students will identify challenges in establishing patterns for the diverse uses of Spanish in the Spanish-speaking world, addressing diatopic, diaphasic and diastratic variations. Through these activities, students will enhance their understanding of the complexities of Spanish language variation, their awareness of the scope of Spanish in the world, and its implications for language teaching.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Advanced Research Methods
fields.description: This course provides a comprehensive approach to qualitative and quantitative research methods, focusing on practical application in professional contexts. Students will develop skills in designing and conducting research projects, selecting the most appropriate data collection and analysis techniques, and addressing ethical considerations in research. Emphasis is placed on analyzing data to draw meaningful conclusions and effectively communicating findings that answer research questions. Additionally, students will explore how applied research contributes to professional growth and decision-making, preparing them to integrate research skills into their careers. This course is taught in Salamanca.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Pan-Hispanic Standards of Spanish
fields.description: This course equips students with theoretical and practical tools for teaching Spanish pronunciation, writing and other normative aspects of the language. Students will gain a comprehensive understanding of oral and written standards and rules across Spanish-speaking countries, focusing on mastering spelling and punctuation based on the current pan-Hispanic orthographic standards (1999, 2005, 2010). Through analysis and practice with real-world materials, students will refine their oral, listening and writing skills in alignment with Spanish linguistic norms. Additionally, students will learn how to effectively select and present appropriate grammatical rules to different target audiences. The course emphasizes the development of custom teaching materials for classroom use, focusing on concrete aspects of Spanish norms. This course is taught in Salamanca.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Applied Research Project
fields.description: This course focuses on mastering the skills necessary to conduct applied research. Students will learn to effectively gather and analyze information to formulate research projects that address real-world issues. The course emphasizes the proficient use of scholarly sources, equipping students with the tools to navigate academic literature confidently. Additionally, students will refine their academic writing skills, ensuring they can express their ideas clearly and correctly while adhering to appropriate academic conventions. Through a combination of theoretical foundations and practical applications, students will prepare to produce high-quality research that meets the standards of scholarly excellence.
fields.prerequisites: Admitted to the Education, MEd, Spanish Language and Culture for Educators concentration.

fields.title: Leadership in Sport and Recreation Professions
fields.description: This course will introduce students to the concept of leadership, explore leadership theory, provide opportunities to develop leadership skills, relate leadership to ethics and values, and assist students in applying good leadership practice into their current and future roles and responsibilities in sport, recreation and campus recreation industries.

fields.title: Philosophy in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course involves a critical review of literature concerning the nature and significance of sport and recreation from a philosophic perspective, including current modes of inquiry. Implications for sport and recreation in education are also discussed.

fields.title: Research Techniques in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course teaches skill in the initiation, conduct and interpretation of research. Research methods in sport, recreation, and campus recreation are included as well as historical, philosophical and descriptive methods. Special emphasis is given to experimental, field and action research.

fields.title: Administration in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course will address specific problems and new developments in the administration of sport and recreation programs and the fundamental concepts and principles of management. The course will focus on improving performance within sport and recreation organizations. Several areas will be discussed, including developing goals, decision making, strategic planning, operational planning, managing change, communication and supervision; various skill sets in these areas will be practiced.

fields.title: Workshop in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course is an intensive study of one aspect of sport, recreation or campus recreation that is of current concern to administrators in the field.

fields.title: Marketing and Promotions in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course provides the student with an examination and utilization of marketing principles in the areas of sport and recreation. Topics will include sport and recreation products and services, marketing strategies, consumer behavior, research and information management, promotions, positioning and sponsorship.

fields.title: Fiscal Planning and Management in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course is an overview of fiscal resources and financial administration of sport, recreation and campus recreation programs and facilities. The course will focus on the financial administration of public agencies, private organizations and commercial enterprises. Management areas relating to financial principles and policies, sources of revenue, types of expenditures, budget preparation, and preparation of grant proposals will be discussed.

fields.title: Facilities and Event Management in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course involves the planning, construction, maintenance and utilization of sport, exercise and recreation facilities. The course will also include planning and managing events in the various types of venues within sport and recreation industries.

fields.title: Facilities and Operations in Campus Recreation
fields.description: This course is designed to explore the problems, principles, and techniques of planning, design, and management of campus recreation facilities. Students will develop the conceptual connection between maintenance/custodial needs, revenue sources, program needs with the planning and design process; operational issues such as reservations, space prioritization, equipment and facility maintenance issues, and revenue generation will also be discussed.

fields.title: Human Resources Management and Development in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course is an overview of human resource management and human resource development in sport, recreation and campus recreation programs. The course will provide an introduction to administrative practices, organizational development and management theory, and apply these concepts into the day to day practices and skills required of an administrator of a sport, recreation and/or campus recreation program.

fields.title: Group and Team Development: Theory, Research and Facilitation in Campus Recreation
fields.description: This course is an introduction to theory, research and the practical considerations of group and team development. Skill development in leading groups and teams, facilitation and processing.

fields.title: The American College Student
fields.description: An examination of developmental theory and review of the literature and research related to the American college student.

fields.title: Programming in Campus Recreation
fields.description: This course is an in-depth analysis of programming in a campus recreation center. Skill development in outcome-based program development and assessment; use of wellness models, health behavior theory, and student development theory in planning; and marketing and programming for diverse populations and skill levels.

fields.title: Advanced Event Planning and Management in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course is designed to provide graduate students with an in-depth understanding and experiences related to event planning and management. The course will build off of the content delivered in SRL 620 . Students will have the opportunity to plan and implement multiple events through the course of the semester. The researching, planning, coordinating, marketing, sponsorship, management and evaluation of special events will be the focus of this course.

fields.title: Legal Concepts in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course is a study of legal issues related to the administration of sport, recreation and campus recreation facilities, programs and services. An in-depth analysis of the legal foundations and responsibilities of sport and recreation agencies including tort and constitutional law, liability and risk management, contractual law, human resource management and the legislative and judicial processes.

fields.title: Reading and Research in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course involves directed reading in designated areas and specialized interests, investigating, researching and reporting. Course may not be repeated.

fields.title: Internship in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: This course involves practical experience in applying administrative theory to problems encountered in a professional setting in sport, recreation or campus recreation industries. Specific assignments will be determined by the needs of the student.

fields.title: Practicum in Sport and Recreation Leadership
fields.description: The practicum is a 1-credit course designed to allow students in the sport and recreation leadership program to gain practical experience in a chosen segment of the industry.

fields.title: Comprehensive Continuance
fields.description: This course involves continued preparation in anticipation of the comprehensive examination. Course may be repeated as needed.

fields.title: Thesis Continuance
fields.description: This course involves continued study, research and writing in the area of thesis concentration. Course may be repeated as needed.

fields.title: Thesis Research
fields.description: This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.
fields.prerequisites: SRL 525 or equivalent, and permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Foundations of Leadership in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: An introduction to the basis for the professions that make up Sport and Recreation Management. A focus on these professions in governmental, voluntary, private and commercial settings is incorporated. Finally both the economical significance and the professional preparation for success in the industry are introduced and practiced.
fields.prerequisites: SRM major or permission of the director.

fields.title: Special Event Management: Le Gourmet
fields.description: This course is designed to provide students with a practical hands-on application of event planning for non-profit fundraising. In this course students will actively plan and execute the Hart School's major annual fundraising event, Le Gourmet.

fields.title: Sport and Recreation Management Seminar
fields.description: This course is for students to learn the business skills required for success in the sport and recreation management industry. Students will evaluate and analyze multiple critical thinking approaches and conflict management and negotiation skills, as well as customer service models, entrepreneurial theories and practices, and concepts within the industries of sport and recreation.
fields.prerequisites: SRM majors only.

fields.title: Introduction to Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: Introduces the sport and recreation management professions in governmental, voluntary, private, public, and commercial settings. Outlines development of sport and recreation and the evolution of the mega-leisure industry. Overviews professional preparation in sport and recreation management.
fields.prerequisites: SRM majors only.

fields.title: Sociology and Psychology of Sport and Recreation
fields.description: The primary purpose of this course is to investigate sport and recreation related activities and services from a sociological and psychological perspective. The focus will be on activity through the lifespan and using theory and current issues from both disciplines to aid the practitioner in their interactions with participants and constituents and with the development and management of sport and recreation related activities and services.
fields.prerequisites: Declared SRM major or disabilities studies minor.

fields.title: Practicum in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: A sequence of selected practicum experiences which provides the student with supervised practicum experience in Sport and Recreation Management.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 241 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: A special studies course designed to explore areas of current topical concern in sport and recreation environments.
fields.prerequisites: SRM major and permission of the director.

fields.title: History of Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course covers the development of sports and recreational activities and their significance in American life from colonial times to the present. It is designed both to supplement students' understanding of American history and to examine the role that sports and recreational activities have played in shaping contemporary society.

fields.title: Management in Sport and Recreation
fields.description: This course will provide students with the knowledge to apply the management principles and theories to specific professional organizations in the sport and recreation industry. Sport and recreation management applications covered include administration principles for specific organizations, human resource management, fiscal management, marketing, and risk management.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 241 .

fields.title: Introduction to Sport Media
fields.description: Examination of the knowledge and skills required for the business of sports communications, including strategic and personal communications, leadership, publishing, advertising, public relation and crisis management. The course also examines sport communications from a sociological and legal perspective and the emergence of online sport communication and the new sport media.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 241 .

fields.title: Programming and Assessment in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: This course will examine the basics of sport and recreation programming and assessment. Students will be presented with tools and strategies for developing and assessing programs and evaluating their outcomes. Students will learn how to program for agencies of various sizes with an understanding of the importance of recognizing service population needs.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 241 .

fields.title: Ethical and Legal Issues in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: This course is designed to introduce students to current ethical and legal issues of concern to professionals in sport, recreation and leisure studies. Students will examine the impact of these issues on organizational and managerial policies and decision-making.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 333 .

fields.title: Sport Marketing and Sales
fields.description: This course will examine how promotional activities and sales efforts are closely intertwined and impact the success or failure of the sport and leisure industry. Particular emphasis will be placed on ticket sales and sport sponsorship.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 333 .

fields.title: Facilities and Event Management
fields.description: This course is designed to explore the principles of planning, design, and management of selected sport, recreation, and exercise facilities. The course will also cover the planning and management of special events. This will include budgeting, design, staffing, evaluation/assessment, crowd management and relative human resource management.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 333 .

fields.title: Human Resources in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: An overview of human resource management and development in sport and recreation environments. This course will provide an introduction to administrative practices involving employer and employee relationships and an application of these concepts to day to day management duties. Course focus will be policies, legal issues, recruiting, hiring, job analysis, creating position descriptions, evaluation, training, development and supervision of staff members and volunteers.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 333 .

fields.title: Internship in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: This full-time professional experience affords the opportunity to apply theory and methodology under qualified supervision from the cooperating agency and the university. While enrolled in this course, students may take up to one additional course without permission and a second course with permission. The second additional course must be approved in advance by the SRM internship coordinator. All internship sites must be approved by the SRM practicum and internship coordinator.
fields.prerequisites: SRM 282 , SRM 333 and 72 credit hours completed.

fields.title: Special Studies in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: Designed to give capable students in Sport and Recreation Management an opportunity to complete independent study under faculty supervision.
fields.prerequisites: SRM major and permission of the director.

fields.title: Special Topics in Sport and Recreation Management
fields.description: This course is designed to allow explorations of areas of current topical concern, or to exploit special situations. Course content will vary. For current course content consult your advisor or the SHSRM Director.
fields.prerequisites: SRM major and permission of the director.

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: See catalog description entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: See catalog description entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Honors
fields.description: See catalog description entitled "Graduation with Distinction" and "Graduation with Honors."

fields.title: Elementary Swahili I
fields.description: The fundamentals of Swahili through listening, speaking, reading and writing. Practice in pronunciation and development of comprehension. One hour's work a week in language laboratory. Students will receive no credit for the course if they have had two or more years of the language in high school.

fields.title: Elementary Swahili II
fields.description: This course builds on the foundations established in SWA 101 through listening, speaking, reading and writing activities. This course provides practice in pronunciation and development of comprehension. There is one hour a week of work in the language laboratory. If student has had two or more years of the language in high school they will not receive credit for the course.

fields.title: Intensive Swahili
fields.description: The fundamentals of Swahili through listening, speaking, reading and writing. The course is the equivalent of SWA 101 - SWA 102 .

fields.title: Intensive Swahili II
fields.description: The fundamentals of Swahili through listening, speaking, reading and writing. The course is the equivalent of SWA 231 - SWA 232 .
fields.prerequisites: SWA 102 or SWA 111 , or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Swahili I
fields.description: A thorough review of first year grammar and vocabulary building. Conversation, composition and readings will be chosen to reach competency at the lower intermediate level Swahili.
fields.prerequisites: SWA 102 or SWA 111 , or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Intermediate Swahili II
fields.description: A thorough review of Swahili grammar and vocabulary building. Conversation, composition and readings will be chosen to reach competency at the advance intermediate level.
fields.prerequisites: SWA 231 or permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Grammar and Communication
fields.description: Intensive training in grammatical structures and their application to oral and written communication. Instruction is in Swahili. Fulfills the College of Arts and Letters writing-intensive requirement for the major.
fields.prerequisites: SWA 232 or SWA 212 , or by permission of the instructor.

fields.title: Swahili Oral and Written Communication
fields.description: Intensive training in the use of modern, everyday Swahili with emphasis on conversation and composition. Readings in Swahili will provide a context for discussion and writing.
fields.prerequisites: SWA 300 .

fields.title: Special Studies in Swahili
fields.description: Special topics or independent studies in Swahili.

fields.title: Management and Problem Solving in Schools
fields.description: This course prepares school-related professionals in identifying school-level problems and synthesizing learning environments to formulate strategic plans for school improvement.

fields.title: Leadership and Communication Skills in Schools
fields.description: This course is designed to prepare school-related professionals with knowledge, skills and dispositions required to be effective teacher leaders, including understanding leadership within the classroom, school, community and profession.

fields.title: Collaborating, Teaming and Leading in Schools
fields.description: This course is designed to prepare school-related professionals to effectively engage in collaboration, facilitating teams and leading in formal and informal roles in schools.

fields.title: Leading Curriculum Revision and Implementation
fields.description: This course prepares school-related professionals to critically examine, revise and recommend curriculum and curricular policy.

fields.title: Introduction to Second Language Acquisition
fields.description: This course provides an overview of first and second language acquisition through the lens of education. Students are guided through an in-depth inquiry process designed to develop researcher-practitioners, an approach that is particularly critical to the promotion of educational justice.

fields.title: Pedagogical Grammar
fields.description: This course develops skills in teaching grammar and syntax in the context of writing. Special focus will be on working with English language learners and the ability to model and teach editing skills and organization of writing using predominant text structures in the content areas.

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL Instruction
fields.description: The course provides supervised field experiences in working with multilingual learners at both elementary and secondary school settings. Preservice teachers will demonstrate competencies related to integrating language and content instruction, and differentiating according to multilingual learners' needs and language proficiency levels.
fields.prerequisites: TESL 300 .

fields.title: Practicum in Second Language Acquisition
fields.description: This one credit practicum provides an opportunity for students to work directly with multilingual learners under the guidance of a university supervisor to identify, recognize and apply principles of English as a new language in educational contexts. Content of the practicum will directly align with topics covered in TESL 300 .

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL Literacy Development
fields.description: This one credit practicum provides an opportunity for students to work directly with English language learners to plan and implement oral language, reading, and writing strategies in language arts and content instruction that are directly related to topics covered in the LED 435 course.
fields.prerequisites: LED 366 .

fields.title: Practicum in Literacy Development
fields.description: This one credit practicum provides for pre-service teachers to work directly with students in grades PK-12 (as determined by the LED 366 instructor) on literacy development under the supervision of a mentor teacher and a University Supervisor. They plan and implement literacy strategies in language arts and content instruction directly related to LED 366 course material. Most pre-service teachers will assist Prek-5 students.

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL
fields.description: This practicum provides an opportunity for students to apply instructional methods and practices for teaching English to speakers of other languages (TESOL) to meet the linguistic needs of multilingual learners under the supervision of a university supervisor. Content and site locations will vary depending upon the specific focus of the practicum.

fields.title: Foundations of ESL PK-12 Collaboration
fields.description: This course is a detailed study of ESL co-teaching and other collaborative practices. The course explores the rationale for teacher collaboration to support ESL instruction; presents current, classroom-based, practitioner-oriented research studies related to co-teaching, co-planning, curriculum alignment, teacher professional development and additional collaborative practices; and offers authentic teacher reflections and recommendations on collaboration and co-teaching.
fields.prerequisites: TESOL majors only.

fields.title: Cross-Cultural Education
fields.description: The course provides students with knowledge of the effects of socio-cultural variables in an instructional setting.

fields.title: Language Assessment for Multilingual Learners
fields.description: This course introduces students to a variety of formative and summative assessment practices for multilingual learners. Students will become familiar with equitable assessment practices that aim to minimize cultural and linguistic biases and promote asset-based approaches.
fields.prerequisites: TESL 300 .

fields.title: Methods in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
fields.description: This course introduces students to instructional methods and practices for teaching English to speakers of other languages (TESOL) to meet the linguistic needs of multilingual learners. Students will develop competences in selecting culturally responsive materials, integrating language and content instruction, and differentiating according to multilingual learners' language proficiency levels.
fields.prerequisites: TESL 300 .
fields.corequisites: TESOL minor: TESL 385 ; TESOL major: TESL 381 .

fields.title: Student Teaching/Internship
fields.description: Enables students to apply skills and attitudes acquired in all components of their professional education preparation. Students design and implement instructional activities under the guidance of teaching professionals.
fields.prerequisites: PSYC 160 , EDUC 310 , EDUC 200 , pre-professional studies and TESOL core courses.

fields.title: Student Teaching Seminar in TESOL
fields.description: This seminar is designed to accompany the student teaching experiences. Its purpose is to provide opportunities for student teachers to process and reflect on their experiences that occur in the classroom and school and to strengthen their professional growth. Broad topic areas include understanding of different instructional practices and implementation of a variety of lesson plans with appropriate behavior management and assessment strategies to meet the needs of English learners. Emphasis is placed on guiding student teachers from theory to the world of the professional educator by exploring their own skill levels and plans for their ongoing professional development.
fields.prerequisites: TESOL majors only.

fields.title: Professional Development, Partnership and Advocacy Seminar
fields.description: Students examine opportunities for professional development from professional associations, universities and other organizations across PK-16. Strategies to build partnerships with colleagues, families and communities are presented. Important social and political issues affecting education of majority and minority students and models of advocacy for students and their families are presented.
fields.prerequisites: TESL 300 .

fields.title: Special Studies in TESOL
fields.description: The course is designed to allow the student to complete an independent study in a TESOL-related area under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Foundations of Language and Culture
fields.description: This course provides students with an understanding of the interrelationship between language and culture to enable them to gain skills to create appropriate learning environments for multilingual learners. Course content includes concepts and issues pertaining to applied linguistics and theories/models of cultural competence and multicultural education.

fields.title: Pedagogical Grammar
fields.description: This course develops skills in teaching grammar and syntax in the context of writing. Special focus will be on working with English language learners and the ability to model and teach editing skills and organization of writing using predominant text structures in the content areas.

fields.title: Cross-Cultural Education
fields.description: The course provides students with knowledge of the effects of socio-cultural variables in an instructional setting.

fields.title: Assessment and Curriculum Development in English as a Second Language
fields.description: The course provides students with a variety of assessment practices for profiling non-native students' abilities and for developing appropriate curriculum.

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL Instructional Strategies
fields.description: This experience provides practice in the integrated teaching of content and language related to the concurrent TESL 680 course. Pre-service teachers will gain experience observing and instructing English language learners in elementary and middle/secondary classrooms dividing their 90-hour practicum between both groups. The seminar sessions provide opportunities to explore issues related to the practices, methods, and issues of teaching English Language learners.

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL 1st/2nd Language Acquisition
fields.description: This one credit practicum provides an opportunity for students to work directly with English language learners under the supervision of a mentor teacher and a university supervisor to identify and recognize principles of first and second language acquisition as evident in classroom contexts. Content of the practicum will directly correlate with topics covered in TESL 626 .

fields.title: Practicum in TESOL Literacy Development
fields.description: This one credit practicum provides an opportunity for students to work directly with English language learners under the supervision of a mentor teacher and a university supervisor to plan and implement oral language, reading, and writing strategies in language arts and content instruction that are directly related to topics covered in the LED 635 course.

fields.title: Practicum in Literacy Development
fields.description: This practicum has pre-service teachers work directly with students in grades PreK-12 (as determined by the LED 566 instructor) on literacy development under the supervision of a mentor teacher and a university supervisor to plan and implement literacy strategies in language arts and content instruction that are directly related to topics covered in the LED 566 course. Most pre-service teachers will assist Prek-5 students.

fields.title: Methods in Teaching English to Speakers of Other Languages
fields.description: This course introduces students to instructional methods and practices for teaching English to speakers of other languages (TESOL) to meet the linguistic needs of multilingual learners. Students will develop competences in selecting culturally responsive materials, integrating language and content instruction, and differentiating according to multilingual learners' language proficiency levels.

fields.title: Integrated Language and Content Instruction for Multilingual Learners
fields.description: This course examines the Sheltered Instruction Observation Protocol (SIOP) Model as a framework for planning and delivering effective instruction for multilingual learners. Students analyze the theoretical foundations and research supporting the model and explore its components across diverse educational settings. Emphasis is placed on fostering academic English development, promoting culturally and linguistically responsive pedagogy, advocating for multilingual learners, and demonstrating instructional leadership in multilingual contexts.

fields.title: Concepts of First and Second Language Acquisition
fields.description: This course examines major theories and research on how first and additional languages are acquired. Students examine cognitive, social and cultural factors that shape language learning and bilingual development. Emphasis is placed on bridging research and practice through the design of inclusive, linguistically responsive instructional strategies that effectively support multilingual learners.

fields.title: Principles and Practices of Language Assessment for Multilingual Learners
fields.description: This course introduces students to a variety of formative and summative assessment practices for multilingual learners. Students will become familiar with evidence-based assessment practices that aim to minimize cultural and linguistic biases and promote asset-based approaches.

fields.title: Development, Assessment and Instruction of Literacy, K-12
fields.description: This course is designed to provide preservice teachers with a foundation of literacy development. Instructional strategies and assessment techniques, which support the acquisition and development of literacy in diverse classrooms across the curriculum in grades K-12.
fields.prerequisites: CSD 300 and junior standing; or departmental permission.

fields.title: Immigration and Education
fields.description: This course examines the multitude of factors that shape the immigrant student experience in U.S. schools. It takes an interdisciplinary perspective, which draws on research from sociology, anthropology, history, economics, political science and education to understand teaching and learning from the perspective of immigrant students and families.

fields.title: Instructional Strategies for TESOL
fields.description: This course is designed to provide pre-service ESL teachers with experiences in designing and implementing instructional strategies to meet the linguistic needs of English Language Learners and utilizing assessment instruments to evaluate student progress.

fields.title: Student Teaching/Internship
fields.description: Enables students to apply skills and attitudes acquired in all components of their professional education preparation. Students design and implement instructional activities under the guidance of teaching professionals.
fields.prerequisites: ECED 512 , EDUC 540 and TESOL courses.

fields.title: Professional Development, Partnership and Advocacy
fields.description: Introduction of professional development offered by associations, professional organizations and higher education. Strategies for building partnerships with colleagues, families and communities are practiced. Advocacy for students' linguistic, academic, and personal development is addressed. Students discuss public issues affecting the education of majority and minority students and develop the skills to support students and their families socially and politically.

fields.title: Research and Reading in TESOL
fields.description: Designed for students who have completed TESL 695 . Applied Research or others who desire to complete a research project pertaining to TESOL or a with a diversity-related focus. In this course, students conduct their research, write up their findings and present their conclusions in a written product.

fields.title: Special Topics in TESOL
fields.description: The course is designed to allow the student to complete an independent study in a TESOL-related area under faculty supervision.

fields.title: Applied Research
fields.description: This course provides an overview of action research and qualitative research for educational settings. Students will identify a key research focus and develop an appropriate research project that is grounded in the principles of the course.

fields.title: Thesis
fields.description: Designed for students who have completed TESL 695 . Applied Research. In this course, students conduct their master's degree research, analyze their findings and present their conclusions in a written product. This course is graded on a satisfactory/unsatisfactory (S/U) basis.
fields.prerequisites: TESL 695 .

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Scenery [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in scenery provides 35 hours of direct, hands-on experience working on a faculty or guest production in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Students will work in the scene shop and build skills in power tool usage, theatrical painting techniques and sourcing materials. Upon completion, students will be able to participate in the functions of a professional-level scenic and/or properties shop.

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Lights [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in lighting provides 35 hours of direct, hands-on experience working on a faculty or guest production in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Students will work in the electrics shop and build skills in hanging and focusing lights, striking, cabling, and maintenance. Upon completion, students will be able to participate in the functions of a professional-level electrics shop.

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Costumes [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in costumes provides 35 hours of direct, hands-on experience working on a faculty or guest production in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Students will work in the costume shop and build skills in alterations, costume crafts, costume stock and show organization. Upon completion, students will be able to participate in the functions of a professional-level costume shop.

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Management [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in management provides 35 hours of direct, hands-on experience working on event management and arts administration in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Students will work with faculty advisors and build skills in stage management, company management, house management and administration. Upon completion, students will be able to participate in the office and management functions of a professional arts organization.

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Performance [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in performance provides students direct, hands-on experience working as an actor or performer in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Eligibility requires having been cast in a faculty or guest directed production. Upon completion, students will understand the expectations and standards required of professional actors and performers.

fields.title: Introduction to Theatre [C2VPA]
fields.description: Study of the theatre as an art form. Emphasis on introducing students to a broad spectrum of theatrical activity and opinion. Consideration of the components that comprise a theatre event including acting, directing, design, costuming, lighting and playwriting. May be used for general education credit. May not be used for major credit.

fields.title: Performance Analysis
fields.description: Plays are examined as texts for performance. Theories of performance and methods for the analysis of performances in and out of the theater are studied.
fields.prerequisites: Theatre and musical theatre majors and theatre minors, American studies minors and creative writing minors only.

fields.title: Theatre Practicum: Sound [Block]
fields.description: This practicum in sound provides 35 hours of direct, hands-on experience working on a faculty or guest production in the School of Theatre and Dance in a block-schedule format. Students will work in the sound shop and learn proper techniques for setting up, testing and operating equipment for live sound and recording. Upon completion, students will be able to participate in the functions of a professional-level sound shop.

fields.title: Acting I: Basic Acting
fields.description: A study of basic acting as a performance experience. Emphasis on fundamentals of performance including concentration, transitions, interaction and the structuring of action.

fields.title: Musical Theatre Laboratory
fields.description: Introduction to issues related to Musical Theatre through music and text analysis, vocal technique, and practice of the repertoire. Topics relating to vocal and physical health, professional practice, and musical theatre resources will also be covered. May be repeated once for credit.
fields.prerequisites: Musical theatre majors only.

fields.title: Voice for the Stage
fields.description: Theories and exercises designed to equip the student with proper speech for the stage through a fundamental understanding of phonetics and articulation.
fields.prerequisites: THEA 251 .

fields.title: Technical Theatre
fields.description: Study of the technical aspects of stage production. Emphasis upon practical experience in the use of stage and shop facilities. Consideration of the physical theater and stage, construction, painting and rigging of scenery as applied to theatrical production.
fields.prerequisites: STAD 171 .

fields.title: Movement for the Actor
fields.description: Students in this course develop and refine movement skills for stage performance. Through a study of approaches, such as Viewpoints, Animal Work, and Laban Techniques, students develop methods of artistic expression using their body. Through movement, students discover new connections to speech and text and improve the condition, flexibility, and responsiveness of their physical instrument. Students also develop the means for making effective physical choices in the creation of a performance.
fields.prerequisites: THEA 251 .

fields.title: Studio Production
fields.description: This course is reserved for students working on student productions through the experimental theatre program in the studio theatre, which may include positions such as cast, crew, dramaturgs, stage managers, designers and assistant designers.

fields.title: Studio Production for Performance Concentrators
